"Creating a channel or a port in a job at its object limit shall be refused, and no object shall be counted beyond the limit."
"Object creation in a job limited to 5 objects is refused at the limit, 0 objects beyond it (the `quota` line)."
"Every charge against a job shall be returned when the resource it paid for is freed, and a job's quota slot shall be given back when the job goes."
"After the quota checks every counter of their jobs is back to zero, and as many quota slots are in use as before them (the `quota` line)."
"A limit set on a job shall bound it together with every job beneath it, and a charge refused at any level shall leave no level charged."
"A charge that would pass a grandparent's limit is refused although the child's own limit allows it, and each level's counter reads as before the attempt."

"A user page fault refused by a job's memory limit shall end a process in the job whose limit was full or beneath it, never one outside it, count the kill in that job and every job above it, and retry the fault."

"A program writing 8 MiB in a job limited to 1 MiB ends by SIGKILL while a larger process in a sibling job lives; exactly 1 process is killed; memory.events counts one OOM kill in the job and its parent and none in the sibling."
"The kernel heap the Linux personality keeps for a job's programs shall be charged against the job's memory limit, and every byte of it returned when it is freed; a sibling job shall be unaffected."

"At a 32 KiB limit each kind of personality object is refused one past its count with ENOMEM (ENOLCK for a lock) while a sibling makes one, and with them gone every byte charged has come back (the `kmem` line)."

"A creation the task limit refuses shall be answered as Linux and the native ABI answer it -- a fork with EAGAIN, a native process_create with SHOULD_WAIT -- and the refused process shall never start."
"A fork past pids.max is answered EAGAIN and counted in pids.events; process_create into a job at its task limit is answered SHOULD_WAIT and the job's task count is unchanged."
"Creating a VMO, a job or a pin in a job at its object limit shall be refused with NO_MEMORY, and each shall be counted as an object for as long as it exists."
"In a job limited to 5 objects and holding 5, vmo_create, job_create and vmo_pin are each refused NO_MEMORY, 0 objects counted beyond the limit, and the job holds 0 once they are all closed."

children.name: Audit
children.doc: The audit record of the TSF's own decisions: O.AUDIT (FAU_GEN.1, FAU_GEN.2, FAU_SAR.1, FAU_SAR.2, FAU_STG.1, FAU_STG.4), for P.ACCOUNTABILITY. docs/certification/AUDIT.md is the design.

children.value: "Each audit ring shall number its records from zero without a gap, the high-value ring's first being the start-up record with the boot's whole audit id and both ring lengths; a second start shall change nothing, and a reader asking for a record the ring overwrote shall be moved on and told exactly how many it lost."

"On a store of four high-value records, the start-up record is number 0 and carries the id and lengths; a second start is refused; after six grants a read from 0 copies records 3 to 6 and reports 3 lost; a read of two from 3 resumes at 5."
"The first eight system records shall stay readable, numbered as the high-value ring numbered them, however far that ring has wrapped, and no record after them shall join them."
"Nine system records and a grant in a ring of four: the boot records read back 0, 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 8, the ring reports records lost, and a read of the boot records from 6 copies 3 and resumes at 9."
"A refusal shall be kept in the refusal ring and a record of every other class in the high-value ring, so that no flood of refusals can overwrite a grant."
"One record of each of the six classes: the refusal alone in the refusal ring, the other five in the high-value ring in the order made."
"A job shall be charged, for the fairness of the refusal ring, to the budget its maker gave it: its parent's for a job its members could make themselves, its own otherwise."
"An anonymous job and one inside it are charged to their unit, a cgroup made in a delegated unit to that unit, and a cgroup root made in a unit to itself: 6 jobs' budgets as given."

"Past 64 refusals charged to one budget in a second, the TSF shall count that budget's further refusals rather than keep them, and write the count once the second has ended, while another budget's refusals and every grant are kept."

"104 refusals from a unit's three jobs keep 64 between them and, once the second has ended, one suppressed record counting 40 under the unit; the delegated unit's refusal in the same second is kept, and a grant made before is still read with none lost."
"A budget whose fairness window is taken to make room for another shall have its count written, not dropped."
"A budget one over its limit, then 32 more budgets: the first's window is closed and its suppressed record counts 1."

"The boot shall start its audit record with the start-up record of the id reads answer, and record whether its self-checks run, who starts devmgr, the mitigations it was built with and the KASLR state, as bring-up read them."

"The kernel's boot records begin with the start-up record, its id the one reads answer and its lengths 512 and 4096, and hold the 4 configuration records with bring-up's values; the boot is not yet recorded as brought up."

"Each decision the TSF makes at a recording site -- a call its rights refused, a widening refused, a limit's refusal, a process made, a job given for a cgroup, a control channel given, a job killed, a cgroup killed, an OOM kill, a device quiesced, a limit set by handle or by cgroup file, a DMA fault -- shall be recorded with its outcome and the subject that made it, the kernel for the decisions it makes alone."

"At the end of a boot with checks, the record holds each of the 12 events the boot's checks provoke, and DMA_FAULT where an IOMMU translates, with the outcome of its class and its subject; none of the OOM kill, the quiesce and the fault names a process; the boot is recorded as brought up."

"The audit record shall be read only through the audit handle with READ, which can be neither duplicated nor sent; a read shall copy whole records from a cursor, and a read that copies none or cannot copy them out shall leave the cursor, the buffer and the reader's position where they were."

"A handle with pid 1's rights reads the boot records, the start-up record first with the kernel's id; a count of 0 copies nothing and moves nothing; a read into unmapped memory is FAULT and counts nothing read; a handle without READ, a channel end and a ring that does not exist are refused; the handle is not duplicated and not sent."

"A boot with init shall keep its audit record on the root volume in a file named by the boot's audit id, holding the start-up record, the configuration, and the decisions only a boot with init makes."

"svc audit reads back the start-up record with the id init named the file by, the checks' configuration as run, STARTER_GIVEN, READER_GIVEN, DEVMGR_STARTED by pid 1 and ROOT_SWITCHED with pid 1 moved."

"Every record up to a power action shall be in the reader's file or on the console: the kernel shall record the power action last, say how far the reader read, and print every record past that, and a run the ring overwrote as one line."
"At test-init's power-off, init's last read is where the kernel saw it stop, and every number from there to the power action is printed as unread or in a lost run."
"A boot that skips its self-checks shall record that it did, where a reader outside it can see."
"A boot with ferrix.checks=skip, read back through svc audit, holds the checks' configuration record with value 0."
"An audit record shall be 64 bytes, each field little-endian at a fixed offset, so that a reader decodes what the kernel wrote."
"A record of distinct bytes encodes to them in order at the offsets the layout names and decodes back equal."

children.name: Failure
children.doc: The safe state and what brings the kernel to it: O.FAILSAFE and ASR-6 (FPT_FLS.1). SAFETY-MANUAL.md §3 defines the safe state.

children.value: "On a failed internal consistency check the kernel shall stop every other processor, print a diagnostic naming the failure and its catalogued explanation, and halt without returning to user mode."
"A boot told to panic at its end (`ferrix.onexit=panic`) ends with the FX-1501 report and no program output after it; every panic site in the item has a catalogue entry (`check-panic-audit.py`)."
"The allocator every kernel stack comes from shall give each an unmapped guard page directly below and above it."
"A kernel stack allocated, written at its first and last word and freed has the page below and the page above it untranslated, and gives back every frame it took."
"A kernel stack overflow shall end in the halt and diagnostic of the safe state, never in a write below the stack."
"A kernel thread that recurses past its stack ends the boot in a report naming the fault -- on x86-64 a double fault taken on its own stack (FX-9004) -- on each architecture, 3 of 3."
"Once a failure report has begun, a line the kernel writes shall reach the console port after a bounded wait even when the port's lock is held and will never be released."
"A report begun while another context holds the port's lock for good reaches the port whole, after at most 10,000,000 attempts at the lock, on each architecture, 3 of 3."

children.name: Storage
children.doc: The btrfs reader and write path, `ferrix-btrfs` and `ferrix-btrfs-write`, in the item since 2026-10-02: O.MEDIA and ASR-9 (FPT_TDC.1, FDP_SDI.2). Their interface below is the `Device` and `WriteDevice` traits the kernel's block layer answers, above it `Volume` and `WriteVolume`; the VFS glue on top (`ferrix-btrfs-vfs`, src/kernel/src/fs/btrfs*.rs) is load, so these promise what the two crates do at `Volume` and `WriteVolume`, not what a program sees through a mount. The low-level requirements are part 24. Some sit under a requirement here by decomposition rather than as a case of its criterion: L.btrfs.31 and .70 (a node's address and generation) refine H.STORE.2, whose criterion tests a data sector, and L.btrfs.16 and .92 (superblock stripes) refine H.STORE.5, whose criterion tests the trees' consistency.

children.value: "The btrfs reader and writer shall answer every volume image, whatever its bytes, with a value or an error, without reading or writing outside a buffer, panicking or looping without bound."

"Each of 4,096 single-byte patches of a superblock, and of a leaf, parses or is refused, and every accessor of what parses answers, 0 panics. The decoders' own totality, and the `btrfs_read` fuzzer's resealed images, are their low-level requirements' and outside this criterion; the write path, which parses every node through the reader, has no hostile-image check of its own yet (TODO.md)."
"A block whose checksum disagrees with its contents shall never be returned as valid: the reader shall read another copy where the chunk keeps one, and otherwise answer an error."
"With the first copy of a DUP data sector damaged, a file read returns the file's bytes from the second; with both damaged, it answers DataChecksum and hands back none of the sector's bytes."
"Until a commit's superblock is written, the volume on the device shall be exactly the last commit, whatever of the commit's other writes have reached it."
"500 inserts committed, and the commit's writes replayed without its superblocks onto the volume as it was, leave a volume that checks clean and holds exactly the last commit's items."
"What a commit or a log commit returned success for shall be found, no older, when the volume is opened after a power cut at any later point, the log replayed if the superblock names one."

"Of 100 cuts over 4 random scenarios of writes, logs and commits, each rebuilt as the device may have left the disk, every one opens, checks clean down to free space and checksums, and rolls back no completed promise."
"Each commit shall leave the extent tree, the block groups' usage, the free-space tree and the superblock's totals agreeing with the trees, so that no block in use is free."

"After 3,000 random edits on the blank fixture, committed as they go, the writer's checker finds every tree block's and data extent's references, each block group's usage and free space and the superblock's total consistent."
"An operation the volume has no room for shall be refused with no space before it changes anything, leaving the transaction able to commit."
"On a 128 MiB volume, creates until its trees are full end in NoSpace with the transaction not aborted, its commit succeeds, and a deletion still makes room for another create."
"An allocation the btrfs writer cannot make shall be answered to its caller as an error, aborting the transaction if an edit had begun, and never as a panic or a stop of the element."

"With every allocation of the writer's operations failed in turn, each operation succeeds or answers an error, no panic is taken, and the volume reopened from the device is the last commit and checks clean."
"An operation that fails after it changed something shall abort its transaction, so that none of it is committed, and the volume reloaded at its last commit shall take no further change."

"Through a mount, a commit whose device write fails answers EIO; the mount then reads the last commit, has no trace of the aborted transaction, answers EROFS to a write, a truncation and a create, and the disk holds the last commit."

children.name: ObjectKinds
children.doc: src/kernel/src/object/mod.rs: what a handle names, its signals, and how objects are dropped without recursing.

children.value: "Object::signals shall report a handle to a process TERMINATED once the process has ended and closed its handles."
"A handle to a process that has ended and closed its handles reports TERMINATED when waited on."
"Object::signals shall report a port READABLE while it holds a packet, and no signal for a VMO, a device, an I/O mapping, a pin or the starter token."
"A wait for READABLE on a port holding a packet returns at once and on an empty port times out; a wait on each of a VMO, a device, an I/O mapping and a pin times out with 0 signals observed."
"Object::waiters shall name a channel end's own queue, which a message written to the end wakes, so that a wait on the end ends at the message and not at its deadline."
"A wait on a channel end with a two-minute deadline returns after a message written 20 ms later and before the deadline."
"dispose shall drop every object it is given and every object those hold, a channel end's unread messages and the handles they carry included, so that nothing an object held outlives it."
"Closing both ends of a channel whose queue holds a VMO with a committed page gives that page back: the native checks' free-frame count is the same before and after, 0 frames kept."
"dispose shall hold at most one queued object's drop on the stack at a time, however deeply objects are nested in one another's queues."
"A chain of N channel ends, each queued unread in the next's inbox, is freed from its outermost end with N in the thousands and no guard-page fault, every frame given back."

"dispose shall close a channel end whose last reference it holds before it returns, even while another context is draining disposed objects, so that the peer sees PEER_CLOSED from the moment the close returns (FX-1004)."
"A close made while another context is marked as draining is followed at once by a write and a read on the peer, each refused PEER_CLOSED, 2 of 2."

"defer shall queue an object for the drainer and, when the queue cannot grow, drop it where it is while fewer than four such drops are under way, so that no object is given up while a drop in place is still allowed."
"Across the allocation-failure rounds, every nth fallible allocation failing for several n, 0 objects are given up (abandoned() reads 0) and every frame comes back."

"defer shall give an object up, and count it, only when the queue cannot grow and four drops in place are already under way, and shall neither recurse further nor stop the kernel: the one exception to H.OBJ.8, an object that outlives its last handle, bounded by the depth and counted by abandoned()."
"With the orphan queue refused its growth and four in-place drops nested, a fifth deferred object is counted as given up (abandoned() rises by 1) and the kernel runs on."
"defer shall drop an object where it is, and give nothing up, when the orphan queue cannot grow and fewer than four drops in place are under way."
"A close of a job handle with the orphan queue's one growth refused answers success, the job is gone when it returns, and abandoned() stays 0."

children.name: Channels
children.doc: src/kernel/src/object/channel.rs.

children.value: "Endpoint::pair shall make two connected ends charged together as two objects to the running task's job, and shall make neither when the job's object limit refuses the charge."
"In a job limited to 5 objects and holding 5, a pair is refused; holding 3, a pair is made and the job holds 5; with everything dropped it holds 0."
"A message written on one end of a channel shall be read, its bytes and the objects its handles name with the rights they carried, only on the other end, in the order written."
"Bytes and a VMO handle written by one process are read by the other as the same bytes and a handle through which the same VMO's contents are read."

"Endpoint::write shall answer a refusal of its take -- a handle the sender does not hold, or one named twice -- as the write's refusal, queueing nothing, so that every handle the write named stays with the sender."
"A send naming a good handle and one that does not exist is refused BAD_HANDLE and the good handle still works in the sender; a send of a channel end through itself is refused INVALID_ARGS."

"Endpoint::write shall take the sender's handles out of its table only after the peer's queue has agreed to take the message, so that a write refused because the peer closed, the message is too big or the queue is full moves no handle."

"A write carrying a handle refused PEER_CLOSED, one refused TOO_BIG for its bytes and one refused SHOULD_WAIT for a full queue each leave the handle in the sender under the same value, usable: 0 handles taken by a refused write."

"A channel end shall hold a bounded number of unread messages (channel::LIMITS, 256); a write to a full one shall be refused as full, and the writer shall not be told there is room until a read makes it."

"Writing to a reader that does not read is refused SHOULD_WAIT before 4097 messages are queued; the writer of the full channel is told neither that its peer has room nor WRITABLE; after draining it is told there is room, and its next write arrives. (That the bound is 256 exactly is the host tests' of the message queue, with the limit as a parameter.)"
"Endpoint::read shall leave a message queued, and report its size in bytes and handles, when the caller has room for fewer of either."
"A read with too little room for the bytes, then for the handle, is refused with the message's sizes both times, and a read with room then returns the message whole."
"Endpoint::unread shall put a message the caller took and could not deliver back at the head of the queue and wake the end's waiters, so that the next read returns it."
"A message carrying an endpoint, read into a buffer that faults, is read whole by the next read with a good buffer, and the endpoint delivered is the one sent."

"Endpoint::read shall refuse, leaving it queued, a message that carries a channel end unless the caller holds the topology lock, so that no end is put back into a queue while a send's cycle walk runs."
"A message carrying an endpoint, read into buffers a fork still shares copy-on-write, is delivered whole after the delivery put it back and read again, and the fork keeps what it had."
"Once its peer has closed, an end with nothing queued shall answer a read PEER_CLOSED, and a write to the peer shall be refused PEER_CLOSED."
"After the peer closes, while another context is marked as draining, a read and a write on the survivor are refused PEER_CLOSED, 2 of 2."
"With nothing queued and its peer open, Endpoint::read shall report the queue empty, which the call answers SHOULD_WAIT."
"A read of an emptied channel end whose peer is open is refused SHOULD_WAIT."
"Endpoint::read shall return every message the peer wrote before it closed before it answers PEER_CLOSED."

"A peer that writes 3 messages and closes leaves 3 to be read, in order, and only the fourth read answers PEER_CLOSED. A write and close between a read's look at the queue and its answer is argued in F-54 (the peer's close is looked at, with Acquire, before the queue), not shown by this check."
"Closing a channel end shall mark it closed under its queue's lock and free every message queued for it unread, with the objects they carry."
"A VMO queued unread in the closed end is freed: the native checks' free- frame count, taken around the check, is unchanged."
"Closing a channel end shall fire the peer's registrations waiting for PEER_CLOSED."
"A registration for PEER_CLOSED on one end fires when the other end is closed, its packet carrying its key and PEER_CLOSED."
"Endpoint::signals shall report READABLE while a message is queued for the end and PEER_CLOSED once its peer has closed."
"A wait woken by a message reports the end READABLE, and a wait for PEER_CLOSED on an end whose peer has closed returns at once."

"Endpoint::observe shall fire a registration for READABLE or PEER_CLOSED at once when either already holds, and otherwise list it under the queue lock that the change it waits for is made under, so it is neither missed nor fired early."
"A registration on a readable end fires at once with its key; one on a quiet end fires on the next message, and one for PEER_CLOSED when the peer closes."
"check_carry shall find that a send carrying channel ends closes a cycle when the inbox it lands in is reachable from what it carries, following the ends queued in each inbox."
"Queueing one channel's end in another and then the second's in the first is refused, the refused send keeps its handle, and 0 frames of a VMO riding in the queue are kept."
"A send carrying an end whose inbox holds another end twice, by two handles to it, shall not be refused as a cycle or as a walk too long."
"With one end carried twice in an inbox, a send carrying that inbox's own end is taken."
"A cycle walk shall visit at most 1024 queued ends, and a send whose walk would visit more shall be refused as too big, keeping what it would have carried with the sender."
"A send whose walk meets more queued ends than the bound is refused TOO_BIG and every handle it named is still the sender's."

children.name: Ports
children.doc: src/kernel/src/object/port.rs.

children.value: "Port::new shall make an empty port charged as one object to the running task's job, and none when the job's object limit refuses the charge."
"In a job limited to 5 objects, exactly 5 ports are made and the sixth refused; with them gone the job holds 0."
"Port::queue_user shall refuse a program's packet as full when 1024 of its packets are queued, whatever room signal packets have been promised."
"Filling a port nobody takes from is refused SHOULD_WAIT at exactly 1024 packets, and not before."
"Port::take shall return a user packet exactly as it was queued, and give back its share of the bound it was counted in."
"A queued user packet is taken with its key, its kind and both data words as queued."

"A registration and an interrupt binding shall reserve room for their packet on the port when they are made, and be refused for memory then if it cannot be reserved, so that queueing a signal or interrupt packet never allocates and never finds the port without room."
"Across rounds of native calls with every nth allocation failing, every port reports 0 packets lost for want of room."
"Port::put_back shall queue a packet the caller took and could not deliver ahead of every other, with its share of the bound, so that the next take returns it."
"A packet taken for a buffer that faults -- a user packet, a signal packet fired on a change and one fired as it was registered -- is returned by the next wait with a good buffer."
"A registration shall not fire before a signal it asked for is asserted, and shall fire once when one is, reporting it with its key, and not again."
"A registration does not fire before its signal, fires once on the message that asserts it with its key and READABLE, and a second write fires nothing."
"trigger shall fire only the registrations whose signals the change asserts, leaving every other listed."
"A message fires the registration waiting for READABLE and not the one waiting for PEER_CLOSED listed ahead of it."
"register shall refuse a registration as full when the object already holds 64, counted after dropping those whose port has gone."
"The 65th registration on one object is refused SHOULD_WAIT; after its ports are closed the object takes 64 again."

children.name: Interrupts
children.doc: src/kernel/src/object/interrupt.rs.

children.value: "Interrupt::new shall claim a line for at most one Interrupt at a time, and a line whose claim failed for memory shall be left free for the next claim."

"A second claim of a held line is refused ALREADY_BOUND; interrupt_create run once per allocation it makes, that one failing, claims the line or answers NO_MEMORY each time, and the next run claims it."

"Dropping the Interrupt that claimed a line shall free the line before the close returns, even while another context drains disposed objects, and a delivery in flight for the old holder shall not reach a new one."

"With a delivery taken and not yet fired, the holder's close lets the line be claimed again at once and the delivery then leaves the new holder quiet; a close made while another context drains lets it be claimed a third time."
"A delivery shall mark the line pending, and Object::signals report the interrupt READABLE, until Interrupt::acknowledge clears it."
"Before a delivery a wait on the interrupt times out; after one it sees READABLE; after interrupt_ack it times out again."
"Line::fire shall wake the tasks waiting on the interrupt and on the port it is bound to, after letting go of the interrupt-safe locks it took."
"In at least 5 of 8 rounds each way, a wait on the interrupt and a wait on its port are ended by the delivery's wake, not by the recheck timer."

"A bound interrupt shall queue one packet on its port, carrying its key, the interrupt kind and when it fired, each time it goes from quiet to pending, and Interrupt::bind shall refuse a second binding while the first port is held."
"A second bind is refused; two deliveries before the acknowledgement queue 1 packet with its key, kind and time, and a delivery after it queues another."
"Interrupt::bind shall queue a packet at once for an interrupt that is already pending."
"An interrupt that fired while its port was gone queues its packet, with its new key and the interrupt kind, on a new port as it is bound."

children.name: maskedFromDeliveryToAcknowledgement
children.doc: Rationale: an edge MSI-X vector's extra deliveries fold into the packet its holder has not answered, so masking it per delivery only cost two exits to the hypervisor per interrupt. The bound keeps interrupt time bounded: at most STORM_BOUND (64) handler runs per scheduling of the holder, where it was 1, each charged to the task the interrupt cut, so a storm costs other partitions up to that bound, accounted in their share (docs/certification/MEMORY-AND-TIMING.md §2.2; AoU-4, ASR-8).

children.value: "A delivery shall mask a line the controller holds before it marks it pending, and acknowledge shall unmask it; a delivery shall leave an edge-triggered MSI-X vector unmasked unless more than STORM_BOUND (64) deliveries have reached it since the last acknowledgement, when it shall mask the vector's entry until the next acknowledgement; acknowledge shall clear pending before it unmasks, so a delivery after it queues a packet of its own; and a refused claim shall leave the holder's line unmasked."

"On an edge-triggered MSI-X vector: read at its entry the claimed line is unmasked and stays unmasked after a delivery; a delivery after the acknowledgement and before the drain queues a packet; after 64 unacknowledged deliveries the entry is still unmasked, after the 65th it is masked with the line's storm count one higher and one packet queued, and after the acknowledgement it is unmasked (the `irq` line)."
"take_delivery shall mask at the controller a line no Interrupt holds and deliver nothing for it."
"A delivery on a line whose holder has let go wakes nobody, queues no packet, and leaves the line masked."

children.name: IoMappings
children.doc: src/kernel/src/object/io_mapping.rs.

children.value: "IoMapping::new shall refuse an aperture that does not start on a page boundary or is not a whole number of pages."
"Every sub-page aperture the machine has (the virtio-mmio transports on ARMv7-A) is refused; 0 are mapped."
"IoMapping::map_into shall map exactly the aperture's pages, readable and writable, onto the device's own physical addresses."
"Each mapped page translates to the aperture's physical page at the same offset, and a forked child reaches the same device pages rather than copies."

children.name: Pins
children.doc: src/kernel/src/object/pin.rs. The budget's and the quarantine's checks, P1 to P5 of docs/NVIDIA.md section 12.2, are in object/pin/check.rs, a child module that may read what pin.rs keeps to itself. Each device has a pin budget B, and live, quarantined and kept counts against it, kept on its domain under the quarantine's lock (NVIDIA N0f). The domain side of a pin is iommu's (part 16).

children.value: "A pin shall map exactly the held pages of the VMO into the device's domain and report each page's device address, in page order."
"A pin of two pages reports 2 addresses, each of which the domain translates to the VMO's page holding what the VMO holds."
"Dropping a pin of a live owner shall take its pages out of the domain, the invalidation complete, before the hold on its frames is released; when the domain refuses, the frames shall be kept."
"On a translated domain a closed pin's pages are no longer reachable through the domain."

"Dropping a pin on a translated domain after its owner terminated shall keep its pages mapped and its frames held, charged to nobody, in the quarantine (on an untranslated domain too, with nothing to unmap: L.object.127), moving them from its device's live count to its quarantined count; a pin closed by a live owner shall not be quarantined, and its pages shall leave the live count."
"A 2-page pin closed by a dead process leaves the device 2 pages quarantined and 0 live; a pin closed by a live process leaves 0 live, 0 quarantined and 0 kept."
"A pin shall be refused QuarantineFull, with nothing counted, when its device's quarantined and live pages and its own would pass twice the device's budget."
"With a budget of 2 pages and nothing kept: a 2-page pin is taken with 2 pages quarantined; a 1-page pin is refused with 4 quarantined; a 2-page pin is refused with 3 quarantined."

"quarantine_release shall give back every quarantined pin of the device's domain, out of the domain first and then to the allocator, counting the pages written after their driver died, and take off the quarantined count exactly the pages it gave back; a pin whose unpin is refused shall move to the kept count, which counts against twice the budget for good."

"Of two 1-page quarantined pins, one refused its unpin: the release gives back 1 page and leaves 0 quarantined and 1 kept; a 2-page pin is then taken at a budget of 2; with 2 more pages quarantined, a 2-page pin is refused QuarantineFull (1 kept + 2 + 2 > 4)."

"device_set_limit shall set a device's pin budget only through a handle carrying SET_LIMIT, never while the device has live pins, and never so that twice every budget raised above the default would pass the ceiling, a quarter of RAM; a refusal shall change nothing. Every answer on a device handle shall be audited with the device, the limit, and the old and new values: a set as DEVICE_LIMIT_SET, a refusal as DEVICE_LIMIT with its status. device_get_limit shall answer the budget, the ceiling and the room."

"Without SET_LIMIT the set is ACCESS_DENIED; with a live pin, BAD_STATE; a budget whose double passes the room, NO_MEMORY, with the budget and the room read back unchanged; a set to the budget it has is taken; the ceiling read back is the kernel's, nonzero, and the room no more than it; and the audit record holds, for the checking process and the device, the three refusals with their statuses and the set, each naming the pin budget and its old and new values."
"A pin shall be refused LimitReached, with nothing pinned and nothing counted, when its device's live pages and its own would pass the device's budget."
"With a budget of 2 pages, a 2-page pin is taken and counted 2 live, and a 1-page pin after it is refused LimitReached with the live count still 2."
"A pin's pages shall be counted live under the quarantine's lock, in the step that tests the budget, before the domain maps them, and given back if the domain refuses."
"A page pinned twice into one domain is refused by the domain, and the live count is as before the refused pin."

"On an untranslated domain, dropping a pin of a live owner shall give its frames back at once and take its pages off the device's live count, keeping nothing: the device of such a domain reaches all of memory anyway (VULNERABILITY-ANALYSIS V-03, finding F-59)."

"On an untranslated domain, six 2-page pins opened and closed in turn by a live process at a budget of 2 pages are each taken, leave the counts at 0 live, 0 quarantined and 0 kept, and leave each frame with no reference but the check's."

"On an untranslated domain, a pin dropped after its owner terminated shall go to the quarantine with its frames held and its pages counted quarantined, not kept, and the next HELLO its device's core accepts shall give it back."

"On an untranslated domain a 2-page pin closed by a dead process leaves 0 live, 2 quarantined and 0 kept with its frames still referenced; DeviceNode::hello_accepted then leaves the counts at 0 and each frame with no reference but the check's."

children.name: QuotaSlots
children.doc: src/kernel/src/object/quota.rs: the counters behind FRU_RSA.1.

children.value: "quota::charge shall add to the slot and to every slot above it only if every level stays within its limit, and a charge refused at any level shall leave no level charged and count one refusal at the level whose limit refused it."

"For each of the four resources, with a child limited to 5 under a parent limited to 3, the fourth unit is refused, child, parent and root each read 3, and one refusal is counted at the parent and none at the child; with the parent unlimited the child takes 5 and refuses the sixth."
"quota::uncharge shall take back exactly the amount from the slot and every slot above it, never below zero."
"A job charged and uncharged the same amount reads 0, and so does every level above it."
"Quota::set_limit shall set the limit the next charge is judged against, and Quota::usage shall report the use, the limit and the refusals."
"pids.max and memory.max written through cgroupfs reach the job's quota and read back as written; an empty job reads 0 used and 0 refused."
"A job's slot shall be held by its job, its child slots, each charge and each task that names it, and freed -- letting go of its parent -- when the last hold goes."
"After the quota checks' jobs are gone the number of live slots is what it was before them: every slot given back."
"claim shall hand out a slot, reused or new, with every use and refusal count at zero, every limit unlimited and the default weight."
"A job made on a slot another job freed after charging 5 of each resource under limits of 3 reads 0 used, 0 refused and no limit for each, and weight 100."
"charge_frame shall charge one page of memory to the slot and hold the slot, refusing when a limit would be passed, and uncharge_frame shall give back both."
"Faults in a job limited to 48 pages' worth are refused when the next page would not fit, the refusal counted, while a sibling faults 48 pages in; with the spaces gone every level's memory reads 0."
"charge_kernel shall charge kernel heap against the memory limit and count it again as kernel memory, both or neither, and uncharge_kernel shall give back both."
"At a 32 KiB limit each kind of personality object is refused one past its count while a sibling makes one, and every byte charged comes back when they go."
"charge_regardless shall add the amount to the slot and every slot above it whatever their limits say."
"A process moved into a job at its task limit of 8 is moved: the job reads 9 tasks and the job it left 1 fewer."
"charging_nobody shall run its work with no job charged for what it allocates, and restore the running task's job afterwards."
"Work run under charging_nobody in a job at its memory limit completes, the job's use is unchanged, and an allocation after it is charged to the job again."
"A Charge shall be taken from the job when the object it pays for is made, refusing the object when a limit would be passed, and given back when the object is dropped."
"Objects in a job limited to 5 are refused at exactly 5, a channel's two ends together; with them dropped the job holds 0."

"effective shall scale a task's weight, at each level from its job up, by the job's weight over the job's load, and adjust shall keep each job's load the weight of its runnable tasks and busy children."
"One spinning task alone in a job keeps about half a processor against eight in another job; with the tasks gone every job's load reads 0."
"Job::set_cpu_weight shall make the job's weight the value written."
"cpu.weight written 300 through cgroupfs reads back 300 from the job."
"Quota::set_weight shall clamp the weight to 1 to 10000, and change a busy job's contribution to its parent's load at once."
"A weight of 0 is stored as 1 and one of 20000 as 10000; setting a busy job's weight changes its parent's load by the difference of the scaled weights."

children.name: Jobs
children.doc: src/kernel/src/object/job.rs.

children.value: "root shall answer the one job at the top of the tree, in which every process starts unless it is forked from a process elsewhere or moved."
"A new process is in the root job, and a fork's child in its parent's job."

children.name: aChildsQuotaIsInsideItsParents
children.doc: The job's audit budget (docs/certification/AUDIT.md §3) is fixed here too, when the job is made: its own id, or its parent's where its maker says the job was its members' own to make (job::Budget), and written into its quota slot for the record of a refused charge. audit::check proves it.

children.value: "A child job shall be made inside its parent, with a quota slot inside the parent's."
"A charge to a grandchild is counted in its parent and in the root of the check's tree too, and a limit on the parent refuses it."
"A child job shall be charged as one object to the running task's job, and refused once its parent has been killed."
"In a job limited to 5 objects and holding 5, job_create is refused and nothing is charged; job_create in a killed job is refused."
"Job::new_named_child shall refuse a name a named child of the job already has."
"A second child named a.slice beside the first is refused."

"A new named child shall be refused when a job at or above its parent already holds as many descendants as its cgroup.max.descendants allows, or is more levels above it than its cgroup.max.depth allows."
"Under a job with cgroup.max.depth 1, a child is made and a grandchild refused Limited; under one with cgroup.max.descendants 2, a third descendant is refused."
"Job::remove_named_child shall refuse to remove a named child that holds a live anonymous job."
"rmdir of a cgroup holding a job native job_create made is refused EBUSY."
"A job remove_named_child has removed shall take no process and no child."
"Through a directory looked up before the rmdir, a move into the removed cgroup and a mkdir in it are each refused ENODEV, and the refused process stays where it was."
"Job::remove_named_child shall refuse to remove a named child that has a member not yet released or a named child of its own, and remove nothing."
"rmdir of a cgroup with one member is refused EBUSY and so is one with a child cgroup; after the member leaves and the child is removed, the rmdir succeeds."
"change_subtree_control shall enable only controllers offered and disable none a child still enables, and a job enabling a domain controller for its children shall admit no process."

"A controller not offered is refused; one a child enables cannot be disabled above it; a move into a job enabling a domain controller is refused, for a process counted in its job and for one that has left the count."
"A job shall keep the owner, group and mode set for each of its cgroupfs nodes, the last set winning, and shall name its path from the root's child down, an anonymous job as job-<id>."
"A node's owner set twice reads as the second; a path names an anonymous job by number above its named child."

"A job shall count its own members not yet released and its populated children, so that it is populated exactly while it or a job beneath it has a member not yet released, and each job whose state flips shall wake its waiters and fire its EMPTY registrations once no lock is held."
"A job with a member, and the job above it, are populated; each empties at its last member's release, not before, and wakes its event queue then and not while it stays populated."
"A job shall assert EMPTY exactly while it is not populated, and Job::observe shall fire a registration for EMPTY at once if the job is empty and otherwise when it empties."
"EMPTY is asserted while the job is empty and not while it has a member; a registration for EMPTY fires at the last release and not the first, and one made while the job is empty fires at once."
"Job::kill shall fire the job's registrations for TERMINATED, and the job shall report TERMINATED from then on."
"A registration for TERMINATED on a job fires when the job is killed, its packet saying what fired it, and a wait then sees the job TERMINATED."

"Job::kill shall mark the job and every job beneath it killed, fire their TERMINATED registrations, and end every process in them and none elsewhere; a job killed, or beneath one killed, shall refuse a new process or child from then on."

"Of 4 programs in a tree of three jobs and none, killing the middle job ends the middle and leaf programs with the kill's status and not the root's; killing the root ends it; the bystander finishes with its own status; a job beneath a killed one takes no new process."
"Job::kill_members shall end every process in the job and beneath it and leave every job as usable as it was."
"cgroup.kill ends the job's 1 member and leaves the job neither populated, killed nor dying, and a new member is taken."
"A process joining a job while a kill of either kind runs over it, or over a job above it, shall be ended, so that a loop of forks cannot outrun the kill."
"A program forking in a loop inside a job is ended with every child by one job_kill and by one cgroup.kill: 0 processes of the job left running after either."
"Dropping the last reference to the deepest job of a chain shall free every job of it with one stack frame, not one per job."
"A chain of 10,000 jobs each holding the one above, built one reference at a time as a job_create and handle_close loop builds it, is freed from the deepest end with no guard-page fault."
"Job::count_oom shall count an OOM or an OOM kill in the job and in every job above it, and wake whatever polls their memory.events."
"After a scoped OOM kill, memory.events counts one OOM kill in the job and in its parent and none in a sibling, and an epoll on it is woken by the kill with EPOLLPRI."

children.name: Processes
children.doc: src/kernel/src/object/process.rs: the core half of a process.

children.value: "Process::new shall make a process counted in its job and charged one task there; when the job's task limit refuses the charge it shall be marked over quota and charge nothing."
"A fork loop in a job limited to 8 tasks is refused at exactly 8, counting the forking process, the refusal counted as pids.events counts it, while a sibling job forks on."
"Process::new shall give the process a handle table that holds at most HANDLE_LIMIT, 4096, handles."
"Duplicating into one process's table until it is refused ends in NO_HANDLES with at most 4096 held."
"A process shall give every task it charged back to its job once, when it is reaped or dropped."
"With the fork loop's processes and the process moved in gone, both jobs' task counts, and their parent's, read 0."
"Process::charge_thread shall charge the job one task for each thread beside the first, refused at the task limit, and Process::uncharge_thread shall give it back once as the thread goes."
"In a job limited to 3 tasks, a process makes 2 threads and a third is refused EAGAIN; as the threads end the job's task count falls back to 1."
"A move shall count the process in the new job and out of the old one, and carry its task charge with it."
"A process of a job with 2 tasks moved into a job at its limit of 8 leaves 9 tasks there and 1 behind."
"A move refused because the destination, or a job above it, has been killed shall leave the process in its job."
"A move into a job beneath a killed one is refused and the process is still in the root job."
"Process::move_new_to shall refuse a process being made when the destination's task limit, or one above it, would be passed, leaving it where it was with nothing charged there."
"process_create into a job at its task limit is refused SHOULD_WAIT, the job's task count unchanged, and the refused process is not started."
"Process::leave_job shall count the process out of its job exactly once, however often it is called."
"A released member is counted out once: the job's live count falls by exactly 1 per member released."
"A process's bootstrap slot shall take one object and hand it over once, refusing a second give before the take and after it."

"A second give to one child is refused ALREADY_BOUND; the child's first process_bootstrap answers the end given with its rights and its second answers zero; a give after the take is refused ALREADY_BOUND."
"A bootstrap never taken shall be closed as its process ends, and the slot of an ended process shall refuse a give."
"A bootstrap never taken is closed as its holder ends, and its peer hears it; a give to an ended child is refused."
"Completing an execve shall seal a bootstrap slot nothing was given, and keep one given before it for the new program to take."
"After an execve with nothing given, a give is refused; one given before an execve is taken after it."
"Bootstrap::put_back shall hold again a bootstrap that was taken and could not be placed in the table."
"process_bootstrap into a full table is refused NO_HANDLES and the next process_bootstrap, with room, answers the handle given."
"Bootstrap::put_back shall hand a bootstrap that could not be placed back to be closed when the process has ended since it was taken."
"A bootstrap taken and not placed while its process ends is closed, and its peer hears it."
"Exit::close shall hand the registrations waiting for a process's end over to be fired, once, and a registration made afterwards shall fire at once."
"A watch registered while the process runs fires when it ends, and one registered afterwards fires at once, with its key."
"A process's Exit shall report its status and the signal that ended it once it has terminated, and nothing before."
"process_status says running before the end, killed by SIGTERM for a process a signal ended, and exited with its code for one that exited."
"A process made through the native ABI and never started shall be ended, with the kill's status, when the last handle to it goes."
"Closing an unstarted process's only handle ends it and it is freed; one whose handle rode unread in a channel ends when the channel is closed."
"A handle ProcessRef::new makes shall hold only how the process ended, and not the process."
"With nothing but a handle to it left, an ended process is freed."
"Control::started shall let go of the reference that held a process nobody had started, so that once started the process is held by its task and not by the handles process_create made."
"A process made by process_create and started, which then exits, is freed while its creator still holds its handle, and the handle reports its status."
"allocate shall hand out the number after the last one handed out, skipping every number in use and wrapping past 32767 to 300, and allocate_init shall hand out 1 only while no process holds it."
"Allocating through the range wraps to 300 and passes over a number still held; 0 numbers handed out twice."
"live shall list every live process once, under its pid and not its threads' numbers, and drop its references with the table unlocked."
"A job kill, which finds its processes through live, reports exactly 1 process ended for a job with 1 member."

children.name: OomKill
children.doc: src/kernel/src/object/oom.rs, and the quota reading it starts from.

children.value: "A user fault refused by a memory limit shall end, with the kill's status, a process of the job whose limit was full or beneath it and none outside it, count the kill there, and retry the fault."
"A program writing 8 MiB in a job limited to 1 MiB ends by SIGKILL, exactly 1 process killed, while a process with more resident memory in a sibling job lives."
"Among the live processes of the full job and the jobs beneath it, kill_within shall choose the one with the most resident pages, and never pid 1."
"With three processes of 1, 4 and 2 MiB resident in the full job, the one of 4 MiB is killed; with pid 1 the largest, the next largest is."
"A fault that failed for want of memory with no limit full, or with nothing killable in the full job, shall fail as it would without the OOM kill and kill nothing."
"A fault refused with every limit unset kills 0 processes and ends its program with SIGSEGV; a system call's fault there answers EFAULT."

"A victim that has ended and closed everything, whose address space no live process shares, shall have that space emptied at once rather than at its parent's wait, and a fault that finds a victim still ending shall wait and retry, killing no second process."
"Two faults at one full limit while the first victim is ending kill 1 process, and the job's memory use falls by the victim's resident pages before its parent waits."

children.name: SpeculationDomains
children.doc: docs/OPAQUE-KERNEL.md §9.2-§9.3a: a job marked at its creation, whose born members' switches skip the predictor invalidation. The customer's decision of 2026-10-01 (docs/BACKLOG.md).

children.value: "entered_space shall skip the predictor invalidation at a switch of address space only when the outgoing space's domain, read as it leaves, and the incoming space's are the same and not zero, and shall otherwise decide the barrier as it did before; forget_root shall clear a processor's last domain with its last root."

"Two members of one marked job switched both ways on one processor decide 0 barriers; a member and a process of no domain, and members of two marked jobs, decide 2; a switch inside the domain issues no invalidation; and a member installed after a forgotten member's root decides 1 (the `domain` line, cases 1, 2 and 10)."

"job_create shall make a job a speculation domain only with JOB_SPECULATION_DOMAIN, only under MANAGE on the parent, and only as it makes the job; it shall refuse any other option bit with INVALID_ARGS, write a DOMAIN audit record for each job it marks and none for a refusal, and make every other job, a child of a marked one included, in no domain."

"job_create with the option and a parent handle without MANAGE answers ACCESS_DENIED, with an unknown bit INVALID_ARGS, and neither adds a DOMAIN record; with MANAGE it adds one, naming the new job, its parent and its domain (the `domain` line, case 4)."

"A process shall be in a speculation domain only if it was made in the marked job, by process_create or by a fork of a member in the same job; its address space shall carry the domain, and a space a process of another domain comes to share shall be in no domain from then on."

"A process made in a marked job reports the job's domain, and a member whose space a process of no domain shares decides the barrier both ways with another member (the `domain` line, case 6); a marked job inside a marked job is a domain of its own (case 7); a child job of a marked job is in no domain, a member's fork is a member, and a process moved into a marked job, its fork, and a process that left before its birth are not (cases 9 and 10)."

"A member shall leave its speculation domain for good, and its address space with it, when it moves between jobs, and when it stops being dumpable: a set-id execve, a change of credentials, or PR_SET_DUMPABLE; and every processor whose last space was in the domain shall issue the barrier before the leave returns. In hardened builds the leave shall find them two ways, and wait for a grace period: a scan that asks each processor whose last domain is the leaver's, and a local check by which each processor, answering the leave's grace period with interrupts masked, compares its own last domain with the domains being left and issues the barrier itself on a match. A build with the mitigations off has no barrier, and its leave waits for no grace period. Each domain being left shall be published in a slot of its own in a set, sequentially consistent and before the scan and before the grace period's generation is advanced, and the answering processor shall read the generation before the set, so that one that records the domain after the scan has passed it is still found (F-60)."

"A member moved out of its job, one whose credentials changed and one made not dumpable each decide the barrier both ways with a member left in the domain (the `domain` line, cases 3 and 5); a member that leaves makes this processor and one running a thread in its space each decide the barrier before the leave returns (case 8); and a processor made, by stage 9's hook between the scan and the grace period, to record the domain after the scan has passed it decides the barrier before the leave returns (case 11), which the local check removed fails."

children.name: DeviceConfiguration
children.doc: A published PCI node's configuration space, written by the kernel and, through device_config_write, by its driver: one lock per node, as a type (docs/NVIDIA.md section 12.1).

children.value: "Every write to a published node's PCI configuration space, by the kernel or by a driver, shall be made holding the node's one configuration lock, through the one type that holds it; enumeration's writers run at stage 10, before any node is published."

"A ConfigWrites is made only by taking the lock, MappedConfig has no write, and bus mastering, an MSI mint and mask, MSI-X's enable and a driver's write go through ConfigWrites. Bus mastering switched on and off on one processor while another makes a driver's configuration writes to the same function, 1,000 rounds, reads back as dma_on says every time (the second config line)."

children.name: ChannelWriteRead
children.doc: docs/OPAQUE-KERNEL.md §9.4, items 3 and 4: channel_write_read (0x1013), the inbox's slot it writes into, its answer in registers, and the wait it trusts. Checked through each architecture's own entry by object::write_read_check, the `wrread` line.

children.value: "Endpoint::write_small shall refuse a message as Endpoint::write does -- the peer closed, more bytes than three words, the queue full -- and shall otherwise hold a message of at most three words without handles in the peer's slot only while nothing waits there and the inbox's spare has room for it or can be given it, queueing it behind what does, so that the slot always holds the oldest message and a buffer for it."
"A small message written behind a queued one is read after it, and a send to a closed peer, one past three words and one on a handle without WRITE send nothing (the `wrread` line)."

"Endpoint::read shall take the message held in the slot before any queued, as a message without handles in the inbox's spare, never failing for memory, leave it with its size reported when the caller has too little room, and Endpoint::unread shall put a message back ahead of one the slot has taken since, so that every reader sees the messages in the order written."

"A message held in the slot is read before one queued after it; a read with room for 2 bytes of a 5-byte slot message is refused with its size and the next read returns it whole; a message taken from the slot and put back after the slot took another is read first, then the other (the `wrread` line)."

"Endpoint::read_small shall take the oldest message only if it carries no handles and at most three words, and give its bytes followed by zeros to the width of three words; it shall leave any other message queued and report its size."

"A 5-byte message held in the slot and a 7-byte message queued each come back from channel_write_read as their bytes then zeros, and a 40-byte message is refused by a small read and then read whole (the `wrread` line)."

"channel_write_read shall send its count bytes from its third to fifth argument registers, then answer the next message on the same end with its size in the return register and its words in the second to fourth argument registers, zero past its bytes; a call that fails shall answer its status in the return register alone and leave the second to fourth argument registers as the program set them, on each architecture's entry."

"Through the entry, a call that sends 3 bytes and finds a 4-byte answer waiting answers 4 and its words, and the peer reads the 3 bytes then zeros; a closed handle, a count past three words, a send without WRITE, a message too big for registers, and a send and a receive on a closed peer each answer their status with registers 2 to 4 as sent, 6 of 6 (the `wrread` line)."

"channel_write_read's wait shall file no recheck while it is listed on its end's queue, and shall end on each of what it waits for: a message arriving on the end, the peer's close, and its process's end or another thread's execve, each of which wakes it; it shall then answer the message, PEER_CLOSED, or EINTR. The message and the close shall be read from the end's state word and the end or execve from the task's END bit, each ordered against the task's blocked state by a SeqCst fence on each side (L.object.141, L.sched.40)."

"A thread blocked in channel_write_read and listed on its end's queue is woken within 10 s by a message, which it answers, by its peer's close, which it answers PEER_CLOSED, and by its process's kill, after which its thread ends (the `wrread` line)."

"Under a channel end's inbox lock, its state word's NONEMPTY shall be set exactly when the inbox holds a message, after every operation that changes that -- a write, a small write, a read, a small read, a put-back and the close's drain -- and its PEER_CLOSED shall be set once the peer has closed, after the peer's closed and before the end's waiters are woken."

"4096 writes, small writes, reads, small reads and put-backs in a pseudo-random order on one pair leave each end's word equal to its inbox after every one, each operation having crossed the empty boundary once first, and a close is marked in the survivor's (the `chword` line); with the put-back's update removed the check fails after a put-back into an empty inbox."

"channel_write_read's wait shall read readiness with one load of its end's state word and one of the caller's END bit, without the inbox lock or the personality; and a writer, a put-back and a closer shall make a SeqCst fence after the word's store and before their wake reads a waiter's state, paired with the wait's fence after it stores BLOCKED, so that a waiter listed and not yet blocked either is found blocked or reads the word."

"The `wrread` line's message and close cases; with the close's mark removed, the close case's waiter stays blocked and the check fails by name. The loom model of a waiter listed and not yet blocked against a writer, a closer, both, and an end finds no lost wake, and its two controls, the writer without its fence and the closer marking after its wake, each find one (`cargo xtask loom`, src/tests/loom)."

children.name: Decisions
children.doc: src/kernel/src/sched/queue.rs and src/kernel/src/sched/mod.rs: when a processor next decides, and what a yield asks for.

children.value: "While any task waits on a processor's queue, CpuQueue::arm_timer shall arm the next decision no more than one configured slice away, however long a request the running task holds."

"With an entity queued that is not eligible and the running one having yielded 600 times, so that its remaining request exceeds 100 slices, the queue's next decision is at most one slice away; with nothing queued there is none."
"A yield by the only task on a processor's queue shall leave its request unchanged."
"After 600 yields with nothing else queued, the running entity's remaining slice is what it was before the first."

children.name: Wakes
children.doc: src/kernel/src/timer.rs and src/kernel/src/sched/mod.rs: the timer's skipped arm, the clock, and the decisions a channel round trip's wakes defer (docs/OPAQUE-KERNEL.md §9.4, items 1, 2, 3 and 6; the consultant's conditions of 2026-10-02).

children.value: "timer::after shall keep, for each processor, the clock read after the hardware was armed plus the delay asked for, and shall leave a one-shot armed only when that is no later than the new deadline; otherwise it shall arm for the new one, so that no interrupt asked for is served later than the hardware's own one-tick rounding of a delay shorter than a tick."
"On the boot processor, a 2 ms one-shot asked for while a 1 s one is armed, and one asked for before a 1 s one, each fire within 200 ms of the 2 ms deadline (the `arm` line)."
"now_nanos shall convert the counter to nanoseconds as ticks times 10^9 over the counter's rate, rounded down, exactly, and u64::MAX past what 64 bits hold."

"At 12 counter rates from 1 Hz to u64::MAX and 10 tick values at each, from 0 to u64::MAX across a second's boundaries and the saturation point, the two-division conversion equals the 128-bit formula (ferrix-vdso's host test)."

"A wake made inside a system call shall leave its decision to the call's end (sched::call_left), the next preempt_enable that brings the count to zero, or the next interrupt exit, whichever comes first; and a Sync wake shall arm the waker's processor's timer for its next decision, so that a waker that does not block leaves the woken task waiting at most one slice."
"Argued in MEMORY-AND-TIMING §2.2c: no check times the deferral, which sits inside H.SCHED.2's bound of one slice plus the timer overruns served."

"A Sync wake shall move the task it wakes onto the waker's processor only when the task is asleep at its home and in nothing else, its affinity allows the waker's processor, and nothing else is queued there, deciding under both processors' queue locks, and shall otherwise wake it where it is."

"At two processors or more, a reader blocked in channel_write_read and free to move, woken by a Sync write from another processor, answers every time and is moved in at least one of 8 rounds; a reader pinned to processor 1 woken from processor 0 answers on processor 1 in each of 8 rounds (the `sync` line)."

"attention_due, asked at every way out to ring 3 on every architecture -- a call's, an interrupt's, a fault's, and the last look of the personality's return_to_user -- with interrupts masked, shall read the running task's pending-work word once, clear STOP and SIGNAL in it if they are set before anything reads what they stand for, and ask the personality's needs_attention when END, STOP, SIGNAL or TRACE was set; FILTERED shall not be read there."

"A program of three threads stopped by its stop alone, which posts STOP and no signal, has both counting threads park and stay still, and runs again after SIGCONT (stage 7's stop check, its second stop); every boot, test-shell, test-threads, test-vfs and test-init pass with the self-checks on, where L.sched.33's look runs at every clear word."

"notify shall post its bits to the task's word with a Release read-modify-write before it wakes the task and interrupts its processor; post and post_own shall only set bits; and only the task's own look shall clear any, with an Acquire read-modify-write, and END never."

"The stop check's second stop, posted by notify's half under the list's lock and woken after it, parks both counting threads; with the post removed the same check fails by name. The loom model of a post against the task's clear and read finds the state read or the bit kept, and its control, the clear after the read, finds neither (`cargo xtask loom`)."

"A wake shall read its target's state only under the run-queue lock of the processor that owns the target, after reading which processor that is again under that lock, with no way out before it that reads the state without the lock."

"At two processors or more, a blocker that holds its own run-queue lock while a poster on another processor reaches its wake, then marks itself blocked and lets the lock go, is woken within 100 ms (the `wakerow` line); with a lock-free exit in wake_at_home the check fails by name."

"With the self-checks on, attention_due shall ask needs_attention at a clear word too, and audit shall stop the machine with FX-0520 when it answers yes while no poster is between its write and its post and the word is still clear; every poster shall bracket its write and its post in a Posting."
"Every boot, test-shell, test-threads, test-vfs and test-init reach their marker with the look on; with enter_stop's STOP to the other tasks removed, test-threads stops with FX-0520's message."

"The hook in notify shall be armed only by stage 9's checks, record which check armed it and the task it watches, be disarmed by that check whatever the check found, and be required disarmed before the boot's marker, with F-60's leave hook, which stops with FX-0908 naming the check if it is not."
"The `wakerow` line, then the marker; with the check's disarm removed the boot stops with FX-0908's message naming the wake row."

"end_record shall store the process's end and then, after a SeqCst fence, post END to every task its list holds, waking each and interrupting its processor, with nothing allocated and no task let go under the list's lock; list_task shall list a task before it can run, failing its start with AllocError when the list cannot grow."

"A program past its cgroup's memory.max is OOM-killed and ends (the `cgroups` line's OOM case, which no signal reaches first); with end_record's post removed it never ends and the check fails by name."

"wake_posted, the wake of every notify and of post_to_tasks, shall make a SeqCst fence after the bits are posted and before the wake reads the task's state, paired with a trusting wait's fence after it stores BLOCKED, so that a wait that reads the bit itself is found blocked or reads it."

"A thread blocked in channel_write_read is ended by its process's kill (the `wrread` line); with that wait reading no END it stays blocked and the check fails by name. The loom model of an end posted against a waiter listed and not yet blocked finds no lost wake (`cargo xtask loom`)."

children.name: Preemption
children.doc: src/kernel/src/sched/preempt.rs and src/kernel/src/sched/mod.rs: the preemption count every crate::sync::SpinLock raises, kept in each processor's record without a locked operation (docs/OPAQUE-KERNEL.md §9.8, 2b; the consultant's OK IF of 2026-10-02, condition 2).

children.value: "A preemption-disabling lock, and a raise by hand, shall raise and lower the preemption count and, for a lock, the locks held of the processor its holder runs on, in that processor's record and without a locked operation, so that no update is lost to an interrupt and none lands on another processor's record: on x86-64 in one GS-relative instruction, with every entry that can reach it running on the kernel's GS base; on AArch64 and ARMv7-A with every exception that can take a lock masked; and a report reading another processor's count shall read each of the count and the locks held whole."

"At two processors or more, two tasks per processor, preempted by the timer and moving between processors, take and let go of a lock 100000 times each with raises by hand among them and move at least once (the `preempt` line). The stress provokes a lost or misplaced update; what detects one is FX-0503's test at the release, which stops the boot when the locks held or the count it lowers is already zero, and, behind it, every processor's count and locks held read zero there by a task that holds nothing. The three atomicity controls (x86-64's record found before the add, the Arm mask removed on aarch64 and on armv7a at two processors) each stop the boot on FX-0503's held-zero message."

"The scheduler shall stop the machine (FX-0503), naming the site that last raised the count, when it is asked to switch with its processor's count raised, and when a release finds the count, or for a lock the locks held, already at zero, having put the word back first; a release that brings the count to zero shall make the decision an interrupt deferred, if interrupts are on."

"The release's cover test refuses a word whose count, or for a lock whose locks held, is zero, and passes one that covers the release (the stage-5 checks). That held-zero test is the detector L.sched.20's stress relies on; the negative controls of a task that sleeps holding a lock and of a release with nothing raised each stop the boot on FX-0503's message."

"may_block shall answer true only when the scheduler runs, interrupts are on, a task is running, and the count of the processor it runs on, read so that the processor and its count are one processor's (one instruction on x86-64, interrupts masked on Arm), is zero."
"A task holding nothing may block; holding a preemption-disabling lock, or with the count raised by hand, it may not; once it lets go it may again (the stage-5 checks)."

"A try_lock of a preemption-disabling lock that fails shall leave its processor's count and locks held as it found them, and with interrupts masked shall not switch; one that succeeds shall raise both by one until its guard drops; and ferrix_sync::SpinLock::try_lock_manually shall take no ticket when it fails."

"With a lock held, a try_lock of it with interrupts on and with them masked leaves the count and the locks held unchanged and, masked, the task's switches unchanged; a try_lock_manually of a held plain lock fails and changes neither; a successful try_lock raises both by one until it drops (the stage-5 checks, and ferrix-sync's host test of try_lock_manually)."

children.name: RunningTask
children.doc: src/kernel/src/sched/borrow.rs and src/kernel/src/sched/mod.rs: the running task borrowed from the processor's record (docs/OPAQUE-KERNEL.md §9.8, 2a; the consultant's OK IF of 2026-10-02, condition 1, and Q1).

children.value: "Whenever interrupts are on, each processor's record shall name, as Arc::as_ptr, the task its run queue's current holds; the scheduler shall write the two together, on that processor with interrupts masked and its queue lock held, at the boot task's adoption, at an idle task's installation and at every switch, and nowhere else."

"From boot to the end of stage 5, an audit compares the record with the queue's current, read under its lock, once the boot task is adopted, as each processor's idle task first runs, in the incoming context of every switch and at every interrupt exit, and finds no mismatch at any site; and two tasks per processor, yielding to each other, resume after a switch 10000 times, each time with the record naming the queue's current and the task itself (the `borrow` line). Removing the record's write at the adoption, at the idle installation or at the switch stops the boot on that site's message."

"with_current shall lend the running task only to a closure, by a reference its result cannot name, read from the processor's record so that the processor and its record are one processor's (one instruction on x86-64, interrupts masked on Arm); current() shall answer the running task as an Arc of the caller's own without taking the run queue's lock; and before the records are kept both shall answer none."

"Each of the borrow check's 10000 resumptions borrows the running task and finds the task itself, and every audit's borrowed pointer equals the queue's current (the `borrow` line); every boot, shell and bench gate runs on current() made this way."

children.name: Discovery
children.doc: src/kernel/src/iommu.rs, the first half: every unit firmware describes, and where it puts each PCI function's DMA. Read apart from bring-up, which programs units, and printed on every boot whether or not the checks run.

children.value: "units shall name every VT-d unit a DMAR describes and every SMMUv3 an IORT, or without ACPI a device tree, describes, each once and none at address 0 or of length 0, with the length of registers no driver may be given."
"The discovery line counts 1 VT-d unit and 0 SMMUv3s on x86-64, and 0 and 1 on AArch64 and ARMv7-A, as the machines xtask boots configure them."
"report shall count on the console the PCI functions firmware places behind a unit, those it places behind none, and those it describes in a way the kernel cannot follow."
"On every machine xtask test-boot boots, the discovery line is printed and counts 1 or more PCI functions behind a unit and 0 unresolved."
"place_dmar shall place a function that a single-hop endpoint scope of a DRHD on its segment names behind that DRHD's unit, as its requester ID."
"On x86-64 each PCI function on bus 0 is reported behind the unit at the DRHD's register base as the stream bus << 8 | device << 3 | function."

"place_iort shall place a function behind the SMMUv3 that its segment's root complex maps its requester ID to, as the stream ID the mapping gives, and a function mapped to an ITS group behind no unit."
"On AArch64 each of the 5 PCI functions is reported behind the SMMUv3 at the IORT's base address as the stream its root complex's ID mapping gives."

"place_tree shall place a function behind the SMMUv3 its ECAM host's iommu-map names for its requester ID, as the stream ID the map gives, taking the host that names the function's segment or the only host."
"On ARMv7-A each of the 5 PCI functions is reported behind the SMMUv3 the device tree gives as the stream its host's iommu-map gives."

"A function firmware describes in a way the kernel cannot follow -- a DMAR scope whose path runs through a function that is not a bridge, or a function below a named bridge whose DMA arrives under a bridge's alias, an IORT mapping to a node that is not there or to an SMMUv1 or v2, a device tree whose hosts cannot be told apart, a map naming a unit that is not among the units -- shall be counted unresolved, never bypassing."
"Each of those descriptions, given for a function no endpoint scope or mapping otherwise places, is counted 1 unresolved and 0 bypassing."

children.name: BringUpAndDomains
children.doc: src/kernel/src/iommu.rs, bring-up and domain_for, and the halves of iommu/vtd.rs and iommu/smmuv3.rs that program a unit and attach a domain to it.

children.value: "bring_up shall turn translation on for the VT-d units a DMAR describes and the SMMUv3s an IORT describes that it can drive."

"On x86-64 (VT-d) and AArch64 (SMMUv3) the entropy device's write outside its domain is refused and recorded by its unit, which a unit does only while translating: 1 or more out-of-domain writes faulted (the `pci` line)."

"bring_up shall leave alone, count and say why, a unit that is not what the driver needs -- a VT-d unit not of version 1, without three-level tables or needing its write buffer flushed, an SMMUv3 without an AArch64 stage 2, 8 stream ID bits or 4 KiB tables with 40-bit output, either left translating by firmware -- or for which there is no frame, and shall unmap its registers."
"Each of those units is counted 1 left alone with its reason on the bring-up line, 0 translating, and its register window is unmapped."
"Once a unit translates, a function behind it with no domain shall reach nothing: VT-d finds no context entry, and every SMMUv3 stream table entry is valid and aborting until a domain is attached."
"A DMA by a function behind a translating unit that has been given no domain is refused and recorded against its stream."

"domain_for shall give a function the DMAR puts behind a translating VT-d unit a domain on that unit as its source ID, and one an IORT root complex sends to a translating SMMUv3 a domain on it as the stream the mapping gives."
"On x86-64 and AArch64 the entropy device's domain names a stream, and its unit records the probe's refused write against that stream: 1 or more out-of-domain writes faulted (the `pci` line)."
"domain_for shall give an untranslated domain to a function no translating unit covers, including every function before bring_up and every function behind an SMMUv3 only a device tree describes."
"On ARMv7-A the first PCI function's domain is untranslated, and so is a domain made before bring_up."
"The first pin into an untranslated domain shall say on the console, once, that device DMA reaches all of memory: degraded trusted mode."
"An ARMv7-A boot prints the degraded trusted mode line exactly once, and an x86-64 or AArch64 boot, whose pins are translated, 0 times."
"A unit shall refuse a second domain for a function or stream that has one, and domain_for shall then answer an untranslated domain and say why, never two domains translating one device."
"For the first PCI function, whose translated domain the stage 10 check pinned through, a second domain_for answers an untranslated domain."
"A translated domain dropped with no page pinned shall detach from its unit, so that the function can be given a domain again."
"A translated domain made for a PCI function that had none, dropped with nothing pinned, is followed by a second domain_for for the function that is translated."

"detach shall return a domain's identifier or VMID and its root table, and on an SMMUv3 the doorbell's tables, only after the unit has forgotten the domain, and shall keep them when the unit never answers."
"Attaching and detaching a domain N times leaves the free-frame count and the identifiers in use as they were; a detach whose invalidation times out frees 0 frames."
"A translated domain dropped while pages are still pinned into it shall stay attached, its tables and context entry or stream table entry kept."
"A domain dropped holding a pin of one page still translates that page's address afterwards, and its function is refused a new domain."

"attach shall refuse a stream past the SMMUv3's table, a unit with no identifier or VMID left, and a function or stream it cannot record for want of memory or a frame, and a refused attach shall give back the root table it took and write no entry."
