"Each refusal leaves the free-frame count, the identifiers in use and the context or stream table entry as they were."
"Every SMMUv3 domain shall map the GICv2m MSI doorbell page at its own address, so that a device's MSI writes, which the unit translates like any DMA, reach the interrupt controller."
"A device in a translated SMMUv3 domain that completes a request by MSI-X has the completion delivered, and a domain without the doorbell mapped has its MSI write faulted."

children.name: Pins
children.doc: src/kernel/src/iommu.rs, Domain::pin and Domain::unpin: the domain side of every pin, the same for both kinds of unit, and the unit's flush that ends an unpin.

children.value: "pin shall map each frame it is given at its own physical address, answer each page's device address in the order the frames were given, and count the pages it holds."
"A pin of two frames through the first PCI function's domain answers the frames' physical addresses in order, the domain resolves each to itself, and its pinned-page count rises by 2."
"unpin shall take a pin's pages out of its domain's tables and count them back."
"After its own domain unpins the two-frame pin, the pinned-page count is back where it was and, on a translated domain, neither frame's address resolves."
"unpin shall refuse a pin another domain took with Foreign, and hand the pin back unchanged."
"A domain asked to unpin the two-frame pin of another domain refuses Foreign and hands the pin back, which its own domain then unpins."
"pin shall refuse a pin of no frames with Empty."
"A pin of an empty list of frames is refused Empty."
"pin shall refuse with OutOfRange, mapping nothing, a frame whose address does not fit in 64 bits or, in a translated domain, in the 39 bits its tables reach."
"A pin into a translated domain naming one frame at or above 2^39 bytes, beside one below, is refused OutOfRange with the pinned-page count unchanged and neither address resolving."
"A pin into a translated domain of a page already pinned there shall be refused with AlreadyPinned."
"On a translated domain, a vmo_pin of a page already pinned into it is refused ALREADY_BOUND."
"A pin refused part-way shall unmap every page it had mapped, and give back the tables that emptied once the unit has forgotten them."
"A pin of three frames whose third is already pinned is refused, and afterwards the first two do not resolve and the free-frame count is as it was."
"unpin shall return only once the unit has completed the invalidation of the pages it took out, and shall answer Unit, handing the pin back, when the unit never completes it."
"An unpin from a unit made never to finish its invalidation answers Unit and hands the pin back; from a unit that finishes, it returns after the unit's completion was read."
"A table an unpin or an undone pin empties shall go back to the frame allocator only after the unit's invalidation has completed, and shall be kept when it has not."
"An unpin that empties a table frees it only after the flush answers; with the flush made to fail, the table stays out of the allocator."
"A VT-d unit in caching mode shall be told to forget a domain's cached translations after a map as well as after an unmap, since it caches entries that were not present."
"Under a VT-d unit in caching mode, a device reaches a page pinned after the same address had been walked while unmapped, with 0 faults recorded."
"A wait on a unit made in a context that may block shall be made with interrupts on, and counted."
"On a translated domain, the boot task's unpin of the two-frame pin raises the count of unit waits made in a context that may block."

children.name: Gate
children.doc: src/kernel/src/iommu/gate.rs: how an operation waits for a unit without masking interrupts.

children.value: "poll shall answer true once the unit answers before the deadline, and false after one last look past it."

"A wait on a unit that never answers, with its deadline already past, answers false; a wait by a task that may block, on a unit that answers on its 101st look, with a deadline 5 s away, answers true."
"A gate shall admit one operation at a time, refuse the next once its patience has passed, and admit the next once the holder leaves."
"With a gate held, an entry with a patience of 10 ms is refused; once the holder leaves, an entry is admitted."
"A task waiting to enter a held gate shall sleep, and shall be woken and admitted when the holder leaves."
"A second task waiting on a gate the first holds for 10 ms is admitted after the first leaves and before its own patience has passed, having slept meanwhile."
"A unit's commands shall run one at a time, each waited for up to the unit's patience, and one the unit does not finish, or an SMMUv3 command it stops on, shall answer an error."
"A command to a unit made never to finish answers an error within its patience, and an SMMUv3 command queue stopped with an error answers it refused."

children.name: Faults
children.doc: src/kernel/src/iommu.rs, the faults half, and the fault readers of iommu/vtd.rs and iommu/smmuv3.rs.

children.value: "A fault shall print as its unit recorded it: a refused access by its stream, page and direction, an SMMUv3 event by its type's name, an event queue's overflow and a VT-d unit's lost fault as such."
"A refused read and a refused write, a lost SMMUv3 event, a VT-d overflow and SMMUv3 events 0x10 and 0xFF each print the words given for them, 0xFF as reserved."
"A VT-d unit's take_fault shall answer the refused access its first record holds as the source ID, page and direction the unit wrote."
"On x86-64 the probe reads its fault back as a write by the entropy device's stream to the probe's page: 1 or more out-of-domain writes faulted (the `pci` line)."
"An SMMUv3's take_fault shall answer a translation, address size, access flag or permission event as a refused access by its stream, page and direction."
"On AArch64 the probe reads its fault back as a write by the entropy device's stream to the probe's page: 1 or more out-of-domain writes faulted (the `pci` line)."
"A VT-d unit's take_fault shall clear each record it answers, and answer a primary fault overflow, once the record is empty, as an Overflow against the record taken last, and clear it."
"With the record full and a second fault dropped, take_fault answers the full record's access, then 1 Overflow naming it, then nothing."

"An SMMUv3's take_fault shall consume each event it answers, answer every event type but the four refused accesses as an Event naming it, and answer an event queue that overflowed as Lost, first and acknowledged."
"A queue holding a C_BAD_STREAMID event answers Event(0x02); a queue whose overflow flag differs from the acknowledgement answers Lost once and then its events, each once."
"enable shall clear a fault firmware left recorded in a VT-d unit, and its overflow, before translation goes on."
"A unit brought up with a fault and an overflow left recorded answers no fault from take_fault afterwards."
"provoke shall clear the unit's faults and register the device's stream and the page, saying so on the console, before the device is made to write it."
"After provoke, the unit holds no fault, and the stream and page are registered and printed on the `on purpose` line."
"A refused access by a registered stream to its registered page, and a VT-d overflow whose full record held one, shall not be counted stray, however late it is read."
"A fault equal to a registered stream and page, taken through a domain and again by the audit, leaves the stray count unchanged; the same fault at another page raises it by 1."
"A fault taken that no check provoked shall be counted stray, and apart when it is not a refused access, whether a check, the clearing before a probe or the audit took it."
"An SMMUv3 event and a VT-d overflow no check registered each raise the stray count and the stray-event count by 1."

"audit_faults shall take the faults every translating unit holds, up to 256 a unit, and report the faults no check provoked since translation went on, the first it read itself, and the provoked ones it found late."
"With 1 stray fault left in a unit's record, the audit reports 1 unit read, 1 stray and that fault as the first."

"Every fault read from a unit, by the fault audit or through a domain, shall be written to the audit record as one DMA_FAULT, refused, naming the device's stream and the page it addressed, with the kernel as its subject."

"On a boot where a unit translates, the audit record holds a DMA_FAULT from the out-of-domain probe, refused, with pid 0; with the record's event swapped at recorded, or its subject made a process, the end-of-boot audit check fails naming it."

"A DMAR scope's path shall be followed through each bridge's secondary bus, and a function shall count as its own requester only if every bridge from it up to its root bus is a PCIe port (root, upstream or downstream): behind a PCIe-to-PCI or conventional bridge, on a bus two bridges claim, or under a loop of bus numbers, it is aliased, never its own. The decision every placement asks (claims) shall answer aliased wherever the walk below a named bridge does."

"Host tests: a path is followed through each bridge's secondary bus; a function behind a root port or a switch is its own requester; one named by a path through a PCIe-to-PCI bridge, on a bus two bridges claim, on a bus no bridge explains below a named bridge, or under a loop of bus numbers is not; only Express port types 4, 5 and 6 forward a requester ID; a scope path with an odd byte is not whole. ferrix_pci::topology::claims, which iommu::claims answers with, claims a two-hop endpoint through a PCIe-to-PCI bridge, a function on a bus no bridge explains below a named bridge and one on a bus two bridges claim as aliased, what PCIe ports alone reach as its own, and nothing outside the scope; with claims answering own whenever the scope reaches the function, three of those tests fail."

"place_dmar shall place a function that a DRHD's endpoint or sub-hierarchy scope reaches, as its own requester, behind that DRHD's unit, and domain_for shall attach a translated domain for it on that unit; a function the scope reaches under an alias, or by a path that is not whole, shall be unresolved and get no domain."

"On x86-64 under KVM and TCG every PCI function, the virtio-rng and edu below PCIe root ports included, is placed behind the unit with 0 bypassing and 0 unresolved, and the out-of-domain probe's write from the rng below a root port (stream 0x100) is faulted by the unit; with domains not following scopes the boot panics on the rng's untranslated DMA, and with placement ignoring sub-hierarchies test-boot fails on 2 bypassing."

"A VT-d unit without ECAP.QI shall be left alone, with the reason printed. On a unit brought up, every context-cache and IOTLB invalidation -- at enable, attach, detach, after an unmap or a caching-mode map, and the quarantine's release -- shall be made through the unit's invalidation queue: the descriptor and a fenced wait descriptor behind it are written and cleaned to memory, the tail is moved past both, and the invalidation completes only when the wait's status word reads that submission's own sequence number. No register-based invalidation shall be issued."

"On x86-64 under KVM and TCG the iommu line counts the context-cache and IOTLB invalidations queued, both more than 0, and no unit reads back a register-based invalidation pending; test-boot requires the line. With one flush put back on the register path, QEMU never performs it while the queue is on and the boot fails at stage 10. Host tests: each descriptor is laid out as the specification says and passes QEMU's reserved-bit masks; the queue registers name sixteen-byte slots; a full queue is never taken for an empty one."

"A VT-d invalidation whose wait status is not written within the unit's patience, or during which FSTS reads IQE, ICE or ITE, shall answer an error, and its caller shall release nothing the unit may still reach: an unpin hands the pin back and its frames are kept and counted in kept. ICE shall be cleared (written one) and counted as soon as it is taken, so that it fails that invalidation only. After IQE or ITE the unit shall be marked failed: every later invalidation on it answers an error without touching the queue, and the failure is reported once to the end-of-boot fault audit as a stray fault."

"On x86-64 under KVM and TCG check R7 unpins a two-page pin whose wait descriptor, through the check-only Wait::Unwritten, writes no status: the invalidation fails, the two pages move from live to kept and the frames stay held, and the iommu line says exactly one invalidation failed, as R7 made it; with Pin::drop taking the error for success the boot panics with 'frames released after a failed invalidation'. On every unit an ICE the check plants fails one invalidation, is cleared and counted, and the next invalidation completes with the unit not failed; with the clear dropped the boot panics with 'an invalidation after a cleared completion error failed'. QEMU's unit cannot raise ICE, so the check plants it in the unit's software mirror of FSTS; that writing one clears it on a real unit rests on the specification's write-one-to-clear semantics for FSTS.ICE, not on a boot. Host tests: a wait writes its sequence number, or with Unwritten nothing, as a valid descriptor; a stopped queue is never taken for a completion, nor a completion error for a timeout."

"A VT-d unit firmware left remapping interrupts shall have IRE cleared and read back clear, and one whose invalidation queue firmware left on shall have the queue drained, QIE cleared and read back clear, each within the unit's patience, before the kernel's own setup; then any IQE, ICE or ITE firmware left in FSTS shall be cleared and FSTS read back clear of them. A unit that does not shall be left alone with the reason printed. GCMD writes shall not repeat CFI."

"On x86-64 under KVM and TCG, before each unit's enable, the check turns its queue on as firmware would and ends it with a completed wait, and open's path turns it off and reads it off; the iommu line counts it on every unit. With the QIE clear dropped from that path, the boot panics with 'firmware left its invalidation queue on and it would not stop'."

"On a VT-d unit whose ECAP.C is clear, every root, context and second-level entry the kernel writes shall be noted and cleaned from the processor's caches to memory (clflush of each line written, then mfence) before the change that wrote it is published: before the context-cache or IOTLB invalidation that publishes an attach or a detach, and before a map or an unmap returns. A change whose record still holds a write not cleaned at that point shall be refused -- an attach or detach before its invalidation, a map or unmap with an error, so that the pin unwinds or the frames are kept -- and counted. That every write to memory the unit walks is noted rests on construction: write_entry, table and the mapper's writes through Walked are vtd.rs's only writers of that memory. On a unit whose ECAP.C is set, nothing shall be noted or cleaned."

"On x86-64 under KVM and TCG, where QEMU's unit reports ECAP.C clear, the iommu line counts the entry writes noted and cleaned and the changes that each found them cleaned before their own publish point, and test-boot requires the line; the check proves each change's noted writes were cleaned, not that every write was noted. With the clean before an unmap's return dropped, the unmap is refused with the line 'a VT-d change was refused: a table write was not cleaned to memory before it was published' and the boot stops at stage 10's next pin; with the clean before an attach's invalidation dropped, both attaches are refused and the boot panics naming the VT-d changes refused for a table write not cleaned to memory. Host tests: every entry the mapper writes, on a map and on an unmap, is cleaned after it is written; a walker that snoops cleans nothing; a write noted and not cleaned reads as unpublished, and a full record cleans early."

"On a VT-d unit whose ECAP.C is clear, every table frame the kernel zeroes for the unit to walk -- the root table, a context table, a domain's second-level root and each second-level table the mapper adds -- shall be cleaned to memory whole before any entry that links it is written."

"On x86-64 under KVM and TCG the iommu line counts the fresh tables cleaned, more than 0. Host tests: each table the mapper adds below the root is cleaned whole before the entry that links it is written."

"An SMMUv3 whose IDR0.COHACC is clear shall be left alone, with the reason printed. One that is brought up shall have CR1 set, while its queues and translation are off, to write-back cacheable, inner shareable accesses to its stream table and queues, read back as written, and each stream table entry's stage-2 walk shall be write-back cacheable and inner shareable."

"On AArch64 the SMMUv3 is brought up and the out-of-domain write is faulted through it; with COHACC's test inverted, the unit is left alone as not snooping and test-boot fails on no write outside a translated domain faulted."

children.name: InterruptRemapping
children.doc: src/kernel/src/iommu/remapping.rs and the interrupt-remapping half of iommu/vtd.rs: NVIDIA's N0g, docs/NVIDIA.md section 12.3, which closes F-57.

children.value: "A VT-d unit shall remap interrupts only where the DMAR says INTR_REMAP and the unit's ECAP.IR is set. Such a unit shall be given one zeroed interrupt remapping table of 256 entries, cleaned whole before it is linked, pointed at by IRTA in xAPIC format (EIME 0) and taken with SIRTP, every cached entry invalidated, before IRE. IRE shall be set without CFI and GSTS read back: a unit whose CFIS reads set shall have IRE cleared again and count as not blocking compatibility format, and a unit that remaps with CFIS clear shall say so on its line."

"On x86-64 under KVM (split irqchip) and TCG, on the patched QEMU whose CFIS follows CFI, the unit's line says remapping on (256 entries, xAPIC format), CFIS=0 read back, and test-boot requires it and fails on 'remapping not enabled'; with CFI set in the IRE write the unit reads CFIS set, turns remapping off and test-boot fails. Host test: IRTA holds the table with EIME 0 and 256 entries."

"An interrupt remapping table entry shall be written only while it is not present: its high quadword, the source ID it checks, first, then its low quadword with P last, both cleaned to memory on a unit that does not snoop, then the entry invalidated index by index in the interrupt entry cache and waited for, before the message or I/O APIC entry that names it is programmed. A present entry shall never be rewritten, and an index whose invalidation failed shall not be used."

"On x86-64 under KVM and TCG the console's present entry is offered a rewrite on every unit that remaps and each refuses it, the console's next delivery still coming through it (the remap line); with the refusal of a present entry dropped, the boot panics with 'a present interrupt entry was rewritten'. The invalidation's order is argued from the code: remap's last statement is the invalidation and its wait, and QEMU does not cache entries, so a check of a skipped invalidation would prove nothing (the consultant's acceptance, 2026-10-02)."

"Every interrupt remapping entry the kernel writes shall be present, record its faults (FPD 0), name one physical destination (DM 0, RH 0) in fixed delivery mode, remap and never post (IM 0), carry the vector minted and the trigger of its source -- edge for a message, the input's for an I/O APIC line -- and check the requester's whole source ID (SQ 00, SVT 01)."
"Host test: an entry carries exactly those fields and none of QEMU's reserved bits; with SVT 0 in the builder, check R3's message naming another function's entry is delivered and the boot panics."

"A VT-d fault record whose reason is 0x20 to 0x26 shall be read as an interrupt fault, with its reason and the entry index it named and no page, recorded in the audit as INTERRUPT_FAULT, and counted stray unless a check registered its stream and reason before provoking it."

"On x86-64 under KVM and TCG checks R1 and R2 read fault 0x25 and R3 fault 0x26 from edu's source ID, each registered, and the end-of-boot audit counts no stray fault; test-boot requires exactly those three reasons provoked and fails on any other. Host test: a fault record's reason tells an interrupt request from DMA, and its index is FI's bits 63:48."

"The machine's interrupts shall count as isolated exactly when every unit its DMAR lists, refused ones included, remaps with CFIS read clear, and stage 10's discovery placed no PCI function behind no unit; a device's, when the machine's are and the unit it is placed behind as its own requester remaps. Before discovery they are not isolated."

"Host test: the rule over a list of units, one refused, one with CFIS set, and a function bypassing, each clears it. On x86-64 check R10 reads device_isolation 0x3 for edu, and bit 1 clear while the check forces the machine's interrupts not isolated."

children.name: MemoryManagement
children.doc: src/kernel/src/mm.rs: the frame allocator's interface, the kernel heap's page supply and allocator, the kernel's and other trees' page tables, and frame zeroing and copying. The buddy allocator and the heap themselves are src/lib/kernel/frame and src/lib/kernel/heap, whose host tests prove them; nothing here restates them. The frame windows at the end of the file serve the checks only (mm-draft-A-notes.md).

children.value: "init shall give the frame allocator every frame firmware reported usable below the direct map's limit, except frame 0 and the pages the per-frame array occupies, and shall refuse a memory map with no usable RAM, or with no usable region inside the direct map that holds the array, before it hands anything over."

"For memory maps built for the purpose, the frames the allocator manages equal the usable frames below the direct map's limit less frame 0 and the array's pages, 0 more and 0 fewer; a map with no usable region is refused NoUsableMemory and one whose usable regions are all smaller than the array NoRoomForPageArray."
"init shall leave frame 0 out of the frames it gives the allocator, on every architecture, so that physical address 0 is never handed out (FX-0601)."
"After memory bring-up the allocator records frame 0 as Reserved or holds no record of it, and a request for a frame lying below frame 1 is refused."
"allocate_frames shall not hand out a frame a live allocation holds, and shall align a block of 2^order frames to 2^order frames."
"Two single frames taken in turn are different frames, and a block of order 4 starts on a multiple of 16 frames."
"deallocate_frames shall return every block allocate_frames handed out to the free frames, whatever order blocks of different sizes are given back in."
"16 rounds of up to 256 blocks of orders 0 to 4, each round giving back every other block first and then the rest, leave the free frame count exactly where it started."
"allocate_frame_run shall hand out blocks of 2^MAX_ORDER frames lying back to back, each an allocated block that can be given back on its own."

"A run of 2 blocks has both block heads allocated and each is given back alone with deallocate_frames; the frame count user/check.rs's run takes around the stage 6 checks comes back to where it started."
"split_frames shall turn an allocated block into single allocated frames, each of which release_frame gives back on its own."
"A block of 2 frames split with split_frames leaves both frames allocated, and release_frame of each answers that it went back to the allocator, 2 of 2."
"share_frame shall count another reference to a frame, and release_frame shall return the frame to the allocator only when it drops the last reference, answering whether it did."

"A page committed to a VMO and shared once reads 2 references; with the VMO dropped it reads 1 and the held frame count is one below its start; release_frame of the last reference answers true and the count is back where it started."
"allocate_user_frame shall charge the frame to the running task's job, refusing the frame when the charge is refused, and the frame's release shall take the charge back from that job."
"Faults made as a task of a job limited to 48 pages are refused at exactly its limit while a sibling job faults 48 pages in, and with both spaces dropped every job's memory reads 0."
"A page table map_in makes for a user mapping shall be charged to the running task's job, refused with the mapping when the charge is refused, and the charge taken back when the table is freed."

"A user mapping made as a task of a job, needing N new page tables, raises the job's memory by N pages beyond its frames; at a limit one page short of them it is refused, 0 tables left made; with the tree torn down the job's memory reads 0."
"disown_frame shall take a held frame's charge off the job it was charged to and leave the frame allocated and charged to nobody."
"A frame allocated as a task of a job and then disowned leaves the job's memory where it was before the allocation, the frame still allocated; its release afterwards changes no job's memory."
"allocate_frames_below shall hand out a block lying wholly below the frame limit it is given, or none."
"Every block of orders 0 to 2 taken below a limit of 256 frames ends at or below frame 256, until a request is refused; all of them given back, the free count is unchanged."
"The kernel heap shall hand each allocation a block that holds what is written to it until it is freed, through growth and reallocation."

"A Box holds the value put in it; a Vec pushed to 4096 values through its reallocations holds each value at its index; a BTreeMap given 2048 inserts returns every value it holds under the key it was inserted with; and the heap has taken at least one page."
"The kernel heap shall count every freed block as free and give the slab pages it no longer needs back to the frame allocator, keeping at most one per size class."

"Around the heap check -- a Box, a Vec grown to 4096 values and a BTreeMap of 2048 inserts, all dropped -- the heap's live bytes come back to what they were, and its pages grow by no more than ferrix_heap::CLASSES."
"KernelAllocator::alloc shall answer an allocation that neither the heap nor an open section's reserve can serve with a null pointer, and count it as a refusal."
"With the heap unable to take a page and no section open, a fallible allocation is refused AllocError and heap_refusals rises by exactly 1; the heap's live bytes are unchanged."
"A page table the kernel's mapper is given, for the kernel's own tables or another tree's, shall hold only zeros."
"A frame filled with a pattern and given back is claimed again as a new table by a mapping; all 512 of its descriptors other than the one the mapping wrote read 0."
"zero_frame shall write zero to every byte of the frame it is given."
"A frame filled with a non-zero pattern and passed to zero_frame reads 0 in 4096 of its 4096 bytes."
"copy_frame shall make every byte of the destination frame equal to the same byte of the source."
"A frame filled with a pattern that differs at every word, copied to a frame filled with another, reads the first pattern in 4096 of its 4096 bytes, and the source is unchanged."
"map_demand_page shall resolve a kernel fault in the on-demand window by mapping one fresh frame at the faulting page, so that the access completes when it is retried."

"Writes to 3 unmapped pages of the window, out of order, each fault once, read back what was written and leave a mapping, consuming between 3 and 6 frames; a fourth into a region whose tables exist costs exactly 1 frame."
"translate_in shall answer, for an address in a tree, the physical address the processor reaches through that address while the tree is installed."

"In each of the 2 rounds check_the_processor_walks_an_installed_space runs, a value written through each of a two-page space's user addresses, the space installed, is read back through it and at the frame translate_in names for it through the direct map, 2 of 2 pages."
"map_in shall map len bytes, rounded up to whole pages, at virt onto phys in the tree rooted at root, with the permissions asked for, and nothing else."
"A mapping of 3 pages made with map_in into an empty tree translates each page to phys plus its offset with the flags asked for, and the pages before and after it do not translate."
"Before it maps a range user-executable, map_in shall make what was written to its frames through the direct map what every processor fetches from them."

"On each architecture and on a multi-core Arm board, code written into a frame through the direct map, then mapped user-executable with map_in and run by a program on another processor, returns the value the new code computes, N of N runs."
"share_kernel_slots shall make the given top level slots of a tree point where the kernel root's do."
"On x86-64, every upper-half slot of a new address space's root equals the kernel root's, and a kernel address translates through the new root to what it does through the kernel's."
"unmap_in shall take a mapping down from a live tree and put every page table the removal empties on the shootdown's list, giving none of them back itself (finding F-36)."

"An unmap_in of the one page mapped in a fresh tree's user half leaves the page untranslated, lists at least one emptied table, counts 0 user tables given back, and leaves every listed table allocated: claim_frame refuses each."
"unmap_unwalked shall take a mapping down from a tree no processor can walk and give every page table the removal empties back to the frame allocator before it returns."

"A 3-page mapping made in a fresh tree and taken down with unmap_unwalked leaves nothing translating, raises the user tables given back by the tables the mapping made, and the free frame count returns to what it was before the mapping."
"prune_in shall give back every page table in the range of a tree that maps nothing, and no table that maps something."

"In a tree where a map_in failed part way, leaving tables above the page it could not map, prune_in over the range gives back exactly those tables, and a page mapped elsewhere in the tree still translates."
"map_io shall map one 4 KiB page at an I/O address in an IOMMU tree, with no block mapping, so that translate_io walking the tree as the unit does finds that page there."
"Two frames mapped into a translated domain are each found by translate_io at their own I/O address, and every leaf of the domain's tree is 4 KiB."
"unmap_io shall take the page down and put every page table the removal empties on the caller's list, giving none of them back itself."
"An unmap_io of the one page mapped in a domain's tree leaves it untranslated by translate_io, lists at least one emptied table, and every listed table is still allocated until the list is released."
"When unmap_kernel returns, no online processor shall still reach the range through the mapping it removed."

"Over 20 rounds in which every online processor reads a kernel page and the page is then moved to another frame with unmap_kernel and map_kernel, every processor reads the page's new value each round: 0 reads through a stale translation."

"unmap_and_release shall hand the caller the frames a kernel unmap removed, and give back the page tables it emptied, only after the shootdown covering the removal has returned, an unmap that failed part way included."

"For an unmap of a vmap allocation, every frame passed to the release closure and every table given back is passed or given after the shootdown count has risen by one, 0 before; the same for an unmap made to fail part way."

"unmap_kernel_all shall make room for all it may release before it unmaps anything and, with no room, unmap in pieces of at most 32 pages, each shot down and released before the next, losing nothing it releases."

"An unmap of a 100-page vmap allocation with every fallible allocation failing removes all 100 pages, gives every frame and table back (0 frames kept, LOST_TO_UNMAPS 0) and takes at least 4 shootdowns."
"protect_kernel shall change what an existing kernel mapping permits in the page tables themselves, leaving it mapped."
"A fresh vmap page's leaf reads writable; protected KERNEL_RODATA it reads not writable and still translates; and protecting it KERNEL_DATA again is accepted."
"Once bring-up has dropped the loader's identity map, no leaf under the kernel's root, nor under the identity map's own root where the architecture has one, shall be both writable and executable."
"The sweep of every leaf under those roots, after the identity map is dropped, counts N leaves, E > 0 of them executable, and 0 both writable and executable (the w^x line)."
"No leaf under the kernel's root that maps a frame of the image's text or read-only data shall be writable, and the direct map shall alias every byte of them read-only."

"The sweep of every leaf under the kernel's root finds the image's text and read-only data non-empty, 0 of the leaves mapping them writable, and the direct map's leaves over them covering every byte (the sealed line)."

"reclaim_boot_memory shall give the frame allocator the loader's and the ACPI-reclaimable frames the per-frame array covers, above frame 0, and none of the page tables, boot stack or boot information the kernel still uses."

"The frames reclaimed equal the loader and ACPI-reclaim frames of the memory map inside the array, above frame 0, and greater than 0; afterwards no frame of a PageTables, BootStack or BootInfo region is free."

children.name: AllocationReserve
children.doc: src/kernel/src/mm/reserve.rs: each processor's allocation reserve, which lets an Arc or a map insert that has started finish (finding F-23).

children.value: "Inside a reserved section, an allocation the heap does not serve shall be served from the processor's reserve, a block of its size class or the large block held for it, so that the section's operation completes."

"With every allocation inside a section sent to the reserve without asking the heap, an Arc of 64 bytes, an Arc of 3000 bytes (past the largest size class) and 200 map inserts each complete and hold what was put in them, and the reserve is drawn on at least 4 times."

"reserve and fill_reserve shall refuse with AllocError, count the refusal and leave interrupts as they found them, when the heap cannot fill the processor's reserve or hold the large block asked for."

"With the heap unable to take a page and the reserve drawn below its depth, reserve is refused AllocError, the refused count rises by 1, and interrupts are enabled after as before; the same for a large block the heap cannot supply."
"draw shall serve an allocation from a reserve only while a section is open on that processor."
"With the heap unable to take a page, an allocation made outside any section is refused and the drawn count is unchanged, while the same allocation inside a section is served."
"When the outermost section on a processor closes, leave shall give a large block that section did not use back to the heap."
"A section entered for a large Arc and closed without making it leaves the heap's large pages and the free frame count where they were before the section."

children.name: UnlinkedTables
children.doc: src/kernel/src/mm/unlinked.rs: page tables an unmap has unlinked from a live tree, held from the allocator until the shootdown or the unit's invalidation that covers them (finding F-36).

children.value: "UnlinkedTables::release, called once the shootdown covering the unmap has returned, shall give every table on the list back to the frame allocator, counting a user tree's as user tables."
"The shootdown for an unmap_in that emptied tables leaves the list empty, and the user tables given back rise by exactly the number it held."
"take_from shall move every table of one list onto another, so that shootdowns merged into one release the tables of both, and none before it."
"Two lists of 2 and 3 tables merged with take_from leave the first empty and the second holding 5, all 5 still allocated; releasing the second gives back 5."
"A list dropped while it still holds tables shall keep them from the frame allocator for good and count them."
"A list holding 1 table, dropped unreleased, raises tables_kept by 1 and the table stays allocated: claim_frame refuses it."

children.name: KernelArena
children.doc: src/kernel/src/vmap.rs: the kernel's dynamic address space -- anonymous allocations, device windows, buffers and guard-paged kernel stacks. check_failed_device_map and check_invariants are check code in this product file (mm-draft-A-notes.md).

children.value: "vmap::allocate shall hand out address ranges inside the arena, no two of them sharing an address or a guard page."
"Two live 8-page allocations have different bases, lie inside ARENA_BASE..ARENA_END, and the higher begins at least two pages past the end of the lower."
"vmap::allocate shall leave the page directly below and the page directly above every allocation unmapped."
"The page below an 8-page allocation and the page at its end do not translate."
"vmap::allocate shall back each page of an allocation with a writable frame of its own."
"Each of the 8 pages of a fresh allocation translates, and a different value written to the first word of each is read back from every page after all 8 are written."
"vmap::allocate shall zero every byte of each page before mapping it."
"An 8-page allocation made after 8 frames were filled with a pattern and given back reads 0 in every byte of every page, 32768 of 32768."
"vmap::free shall unmap an allocation and give all its frames back, and shall refuse an address it has already taken back."
"Two 8-page allocations are freed; a second free of the first is refused; its base no longer translates; and the free frame count is back where it stood after a warm-up pair had been made and freed."
"vmap::allocate shall refuse an allocation of zero pages as a bad length."
"An allocation of 0 pages is refused BadLength(0)."
"vmap::allocate, allocate_stack and free_stacks shall answer an allocation refused part way as running out of memory, undoing what was done, and keep no frame of it."

"With each allocation that making three kernel stacks and freeing them -- one alone, then two in one call -- makes failed in turn, frames included, every run ends in success or as running out of memory, and the frame window alloc_check's run opens around the runs keeps 0 frames."

"map_device shall map a device window as device memory, not executable, at an address with the same offset in its page as the physical address asked for, and unmap_device shall take it down without giving the aperture's frames to the allocator."

"A window of 0x100 bytes at offset 0x40 into a frame starts at offset 0x40 in its page, translates to the address asked for and is mapped device and not executable; unmapped, it no longer translates and the free frame count is unchanged."
"map_device shall refuse, before it reserves or maps anything, a range that touches any byte of the kernel image."

"Windows asked for over the image's first 0x100 bytes, a two-page range from the page below it into it, its last byte and a page at its middle are each refused KernelImage naming the address asked for, 4 of 4, and the arena holds as many allocations as before."
"map_device shall refuse as a bad length, before it reserves anything, a range whose end rounded out to a page is past the top of the address space."

"Four ranges that wrap -- the offset plus the length, the rounding of that, the top page with a page's length, and 0x100 bytes at 0x40 into the top page -- are each refused BadLength naming the length asked for, 4 of 4, and the arena holds as many allocations as before."
"A device window whose mapping fails part way shall leave none of its own pages mapped and remove no mapping it did not make."
"A two-page window whose second page is already mapped is refused, its first page does not translate afterwards, and the mapping in its way still translates to where it did."
"The arena's regions shall stay sorted and non-overlapping, and every live allocation's span shall stay reserved in it, through every reserve, claim and release."
"After the stage 2 arena checks' allocations, windows and frees, the arena's regions are sorted and do not overlap, and each live allocation's span is found in it, 0 exceptions."
"device_windows shall list the physical range of every live device window and nothing an anonymous allocation holds."

"With one device window over a known frame and one anonymous allocation live, device_windows lists the window's range and no range of the anonymous allocation's frames; with the window gone, it no longer lists it."

"allocate_stack shall make a kernel stack of STACK_PAGES pages, its top 16-byte aligned and every byte of it writable, with an unmapped page directly below and above it, and free_stack shall give all its frames back."

"A stack from allocate_stack is 4 pages long with its top 16-byte aligned; a value written at its first word and at its last is read back; the page below its base and the page at its top do not translate; and free_stack returns the free frame count to where it was."
"free_stacks shall take every stack it is given out of use, unmap all of them under one shootdown, and make their addresses available again only after it."
"Freeing 8 stacks with free_stacks takes exactly 1 shootdown, gives back every frame, and none of the 8 addresses is handed out again before the shootdown has returned."
"Buffer::zeroed shall make a buffer of len zeroed bytes on pages that need not be contiguous, none for a length of zero, and the buffer's drop shall free them."

"A buffer of 5 MiB, more than the heap's largest block, reads 0 in every byte and holds what is written; a buffer of 0 bytes takes no allocation; with both dropped the arena's allocations and the free frame count are where they were."

children.name: EarlyMemory
children.doc: src/kernel/src/early.rs: physical memory and page tables before there is a frame allocator -- the loader's tables extended from a pool of sixteen frames in .bss. read_physical_byte and translate serve only stage 1's checks, which are in main.rs (mm-draft-A-notes.md).

children.value: "map_device and map_framebuffer shall install in the loader's tables a window that translates each page to the physical address asked for, with device or framebuffer attributes."

"The framebuffer window, where firmware left one outside reclaimable memory, translates to the framebuffer's physical address; a device window translates to the registers asked for and is mapped device and not executable."
"map_window shall refuse, before it maps anything, a range that touches any byte of the kernel image."

"Early device windows asked for over the image's first page, a range straddling its start, its last byte and a range straddling its end are each refused KernelImage naming the address asked for, 4 of 4, and the window address still does not translate."
"map_window shall refuse with RangeOverflow, before it judges the range against the image or maps anything, a range whose end rounded out to a page is past the top of the address space."
"The top page with a page's length and a page with a length of 2^64 - 1 are each refused MapFailed(RangeOverflow), 2 of 2, and the window address still does not translate."
"EarlyMemory::allocate_table shall hand out each of its 16 pool frames at most once and then refuse, which a mapping reports as running out of memory."
"An EarlyMemory asked for 17 tables answers 16 distinct page-aligned frames inside the pool and then none; a mapping that needs a table after that is refused MapFailed(OutOfMemory)."

"direct_map_ram shall answer a direct-map address only for a physical address inside a run of RAM that record_ram recorded from the memory map, clipped to the direct map's span, and record_ram shall record those runs whole, in whole pages, ascending and apart, or refuse to bring memory up."

"At least one run is recorded, each whole pages, ascending and apart; a frame the allocator hands out is answered with the direct_map address; the page past the highest run, a page between two runs where the memory map has one, and a device's aperture are each answered None (the stage 2 memory check and the `copies` line)."

"A library crate's map insert through ferrix_fallible shall run in a reserved section the kernel installs at boot: completed from the reserve when the heap refuses, refused before it starts when the reserve cannot be filled, and refused when its nodes are larger than any size class."

"With every allocation inside a section sent to the reserve, 200 inserts through ferrix_fallible::try_map_insert complete, hold what was inserted and draw on the reserve at least twice; with the checking processor's fills refused, an insert is refused, the refused count rises and the map is unchanged; a map of 256-byte values is refused."
"refuse_reserve_fills shall make every section entered on the calling processor refused, as if its reserve could not be filled, until it is turned off."
"With fills refused, a library map insert on the checking processor is refused and the refused count rises; turned off again, the next insert completes."

children.name: VirtualMemoryObjects
children.doc: src/kernel/src/user/vmo.rs: the pageable memory object -- a sparse list of frames committed on first touch, shared by a fork until a write copies, held in place for a device, moved by mremap, cut by a file's truncation -- and the three phases a page leaves it by: out of the list, forgotten by every space that maps it and shot down, and only then released.

children.value: "Vmo::new_anonymous shall make an object of the pages asked for with no page committed and no frame taken."
"A fresh object of 1024 pages has 0 pages committed, the free-frame count is what it was before it was made, and its size reads 1024 pages and 1024 x 4096 bytes."
"Vmo::commit shall give a page its first frame filled with zeros."
"Page 2 of a fresh 4-page object, committed, reads 0 in each of its 4096 bytes through the direct map."
"Vmo::write_page to a page that holds no frame shall commit a zeroed frame before it writes, so that the bytes of the page it does not write read as 0."
"A frame filled with a pattern and freed is taken by a write of 8 bytes at offset 100 of an uncommitted page; the other 4088 bytes of the page read 0."
"Vmo::commit of a page that holds a frame shall hand back that frame and take no other."
"Page 3 committed twice gives the same frame both times, the second commit taking 0 frames; the object names that frame at page 3 and none at the untouched page 4."
"Vmo::commit shall refuse a page at or past the object's end as OutOfRange, naming the page and the object's size, and take no frame for it."
"commit of page 4 of a 4-page object is refused OutOfRange { index: 4, pages: 4 }, and the object has 0 pages committed after."
"Vmo::commit_within shall refuse a page at or past the object's end as OutOfRange, naming the page and the object's size."
"commit_within of page 1 of a 1-page object is refused OutOfRange { index: 1, pages: 1 }."
"Vmo::commit shall take one frame for each distinct page committed and no more, and dropping the object shall give every one of them back."
"Of a 2048-page object, 7 scattered pages committed out of order leave exactly 7 committed and the free-frame count 7 lower; with the object dropped the count is what it was before it was made."
"Dropping an object shall give back its own reference on each frame it holds, and so free only the frames no other holder still references."

"A committed page given a second reference: with the object dropped the frame has 1 reference and is not free (the free count 1 below where it began); with the last reference released the count is back where it began."

"Vmo::new_anonymous and Vmo::fork shall each charge one object to the running task's job for as long as the object lives, and be refused, making nothing, when the job's object limit is full; Vmo::new_filled, a file's page cache, shall charge none."

"In a job limited to 5 objects and holding 5, vmo_create is refused NO_MEMORY and a fork of an object is refused, 0 objects counted beyond the limit; with every object dropped the job holds 0; a tmpfs file made in the job adds 0 objects."
"Vmo::read_page of a page that holds no frame shall read zeros and commit nothing."
"A read of 4096 bytes of page 5 of a fresh 8-page object returns 4096 zeros, and the object has 0 pages committed and the free-frame count is unchanged after."
"Vmo::read_page and Vmo::write_page shall refuse, as OutOfRange and copying nothing, a page past the object's end or a byte range that runs past the end of its page."

"Of a 2-page object, a read and a write of page 2, and of 8 bytes at offset 4092 of page 0, and of a range whose end overflows, are each refused OutOfRange, 6 of 6, with 0 pages committed and the caller's buffer unchanged."

"Vmo::fork shall give the new object each committed page by a further reference to the same frame, and Vmo::write_page to a page another object shares shall copy it first, so that the write is not seen through the other object."

"A 1-page object written `before` and forked names the same frame as its fork; `after!` written through the original moves it to another frame, and the original reads `after!` while the fork reads `before`."

"When Vmo::write_page copies a shared page, it shall have every address space that maps the object forget the page, invalidated on every processor that may hold it, before it gives back the object's reference on the original, so that a mapping faults the copy in."

"A shared object a process maps and reads on another processor, whose page a fork of the object shares, written through Vmo::write_page: the process then reads the bytes written, not the original's, and its space translates the page to the copy."
"Vmo::replace shall put the new frame in the page, return the frame it displaced, and give back only the object's own reference on that frame."

"Replacing a page whose frame has a second holder returns that frame, the object names the new frame, and the old frame has 1 reference; with the other holder's release and the object dropped the free-frame count is back where it began, 0 frames kept."
"Vmo::replace of a page that holds no frame shall put the frame in and report nothing displaced."
"A replace of page 1 of a 2-page object with nothing committed returns nothing, and the object then names the frame given at page 1."

"Vmo::decommit_range shall take a page out of every address space that maps the object, invalidated on every processor that may hold its translation, before the page's frame goes back to the allocator."

"On two or more processors, a page of a shared object that two processes on two processors have touched (rmap_check::check's setup) is decommitted: 1 page given back, neither space translates it, the kernel claims the freed frame and poisons it, and the process on the other processor then reads 0, not the poison, and writes to a new frame, the freed one keeping its poison."

"Vmo::replace shall take the page out of every address space that maps the object, invalidated on every processor that may hold its translation, before it gives back the displaced frame, so that every mapping reaches the new frame."

"On two or more processors, a page of a shared object two processes on two processors have touched (rmap_check::check's setup) is replaced with a frame holding a pattern: the displaced frame is returned, neither space translates the page, the kernel poisons the displaced frame, and the process on the other processor reads the pattern, not the poison, and writes into the new frame, as the other process then does."

"Vmo::retire given the address space under whose lock phase one ran shall not ask that space again, shall run that space's pending shootdown together with the others', and shall release the frames only after every one has completed."

"A copy-on-write fault taken on one processor on a page the same space's thread has cached on another, finished through Vmo::take_page and Vmo::retire with its own space: the displaced frame, claimed back and poisoned once released, is never read by the other processor's thread, which reads the copy."

"Vmo::decommit_range shall give back every page of its range that is not held, taken out of every space that maps the object, even when no allocation can be made: a chunk of pages at a time from the stack, and the spaces asked one at a time."

"80 pages of a mapped 160-page object, committed through faults, decommitted with every fallible allocation failing (at least 1 failed): 80 pages given back, 0 left committed, 0 still translated, and 0 frames kept."

"Each operation of an object that allocates -- commit, fork, write_page, hold, take_page, take_range, adopt_pages, attach, take_mapped_writes and a retirement's list of the spaces to ask -- shall answer a failed allocation as running out of memory, or carry on without the memory, and keep no frame."

"In the memory sweep, with each allocation of each scenario (fork, move, shared, split, cut, object, stacks, code) failed in turn, every run ends in success or in running out of memory, the run in which nothing failed succeeds, and each scenario's frame window keeps 0 frames (the `sweep` line)."
"Vmo::hold shall commit each page of its range, copying into a frame of its own a page a fork left shared, with its contents, and report the frames in page order."

"Holding pages 1 and 2 of a 4-page object whose page 1 a fork shares reports 2 frames, the ones the object names at pages 1 and 2; page 1's is not the shared frame and has 1 reference, the fork still names the shared one, and page 1 still reads `held`."

"While a page is held, Vmo::decommit_range and Vmo::decommit_from shall skip it, Vmo::replace shall refuse it and leave the frame offered with the caller, and Vmo::write_page shall write it where it is."

"With pages 1 and 2 of a 4-page object held, decommit_range(0, 4) and decommit_from(0) each give back 0 pages and 2 stay committed; a replace of page 1 returns nothing, page 1 keeps the held frame, and the frame offered is freed by the caller's release; a write to page 1 leaves it at the held frame."
"While a page is held, Vmo::decommit_range and Vmo::replace shall leave it mapped at its frame in every address space that maps the object."

"On two or more processors, a page of a shared object two processes map (rmap_check::check's setup) is held: a write by one process reaches the held frame; decommit_range gives back 0 pages and a replace is refused, the object still naming the held frame; both spaces translate the page to the held frame before and after, and both processes read the marker written."
"Vmo::fork shall give the new object a copy of a held page, with its contents, rather than a reference to the held frame."
"A fork of an object whose page 1 is held names another frame than the held one at page 1, the held frame keeps 1 reference, and the fork's page 1 reads `held`."
"A page shall stay held until the last Held covering it is dropped, and then be an ordinary page again."

"Page 2 held by two holds and page 1 by one: with the first hold dropped, decommit_range(0, 4) gives back 1 page and page 2 keeps its frame; with the second dropped it gives back 1 page and 0 stay committed."
"Vmo::hold shall refuse a range of no pages and a range that runs past the object's end."
"Of a 4-page object, hold of 2 pages from page 3 and hold of 0 pages from page 0 are both refused."
"Holding pages, copying them for a hold or a fork, and letting the holds go shall keep no frame once the objects and their holds are dropped."
"The free-frame count taken before and after the held-page scenario (a write, a fork, two holds, a refused replace, a fork while held, decommits) is the same: 0 frames kept."
"Vmo::holds_any shall say whether any page of a range is held."
"Of a 4-page object with page 2 held, holds_any is true for pages 0 to 3 and for page 2 alone, and false for pages 0 and 1 and for page 3; with the hold dropped, false for pages 0 to 3."
"Vmo::adopt_pages shall refuse to move a range any page of which is held."
"An mremap that must move a private region, one of whose pages is held, is refused (SpaceError::OutOfMemory), 1 refusal."

"Vmo::adopt_pages shall name each committed page of the range in the new object at the same offset from the range's start, and Vmo::release_moved shall take them out of the old object, so that a private region an mremap moves reaches the pages it had."

"A two-page private mapping, written across its page boundary, grown to four pages by an mremap that must move it: at the new address its first page and the string across the boundary read as written and the old address reads nothing; shrunk to one page and moved to a fixed address, it still reads its first page as written."

"Vmo::disown_pages shall make the object the pages moved to forget every one without releasing a frame, and Vmo::adopt_pages refused for memory shall leave that object naming none, so that the object the pages came from still holds each once."

"An mremap of a written private region made to fail after its pages moved leaves the region reading what was written, each frame with the reference count it had, and 0 frames kept once the space is dropped."
"Vmo::attach shall record each address space that names the object, so that Vmo::mapper_count counts every live space that maps it."
"A shared object mapped by a process, and by the child forked from it, has a mapper count of 2 before either runs."
"Vmo::detach shall remove the one name it is given, the list shall drop spaces that have gone whenever it is taken, and it shall give back most of its room once it lists under a quarter of it."

"An object mapped 1000 times by one space under 1000 ids and 1 time by a second: with 999 ids unmapped and the second space dropped, mapper_count is 1, and the heap the list held is back within 4 entries' room of 1 mapper."
"Vmo::attach shall stop the kernel with the PRIVATE_OBJECT_SHARED report rather than give an object that backs a private region a second mapper, or a private mapper to an object already mapped."
"A negative control, attaching a second mapper to an object with a private one, ends the boot with the PRIVATE_OBJECT_SHARED report; no mapping the kernel makes in a boot does so."
"Vmo::attach shall charge the heap one name of an object holds against the running job's memory limit, record nothing when the charge is refused, and the charge shall go with the name."
"In a job with a 32 KiB limit, shared mappings of one file are refused ENOMEM before the limit is passed while a sibling job maps one; with them unmapped every byte charged has come back."
"Vmo::make_coherent shall be refused while any address space maps the object, and once none does shall mark it so that Vmo::is_coherent says so."
"A 1-page object mapped shared in a space is refused make_coherent; unmapped, make_coherent succeeds and is_coherent is true."

"Vmo::fill_for_fault shall have an object made over a file's source fill an absent page from the file before a fault commits it, the pages filled going in through Vmo::insert_absent, so that a mapping shows the file's bytes, never zeros in their place."

"Through a 64-page object over a page source mapped shared and privately (check_a_mapping_faults_in_its_source's setup), a read of page 5 through the shared mapping returns the source's byte after 1 call to the source, with 32 pages committed; a private write to page 50, which nothing had read, reads back beside the source's next byte, and the object's own page 50 still holds the source's bytes."
"Vmo::insert_absent shall put a frame in a page only if the page is inside the object and holds nothing, and otherwise, or with no memory to record it, leave the frame with the caller."

"Of a 2-page object with page 0 committed, insert_absent of page 0, of page 2 and of page 1 with every allocation failing each answers false and page 0 keeps its frame; of page 1 it answers true and the object names the frame there; every frame refused is freed by the caller's release, 0 frames kept."

"Once Vmo::set_file_len has lowered the end of the file an object holds, a fault through a shared or a private mapping of it shall commit and reach no page wholly past that end, a page a private mapping copied included."

"A tmpfs file mapped shared and privately over 4 pages, the private mapping having copied pages 0 and 1 (check_a_shared_file_mapping's earlier steps), truncated to one page: page 0 still reads through the shared mapping, and each of the other 3 pages is refused through the shared mapping and through the private one, 3 of 3 each."

"Vmo::cut_mappings shall take every mapping of the object's pages from a cut down, and give back the copies private mappings made of them once no processor can reach them, so that a file grown again shows zeros there through every mapping."
"The file of L.user.39's criterion grown back to two pages reads 4096 zero bytes at page 1 through the shared mapping and through the private mapping that had copied it."
"Vmo::decommit_from shall give back every committed page from its first page on that is not held, so that a file truncated and grown again reads zeros there, never its old bytes."
"A tmpfs file of 3 pages and 123 bytes, truncated into its second page and grown back, reads its first page and 10 bytes as written and 0 in every byte after."

"Vmo::raise_shared_may_write and Vmo::lower_shared_may_write shall count the shared mappings that may write the file an object holds, a fork child's copies included, so that Vmo::writably_mapped says whether any is left."
"F_SEAL_WRITE on a memfd is refused EBUSY while a writable shared mapping of it lives, refused EBUSY again while only a fork child's copy of that mapping does, and accepted once neither does."

"Vmo::take_mapped_writes shall report every page the object holds while a shared mapping that may write has been made since the last report or still lives, none otherwise, and on running out of memory keep the mark so that the next report names them."

"Of an object with 3 pages committed: before any writable shared mapping, a report names 0 pages; with one made and gone, the next names 3 and the one after 0; with one alive, every report names 3; a report refused for memory is followed by one naming 3."

children.name: AddressSpaces
children.doc: src/kernel/src/user/space.rs: a process's address space -- the region map and the page tables under it, the mappings of VMOs, files, devices and windows, demand faults and copy-on-write, protect, unmap, mremap and madvise, and the shootdown every takedown of a translation runs before anything it reached is given back.

children.value: "AddressSpace::new shall make a space holding no region, with its root table in a page-aligned frame."
"A fresh space holds 0 regions, and its root table's physical address is non-zero and a multiple of the page size."
"AddressSpace::new shall make a space whose map places no region below MMAP_MIN_ADDR, 64 KiB, whether asked for a fixed address or given a hint, and lets a region start at the floor itself."
"map_anonymous at address 0 is refused; an mmap hinted at 0x10 is placed at or above 64 KiB; a MAP_FIXED mmap at 64 KiB lands there."
"map_anonymous shall refuse a range outside the user half with NotUserRange and insert nothing."
"A one-page mapping at the kernel half's base is refused NotUserRange, and the space still holds 0 regions."
"map_device and map_window shall refuse a physical range that touches the kernel's image with Refused, whatever the caller holds, and insert nothing."
"A device mapping of the image's first page and a window of two pages straddling the image's start are each refused Refused, and the space holds 0 regions after both."
"map_device and map_window shall refuse a physical range that wraps the address space with BadRange, before any other test, and insert nothing."
"The top page, and a whole-pages length from a low page that runs past the top, are each refused BadRange by map_device and by map_window, 4 of 4, and the space holds 0 regions."
"map_device shall refuse a length that is not whole pages with BadRange and a range reaching past the user half with NotUserRange."
"Device mappings of no length and of half a page are refused BadRange, and one of two pages from the user half's last page is refused NotUserRange at that address: 3 refusals of 3."

"map_anywhere shall refuse a length of zero, map_object an executable mapping and a range past the user half, map_file an offset that is not whole pages, and protect a range past the user half, each with its own error."

"map_anywhere of no length is BadRange; map_object executable is Refused and past the user half NotUserRange; map_file from half a page in is BadRange; protect of two pages from the user half's last page is NotUserRange: 5 refusals of 5."
"fault shall answer an address no region covers with NotMapped, which the process receives as SIGSEGV."
"A read fault at the first address past a two-page region is answered NotMapped."
"fault shall refuse a write to a region that does not permit writing with Refused, and resolve a read of it."
"In a read-only region a write fault is answered Refused and a read fault at the same address succeeds."
"fault shall refuse a read of a region that permits nothing with Refused and install no translation for it."
"A read fault in a PROT_NONE region is answered Refused, and the page does not translate in the space's tables afterwards."

"An anonymous mapping shall commit no frame until a page is faulted, each fault shall map the faulting page and no other, an unmap shall give back the pages of its range and leave the rest mapped, and dropping the space shall give back every frame it held."

"Mapping 4 pages costs exactly 1 frame, the root; faulted out of order, each of the 4 translates and holds what is written to it; re-faulting a present page costs 0 frames; unmapping the first 2 gives back at least 2 frames, page 0 no longer translates and page 2 still does; with the space dropped the free count is what it was before, 0 frames kept."
"install shall make the running processor translate user addresses through the space's own tables, on the first installation and on every one after an uninstall."

"Over 2 rounds of install, use and uninstall, a write through each of 2 user addresses reads back through the address and through the direct map's alias of the frame the space's tables name, for both pages in both rounds; and the space dropped keeps 0 frames."
"install and uninstall, as the scheduler calls them, shall leave a task reading its own space's frame at a user address however often one processor alternates between two spaces."

"Two tasks pinned to one processor, each in a space holding a different value at one address, yield between reads: 128 reads of 128 return the reader's own value and 0 the other's (the `spaces` line), and the spaces dropped keep 0 frames."
"fork shall give the child the same object for a MAP_SHARED region, not a copy, so that the two spaces reach one frame with one holder and see each other's writes."

"After a fork of a space holding a written shared page, the child's write fault maps the parent's frame, the frame has 1 holder, a write through the child's frame reads back through the parent's, and the spaces dropped keep 0 frames."

"fork shall take the parent's translations of its private writable pages down and share their frames with the child, and a write to a page some other space still holds shall copy it into a frame of the writer's own, while a write to a page nobody else holds any more shall copy nothing."

"After a fork of 2 written private pages the parent translates neither; read faults leave both sides on the original frames with 2 holders each; the child's write, made with its space installed, lands in a new frame of 1 holder, leaves the original at 1 holder with the parent's value, and a second write copies nothing; with the parent dropped the child's write to the other page keeps its frame and contents; 0 frames kept."
"with_page shall let a write go straight through to a copy-on-write page this space alone holds, taking no translation down."
"A kernel write through with_page to a page the child has already copied succeeds and begins 0 shootdowns of the child's space."
"A private page read-only at a fork and made writable afterwards with protect shall be copied by the side that writes it, the other keeping its own."

"A page written, protected read-only, forked and protected writable in the child is copied by the child's installed write: the child's frame differs from the parent's, holds the child's value, the parent's holds its own, and 0 frames are kept."
"A write by a program's own instruction to a private page its fork still shares shall be copied for the side that wrote it and be seen by neither the other side nor the page."
"The `cow` program, whose parent and child each write a page both shared after the fork, exits 61 (the `cow` line)."
"A forked program's write to a MAP_SHARED anonymous page shall reach its parent, a page the child faults in first included, and its write to a MAP_PRIVATE page shall not."
"with_page shall hold the page it translated for as long as its copy runs, so that an unmap of the page on another processor does not return before the copy ends."

"On a machine with two processors or more, a copy holding a page in with_page on one processor for 30 ms reads the page's byte, the unmap started on the other while it held had not returned when the copy ended, and it had returned once both tasks were gone (the `unmap` line)."
"with_present_page shall refuse a write in a region that does not permit writing with Refused."
"with_present_page asked to write in a read-only region is answered Refused at that address."

"with_present_page shall run nothing and answer that the page must be faulted first when the page is absent or, for a write, a copy-on-write page another space still holds or a private file mapping's page its shadow does not hold."

"with_present_page answers Ok(None), and its closure is not run, for an absent page, a write to a page a fork still shares, and a write to a file page a private mapping has only read; after a fault each answers Some."
"map_window shall refuse an executable window with Refused, a length that is not whole pages with BadRange and a range reaching past the user half with NotUserRange."
"A window over a frame asked read-execute is Refused, of half a page BadRange, and of two pages from the user half's last page NotUserRange: 3 refusals of 3."
"A window's region shall keep what map_window was given to keep until no region names the window, and an unmap of another mapping shall let go of that mapping's file and not of the window's keeper."

"Mapped, the window holds its keeper (count 2) and is the highest mapping; a file mapping beside it unmapped leaves its open file at count 1 and the keeper at 2; the window unmapped leaves the keeper at 1."
"A page of a device region shall be faulted in to the device's own physical page, in the space that mapped it and in a fork child of it alike."
"On a machine with a whole-page aperture, io_mapping_map's address, faulted, translates to the aperture's physical address in the process's space and in a fork child's."

"io_mapping_map_combining shall map an aperture the device says is prefetchable write-combining, its pages faulted in to the device's own memory, and shall refuse an aperture of registers with INVALID_ARGS; on x86-64 it shall refuse every aperture with INVALID_ARGS unless every processor programmed its PAT with the write-combining entry."

"On x86-64, AArch64 and ARMv7-A -- each of whose test-boot machines has a virtio-pci function with a whole-page prefetchable aperture, the boot's handles line saying 1 mapped write-combining -- its write-combining mapping reaches the aperture's physical address and its page table entry reads write-combining (normal non-cacheable on the two Arm architectures), not device; a register aperture's is refused with INVALID_ARGS; on x86-64, with one processor's PAT counted as not programmed, the prefetchable aperture's is refused with INVALID_ARGS, and with that refusal dropped stage 9 fails naming it."

"A page of device memory shall be mapped into user address spaces with one memory type at a time: map_device and map_window shall refuse a range any page of which a live user mapping holds as another of device, write-combining or cached with OtherMemoryType -- ALREADY_BOUND from io_mapping_map and io_mapping_map_combining, EINVAL from mmap of a render node's blob -- and a mapping's hold shall end only once no region of any address space maps it, after its unmap's shootdown has returned. Holds shall be counted in one claim per distinct range and type, an I/O mapping's range being its whole aperture and a window's its whole blob, so that no number of mappings adds a claim."

"On x86-64, AArch64 and ARMv7-A, with a prefetchable aperture mapped write-combining, io_mapping_map of it is ALREADY_BOUND and a cached window over it is OtherMemoryType; with it mapped as a cached window, and then uncached, after the write-combining mapping is unmapped, io_mapping_map_combining is ALREADY_BOUND; with every mapping of it unmapped it maps write-combining again; mapping the cached window again, whole and one page of it, leaves the number of claims unchanged; with the type comparison dropped from memory_type::hold, stage 9 fails naming the uncached mapping made beside the write-combining one, and with every hold given a claim of its own it fails naming the claim the window's second mapping made."

"with_page and with_present_page shall refuse a copy to or from a page of a device region with Refused, before the page is faulted in or a direct-map address is formed for it, and shall form one only through direct_map_ram."

"A writev() from and a readv() into a device's aperture mapped by io_mapping_map, a cached window past all RAM and, where the memory map has a hole between runs of RAM, a window over it are each EFAULT with the page still absent, and with_present_page refuses each for reading and writing; with the aperture's page faulted in, both copies are EFAULT again (the `copies` line)."

"remap shall refuse a new length of zero with BadRange, an old range longer than its region with NotMapped and a fixed destination overlapping the old range with BadRange, and leave a remap to the same length where it is."

"On a two-page region, a remap to length 0 is BadRange, of three pages NotMapped, to a fixed address one page in BadRange -- 3 refusals of 3 -- and to the same length anywhere answers the region's own address."
"remap shall grow a region where it is when the pages after it are free, even when it may move."
"A one-page region with free pages after it, remapped to three pages anywhere, answers its own address."
"remap shall refuse with OutOfMemory to grow a shared region over offsets of its object that another region of the space already names."
"A three-page shared region whose last page was moved away on its own cannot grow its first two pages back to three in place: OutOfMemory."
"remap shall refuse with OutOfMemory to move a private region that holds a page a device holds."
"A written one-page region whose page is held, with a neighbour in the way, is refused OutOfMemory when remapped to two pages anywhere."

"remap shall refuse to grow a region in the way of a neighbour unless it may move, and shall carry a region's contents with it when it moves it, grow it with zeros and shrink it in place, leaving nothing readable where it no longer is."

"Two written pages with a neighbour after them: growing to four without MREMAP_MAYMOVE is ENOMEM; with it they move, a string in the first page and one across the page boundary read back at the new address, the old address is unreadable and the fourth page reads 0; shrunk to one page in place it keeps the first page's string and its tail is unreadable; moved to the old address with MREMAP_FIXED it lands there with the string."
"protect and remap shall refuse with Refused a region vmo_map made, whose protection and size are its handle's."
"A read-only vmo_map region is refused Refused by protect to read-write and by remap to two pages: 2 refusals of 2."

"map_object shall map the object itself, shared, so that its bytes and the mapping's are the same bytes, a fork child writes into the same object, and the mapping outlives the handle it was made with."

"A VMO mapped at the address asked shows bytes vmo_write put there; bytes written through the mapping, and through a fork child's, are read back by vmo_read or the parent; with every handle to the VMO closed the mapping still shows its bytes."
"map_shared_code shall map a two-page object as a read-only shared data page below a read-and-run shared code page, neither writable nor able to be made writable."

"Where the architecture has a vDSO, a space it is mapped into shows the code page read, execute, shared and not writable over a data page read, shared and neither, the image reads as ELF, and a write through with_page and a protect to read-write are each refused on both pages, 4 of 4."
"shared_code_at shall answer where map_shared_code put an object in the space, so that a signal's return trampoline is found at its place in the mapped vDSO."
"On an architecture whose vDSO holds only its signal return trampoline, a fresh space the vDSO is mapped into finds the trampoline at the mapped image plus the trampoline's offset (the `vdso` line)."
"shared_object_at shall name, for an address in a shared region, the object and byte offset every space mapping that object names it by."
"A parent waiting without FUTEX_PRIVATE_FLAG on a MAP_SHARED word is not woken by its fork child's private-keyed wake of the same word and is woken by the child's shared wake."
"advise with Discard or Free on private anonymous memory shall give the range's frames back at once and leave the range mapped, reading zeros, its neighbours untouched; a hint shall drop nothing."

"Of 10 written pages, MADV_DONTNEED of pages 1 to 8 gives back exactly 8 frames, lowers the resident count by 8, pages 1 to 8 read 0 and pages 0 and 9 their pattern; MADV_FREE the same; 12 hints over all 10 pages each answer 0 and every page keeps its pattern."
"advise dropping a page a fork left shared shall take only this space's reference, so the other space keeps the page's contents."
"After a fork, the parent's MADV_DONTNEED of a written page leaves the parent reading 0 there and the child reading the page's pattern."

"advise shall drop a private file mapping's copies and show the file there again, drop only a shared file mapping's translations, take no page out of the file, and refuse Free and Remove on a file mapping as Linux does."

"Two copied pages of a private memfd mapping, dropped, give back exactly 2 frames and show the file's bytes; a shared mapping dropped still shows what it wrote, as the file does; MADV_FREE is EINVAL on both, MADV_REMOVE EACCES on the private and EOPNOTSUPP on the shared; the file's committed count is unchanged."

"advise with Remove on shared anonymous memory shall take the range's pages out of the object, so every space that maps it reads zeros there and the frames go back, and Discard there shall keep the contents."
