"Of 4 written shared pages seen by a fork child, MADV_REMOVE of pages 1 and 2 gives back exactly 2 frames, both spaces read 0 there and the pattern at pages 0 and 3; MADV_DONTNEED of page 0 keeps its pattern; MADV_FREE there is EINVAL."
"advise shall advise every mapped part of a range and then answer Unmapped for a part no region maps, and shall refuse Remove on private anonymous memory as Invalid."

"MADV_REMOVE on private anonymous memory is EINVAL; madvise of 0 bytes answers 0; over two pages whose second is unmapped MADV_DONTNEED is ENOMEM and the first page reads 0 after, and MADV_WILLNEED is ENOMEM."
"advise shall refuse as Invalid any advice that drops pages on a device region, and Discard without locked_too, Free and Remove on an mlocked region, dropping nothing there."

"MADV_DONTNEED, MADV_FREE and MADV_REMOVE on an mlocked region and MADV_DONTNEED on an I/O mapping are each EINVAL, 4 of 4, with 0 frames given back and the pages' contents kept; MADV_DONTNEED_LOCKED on the mlocked region drops it."
"advise that has no memory to note what it would take shall answer NoMemory before taking the region's pages or translations, the parts before it already advised."
"With each allocation of an MADV_DONTNEED over three regions failed in turn, each run answers 0 or EAGAIN, the pages of the refused region and after it keep their contents, and 0 frames are kept."
"protect shall take the range's translations out of the tables, so the next access is judged by the new permissions, and keep the pages' contents."
"After mprotect of a written page to read-only the page does not translate, a copy into it is refused, and a copy out of it reads what was written."
"protect shall invalidate the old translation on the processor that made the call, so the program's next write to a page it made read-only faults."
"The `mprotect` program, pinned to another processor where there is one, writes a page, makes it read-only and writes again, and is ended by SIGSEGV (status 139), not exit 1."
"protect shall reach every processor that may hold the space's translations, so that a thread on another processor cannot write through the writable entry it cached before."

"On a machine with two processors or more, a child that wrote a shared page and holds still on its processor has the page protected read-only from this one: the page no longer translates, and the child's next write ends it with SIGSEGV, 11, instead of answering (the `rmap` line)."
"protect shall refuse with Refused to make writable a range reaching a shared file mapping that may not write its file, before changing anything."
"mprotect to read-write of a shared read-only mapping of a file opened read-only answers EACCES."

"forget_runs shall take down every translation the space has of the object's named pages and answer the processors that may still cache one, so that the object's shootdown reaches them before the frame goes back."

"On a machine with two processors or more, with a shared page touched by a parent and its fork child on two processors, decommitting it leaves it translated in neither space; the given-up frame, claimed and poisoned, is not what the child then reads (it reads 0) or writes (the poison stays whole), and the page comes back in another frame."

"forget_runs shall ask for the whole TLB of the space's processors to be flushed, and answer them, whenever a shootdown of the space has begun and not returned, even when it found no translation to take down."

"A decommit of a page whose translation a concurrent unmap has taken out of the tables, but whose shootdown has not returned, is answered with the space's processors and a whole-TLB flush, and the frame is claimed back only after that flush."

"A page of a file mapping wholly past the file's end shall be refused, shared or private, and a truncation shall take a private mapping's copies past the cut, so the file grown back shows zeros there."

"A file of 2 pages and 100 bytes, mapped 4 pages shared and 4 private and cut to 1 page: page 0 still reads, pages 1 to 3 are refused in each mapping, 3 of 3 and 3 of 3; grown back to 2 pages, page 1 reads 0 in both."
"A shared file mapping shall show the file's own pages, so that a write through it is what the file reads back and a write to the file is what it shows."

"A shared mapping of a file of 2 pages and 100 bytes shows those bytes and zeros to the end of the third page; bytes written through it are what the file reads back, and bytes written to the file are what it shows."

"A private file mapping shall show the file until it writes a page and then keep that page to itself, so that neither its writes nor a read into it reach the file or a shared mapping, while the file's writes still show through pages it has not copied."

"The private mapping shows the file's first page; a write through it and a read() into it each show in it and in neither the file nor the shared mapping; a write to the file shows through a page it never copied and not through one it did."
"fork shall give the child the private file mapping's copies, and the child's write into one shall reach neither the parent nor the file."
"A fork child reads the parent's private copy; its write into a page the parent copied before the fork is seen by neither the parent nor the file."
"A program's write to a private file mapping's page it has only read shall copy the page and go through, not fault on the file's read-only page forever, and shall not reach the file."

"A program reads a private file page then writes it, and answers within 10 s with the file's word before and its marker after; forked and the child dropped, its next write answers too; the file's first word is unchanged."
"map_file shall place a fixed private mapping exactly where asked, showing the file, an executable one not writable, and a writable one made read-only by protect keeping what was written."

"A fixed read-execute file mapping lands at its address, shows the file's first page and refuses a write; a fixed read-write one lands next to it, takes a write, and after mprotect to read-only keeps it and refuses the next write."
"with_regions shall show each region with its permissions, share mode and file, so that /proc/<pid>/maps names a shared writable file mapping by its file."
"/proc/<pid>/maps of the check's process has a line marked rw-s that ends in the mapped file's path."

"fault shall be refused when the frame or page table it needs would pass the running task's job's memory limit, without holding back a sibling job, and a space's drop shall give every frame and table it was charged for back."

"Faulting a space in page by page as a task of a job limited to 48 pages' worth stops short of 48 pages, the refusal counted and the job's memory within one page of its limit; a sibling faults all 48 in; with both spaces dropped every level's memory and kernel memory read 0 (the `quota` line)."
"Every address space operation that allocates -- fork, the maps, fault, remap and unmap -- shall answer a refused allocation with OutOfMemory or absorb it, and keep no frame."

"With the n-th allocation failed alone for every n until a run in which none was, each run of the fork, move, shared, split, cut, object, stacks, code and page scenarios ends in success or out of memory, never another refusal, the run with nothing failed succeeds, and each scenario's frame window keeps 0 frames (the `sweep` line)."
"The address space operations stage 6 checks shall give back every frame they took and every page table their takedowns emptied, none left on a shootdown list dropped unreleased."
"After stage 6's object and address space checks 0 page tables are counted kept (mm::tables_kept), and the held frame count is what it was before them, 0 frames leaked (the `objects` line)."
"set_ceiling shall move the top of the window every mapping may reach, refusing an end past the user half or below a region still mapped and changing nothing then."

"With the ceiling set to 4 GiB less a page, an anywhere mapping lands below it and a fixed one reaching past it is refused; setting it past the user half, or below a mapped region, is refused BadRange and ceiling() reads as before."
"fault shall have a file's object read a page of a file on a disk before mapping it, and answer a page the filesystem could not read with Unreadable and one it had no memory for with OutOfMemory."
"A shared and a private mapping of a file on a disk show its bytes, not zeros, on their first touch; a page whose read fails ends the program with SIGBUS."
"fault shall stop a debug kernel, naming the outermost lock's site, when it is asked to resolve a fault while a lock that disables preemption is held."
"In a debug build, a fault asked for while a spin lock is held stops the kernel with the assertion's message and that lock's file and line."
"unmap shall give back no page of its range, and no page table it emptied, before the shootdown covering them has returned from every processor in the space's set."

"On a machine with two processors or more, a page a program on another processor keeps reading is unmapped from this one; its frame, claimed back and poisoned the moment it is free, is never what the program reads: 0 poisoned reads, and the program faults."
"map_code_page shall map a one-page object as a single read-and-run shared page, never writable, and refuse an object of any other size before changing the space."

"A two-page object is refused with BadRange and the space keeps its regions; a one-page object maps as one region read, execute and shared and not writable, one page long, and unmapping it leaves the space's regions as they were (the sweep's page scenario, the `sweep` line)."

children.name: Descriptors
children.doc: src/kernel/src/arch/x86_64/gdt.rs: each processor's descriptor tables, its task state, and which selectors ring 3 may hold.

children.value: "loadable shall answer a selector, with RPL forced to 3, when it names 32-bit user code, user data, or a thread-local slot whose descriptor ring_3_segment accepts -- present, code or data, DPL 3, no L bit, and data or readable non-conforming code -- and the null selector for every other, one with the LDT bit included."

"7 selectors -- user data and a thread-local data slot at RPL 3 and at RPL 0, 32-bit user code, and null at RPL 0 and 3 -- load at RPL 3 or as null; 18 others -- kernel code and data, 64-bit user code, the TSS, slots 1, 10 and 15, an LDT selector, 0xFFFF, and a thread-local slot holding nothing, DPL-0 data, a call gate, a TSS, an L-bit segment, an absent segment, unreadable code or conforming code -- load as null (the `gdt` line)."

"load, for init and init_secondary, shall put a flat 4 GiB ring-3 32-bit code segment at selector 0x23 and ring-3 data at 0x2b in the processor's GDT, so that a program runs in compatibility mode there."
"An i386 program entered at 0x23 with its stack at 0x2b writes a line through int $0x80 and exits 42 (the first `i386` line)."

"init and init_secondary shall load on each processor its own TSS, through the descriptor tss_descriptor encodes, whose interrupt stack table names that processor's own double-fault, NMI, debug and machine-check stacks with the occupancy word at each zero, and whose RSP0 is nonzero."

"On every processor, the TSS the task register names has that processor's table as its base and limit 103; its four IST entries lie in four stacks no other processor's TSS names, each occupancy word 0; RSP0 is nonzero."
"load shall set every TSS's I/O permission bitmap offset past its end, so that ring 3 may touch no port."
"A program executing inb and outb on a port is ended by SIGSEGV, 2 of 2."
"init_secondary shall report a failed interrupt-stack or table allocation, and secondary_start shall end the boot in the catalogued SECONDARY_GDT report."
"A secondary start whose stack allocation fails ends in the SECONDARY_GDT report, and no FERRIX-BOOT-OK."
"restore_user_state shall point this processor's TSS RSP0, found through STR and SGDT by set_privilege_stack, and its SYSCALL entry stack at the incoming task's kernel-stack top."
"After each of N switches between two user tasks on one processor, RSP0 and the per-processor entry stack read back equal to the running task's kernel-stack top: 0 mismatches."

children.name: UserState
children.doc: src/kernel/src/arch/x86_64/switch.rs, with gdt.rs's thread-local slots: the context switch, and the user-mode state a trap does not save.

children.value: "set_thread_area shall write a descriptor into the calling thread's slot of this processor's live GDT, and thread_area shall read the slot back, each with interrupts masked."

"An i386 program's set_thread_area with entry -1 is given 12, then 13, then 14; %gs loaded with 0x63 reads its own word; get_thread_area(12) answers its base; lar on 0x73 from ring 3 finds DPL 3 and no L bit; the program exits 42 (the thread-local `i386` line)."
"save_user_state shall save the outgoing thread's thread-local slots and data selectors, and restore_user_state shall write the incoming thread's slots and reload its selectors through loadable."

"Two i386 programs pinned to one processor, both with entry 12 and %gs 0x63 but bases 4 bytes apart, each read their own word through %gs 200 times with a sched_yield between reads: neither exits 46, both exit 42."
"save_user_state shall save FS_BASE and the program's GS base, and restore_user_state shall restore each where the thread's FS or GS selector is null."
"Two 64-bit programs pinned to one processor, each with its own ARCH_SET_FS and ARCH_SET_GS base, read their own words through %fs and %gs N times across sched_yield: 0 foreign reads."

"save_user_state shall save the outgoing task's x87 and SSE state, and its AVX state where enable_extended_state enabled it, with XSAVE64 of the enabled components, or FXSAVE64 without XSAVE; restore_user_state shall restore the incoming task's with XRSTOR64, or FXRSTOR64."

"Two programs pinned to one processor, each holding distinct XMM values, YMM upper halves where AVX is enabled, and MXCSR and x87 control words across N sched_yields, read back their own: 0 mismatches."
"UserState::capture shall copy the calling task's FS and GS bases, thread-local slots, data selectors and x87 and SSE state for a fork child."
"A fork child reads its parent's %fs word, MXCSR and an XMM value set before the fork, and an i386 child its parent's %gs word."
"reset_user_state shall, at execve, empty the thread-local slots, load null data selectors with zero FS and GS bases, and load UserState::new's x87 control word 0x037F and MXCSR 0x1F80."

"A program that set a thread pointer, a thread-local entry and an unmasked MXCSR and then execve's finds in the new image FS base 0, get_thread_area(12) empty, MXCSR 0x1F80 and x87 control word 0x037F."
"load_fpu shall load the x87 and SSE registers from the state rt_sigreturn filled from the frame."
"A handler that changes its frame's fpstate MXCSR (legal bits) and an XMM register returns to find both changed."
"enter_compat_segments shall load user data (0x2b) into DS and ES and null into FS as a 32-bit program is first entered or execve'd."
"An i386 program whose first instructions read and write through DS and ES exits 42, on first entry and after an execve."
"A 32-bit program's signal handler shall be entered with user data in DS and ES, loaded through loadable against the running thread's slots with interrupts masked."

"The i386 signal program's SA_SIGINFO handler reads its siginfo and writes its ucontext's EAX through DS, the plain handler writes its sigcontext, both return, and the program exits 42 (the signal `i386` line)."
"restore_user_state and load_program_selectors shall load each data selector only through loadable, so that a saved selector naming a slot emptied since loads as null instead of faulting in ring 0."
"A 32-bit thread whose saved %fs names a thread-local slot emptied before it is next restored resumes with %fs 0, and the boot continues."
"prepare_stack shall lay out a stack so that the first switch_to it runs the task's entry, and switch_to shall save one context's callee-saved registers and stack pointer and resume another's."
"1000 threads spawned on one processor all run to completion, each switched to at least once (the `tasks` line)."

children.name: Processors
children.doc: src/kernel/src/arch/x86_64/smp.rs and apic.rs's commands: starting each processor, and the interrupts processors send each other.

children.value: "describe_cpus shall list the processors the MADT enables, and CpuStarter, send and issue shall start each with INIT and start-up commands to the APIC ID it names, so that it runs kernel work under its own per-processor record."
"Each of the N processors listed runs its share of the work in each of 100 rounds, 0 of it on a processor whose APIC ID is not its record's (the `smp` line)."
"issue with the all-but-self shorthand shall deliver a fixed interrupt on the IPI vector to every other started processor, whose local APIC init_this_cpu enabled at task priority 0."
"Over 100 rounds of work run everywhere, every secondary takes at least one inter-processor interrupt (the `smp` line)."
"CpuStarter::finish shall unmap the start-up trampoline's identity mapping and give its code page and root table back to the frame allocator."
"The free frame count after finish equals the count before CpuStarter::new, and the trampoline's page does not translate in the root."
"CpuStarter::new shall take the boot processor's CR4, and secondary_start shall load it on each secondary once it is in long mode."
"Each of the N online processors reads CR4 equal to the boot processor's, SMEP and SMAP set where offered."
"send shall deliver a fixed interrupt on the IPI vector to the one processor whose APIC ID it names."
"For each secondary, send_ipi_to raises that processor's IPI count by at least 1 and leaves every other secondary's unchanged."
"send shall refuse an APIC ID above 255 without writing the interrupt command register."
"send_ipi_to(256) answers an error and no processor's IPI count moves."

children.name: ParanoidEntries
children.doc: src/kernel/src/arch/x86_64/paranoid.rs: the NMI, #DB and #DF entries, which decide GS for themselves.

children.value: "ferrix_paranoid_entry shall count an NMI taken in the kernel and return from it, with note_gs finding its GS naming a processor's record, and send and issue shall deliver the NMI a processor sends to its own APIC ID."
"An NMI sent to this processor with interrupts masked is accepted, at least one NMI is counted and returned from, and 0 handler runs find a GS naming no processor's record (the `nmi` line)."

"debug shall count a kernel #DB against the breakpoint slot DR6 names, set RF so that the instruction runs, and return, with note_gs finding the kernel's GS, including in the SYSCALL trampoline's stretches on the program's stack."

"Breakpoints on the SYSCALL stub's swapgs and on its sysretq, while a program writes and exits, fire at least 2 and at least 1 times, 0 of them with a foreign GS, and the program exits with its status (the first `debug` line)."
"take_debug_status shall read and clear DR6 on each kernel #DB, so that debug counts each breakpoint once and runs the hook once per #DB."
"With breakpoints armed on a kernel function and on the hook every #DB handler calls, one call of each counts exactly 1 hit per slot and 3 hook runs (the second `debug` line)."

"ferrix_paranoid_entry shall end in its catalogued report a second exception on one IST stack, a machine check and any other vector, and debug shall end in its report a kernel #DB that no breakpoint raised."
"Each of a provoked nested IST entry, a kernel single-step #DB and an injected #MC ends in its catalogued report, and no FERRIX-BOOT-OK."

children.name: Speculation
children.doc: src/kernel/src/arch/x86_64/speculation.rs: the side-channel defences, per processor, and the index clamp.

children.value: "init on the boot processor and apply_this_cpu on each secondary shall record the side-channel defences the processor applied: clamped indices among them in a hardened build, none in a --mitigations off build."
"Each of the N processors has a record; in a hardened boot each includes clamped indices, in a --mitigations off boot each is empty (the `cpu` line)."

"apply shall read back each control the plan writes -- IA32_SPEC_CTRL's IBRS, STIBP and SSBD, EFER.AIBRSE, AMD's VIRT_SPEC_CTRL.SSBD -- and record READ_BACK_FAILED on a processor where one did not hold."
"Under KVM, where the processor offers the controls (`test-boot --accel kvm`), 0 of the N processors record READ_BACK_FAILED. Under TCG the processor offers none and nothing is written."
"clamp_index and clamp_below shall answer the index when it is below its bound and 0 when it is not, in a hardened build, and the index unchanged in a --mitigations off build."
"Hardened: indices inside their bound come back themselves and clamp_index(9, 4) and clamp_below(u64::MAX, 0x2000) through black_box come back 0; --mitigations off: both answer their input."
"switch_barrier shall, in a hardened build, refill the return stack with 32 entries and answer that it issued a barrier."
"After programs have run in different address spaces, a hardened boot counts at least one switch barrier (the `cpu` line)."
"switch_barrier_in_domain shall, in a hardened build, refill the return stack with 32 entries and issue no IBPB: inside one speculation domain only the predictor invalidation is left out."
"Switches between two members of one marked job decide no barrier (the `domain` line, case 1), and the hardened build's return-stack refill runs at each of them."

"Every processor shall program IA32_PAT with X86_PAT before anything maps write-combining, entry 1 write-combining and entries 0 and 3 write-back and uncacheable as at power-on; and a leaf the kernel maps write-combining shall select entry 1 by its write-through bit alone, with device memory's uncacheable entry winning where both are asked."

"Host tests: a write-combining leaf has PWT and not PCD, reads back as itself, and loses to device; X86_PAT's entries 0, 1 and 3 are 0x06, 0x01 and 0x00. On x86-64 the boot's cpu line says entry 1 is write-combining, and every processor read its PAT back, or stage 9's check fails."

"Plan::for_processor shall choose enhanced IBRS where IA32_ARCH_CAPABILITIES offers it, else AutoIBRS, else IBRS; STIBP unless enhanced IBRS; SSBD unless the processor reports it is not affected; the IBPB barrier where IBPB is offered; VERW on exit only for an Intel processor with MD_CLEAR and without MDS_NO; and offered shall decode those bits from CPUID and IA32_ARCH_CAPABILITIES."
"For each row of a table of CPUID and capability words, the plan's defences and MSR values are the expected set."

"report_exposure shall print one `cpu` line saying, for Spectre v2 into ring 0, between programs, store bypass and Meltdown, whether the plan covers it, the processor is not affected, or it is uncovered (AoU-11)."
"Under TCG's qemu64 the line reports Spectre v2 into ring 0 not covered and Meltdown not affected; under KVM with auto-IBRS offered it reports it covered."

children.name: Timers
children.doc: src/kernel/src/arch/x86_64/clock.rs and apic.rs's timer and I/O APICs: the counter, its rate, and the timer interrupt.

children.value: "init shall enable the boot processor's local APIC at task priority 0, and calibrate shall measure its timer's rate over 10 ms of the counter, so that arm(n) fires n ns later by the counter."
"250 ticks of a 1 ms periodic timer, timed by the counter, measure within 25% of 1000 Hz, with 0 unclaimed interrupts."
"arm shall fire the timer interrupt once, at least one tick later, and disarm shall stop it and mask its entry."
"A 1 ms one-shot fires, and does not fire again over the following 10 ms."
"quiesce_io_apics shall mask every redirection entry of every I/O APIC the MADT describes."
"After interrupt bring-up every redirection entry nothing routed since reads back masked, on every I/O APIC: 0 unmasked."

"IoApicInput::for_isa shall find the I/O APIC input the MADT's override puts an ISA IRQ on, with its polarity and trigger, or refuse where no I/O APIC covers it; route shall write the destination before the vector, the signalling bits and the mask."
"The serial port's input reads back its vector and this processor's APIC ID, masked until enable_console_receive and unmasked after, and a byte sent to the port is taken by that interrupt."

"clock::init shall bring up a 64-bit counter and its frequency: the invariant TSC measured over 10 ms of the HPET where both exist, else a 64-bit HPET at its stated period, else the TSC measured against a 32-bit HPET, else against PIT channel 2."
"counter_hz agrees with a reference the counter was not calibrated from, within a stated tolerance, on each path a gate boots."
"clock::init shall fail with a named reason, not answer a counter, when the HPET's counter does not advance or the PIT never reaches its terminal count."
"With the HPET's counter held still, and with no HPET and the PIT's output held low, init answers an error, 2 of 2."
"counter_now shall answer the TSC, or the HPET's main counter read whole across a 32-bit carry, never decreasing on one processor."
"N consecutive counter_now reads on each online processor never decrease."
"counter_is_tsc shall answer true only when the counter counter_now reads is the TSC, at counter_hz, so that the vDSO reads the clock itself only then."
"The vDSO program exits 120: each of the 7 clocks, gettimeofday and time through the vDSO answers between system calls made on either side."

children.name: SignalFrames
children.doc: src/kernel/src/arch/x86_64/signal.rs: a 64-bit program's signal frame, its return, and the context resumed from it.

children.value: "setup_signal_frame shall, for a 64-bit program whose handler names a restorer, write Linux's rt_sigframe below the stack -- pretcode the restorer, a ucontext holding the interrupted registers and mask, the siginfo -- and enter the handler with RDI the signal, RSI the siginfo and RDX the ucontext; restore_signal_frame shall load the registers and mask that frame holds, a register the handler changed through the ucontext included."

"The 64-bit signal program exits 77: its SA_SIGINFO handler for SIGUSR1 saw EDI 10, si_signo 10 at RSI and SIGUSR1 blocked, the 70 it added to the ucontext's saved RBX came back through rt_sigreturn, and the mask after the return is empty (the `signals` line)."

"restore_signal_frame shall refuse a 64-bit frame whose RIP or RSP lies outside the user half, and resume a frame's program with RFLAGS limited to the restorable flags and IF, and CS and SS ring 3's, whatever the frame holds."

"64-bit frames with a kernel-half RIP and with a kernel-half RSP end with SIGSEGV; frames asking IOPL 3, IF clear, TF, and CS and SS 0x10 and 0x18 resume in ring 3 with IOPL 0 and IF set, read by pushfq and by moving CS and SS."
"UserContext::sanitised shall leave CS 64- or 32-bit user code, SS user data and RFLAGS the restorable flags and IF, whatever the trap frame held."
"A context with CS 0x10, SS 0x18 and RFLAGS 0x3100 comes back with user code, user data and RFLAGS 0x202."
"A handler's frame shall carry the interrupted x87 and SSE state, and its return shall reload it, MXCSR masked to the processor's MXCSR_MASK."
"A value in XMM0 and in the x87 control word, clobbered by the handler, reads back after the return for each ABI; a frame with reserved MXCSR bits set returns without a #GP."
"setup_signal_frame shall refuse a frame for a handler installed without SA_RESTORER, and for a 32-bit program whose frame stack lies above 4 GiB."
"A program that signals itself with such a handler is ended with SIGSEGV, 1 of 1 per ABI."

children.name: CompatSignalFrames
children.doc: src/kernel/src/arch/x86_64/signal/compat.rs: an i386 program's two signal frames and their returns.

children.value: "setup_signal_frame shall, for a 32-bit program, write rt_sigframe_ia32 for an SA_SIGINFO handler and sigframe_ia32 for a plain one and enter the handler on it; rt_sigreturn and sigreturn shall load back the saved general registers, a saved EAX the handler changed included."

"The i386 signal program exits 42: its SA_SIGINFO handler saw signal 10, si_signo 10 and its own pid, and its kill answered the 0x77 it wrote to the ucontext's EAX with ESI 0x5eed intact; its plain handler saw 12 and its kill answered the 0x88 it wrote to the sigcontext (the signal `i386` line)."

"compat::restore shall refuse an rt_sigreturn frame whose code selector is kernel or 64-bit code, whose stack selector is the kernel's data, whose flags hold IOPL or VM, or whose GS, FS or DS names a kernel slot, the LDT or the TSS, so that the program ends with SIGSEGV; and shall take a frame changed only in its saved EAX."
"Of frames forged with CS 0x10, CS 0x33, SS 0x18, flags 0x3202, flags 0x2_0202, GS 0x10, FS 0x07 and DS 0x43, 8 of 8 end with SIGSEGV; the same program with only EAX changed exits 42."
"compat::restore shall also refuse a frame holding VIF or VIP, or an ES naming a kernel slot, and every forgery through plain sigreturn as through rt_sigreturn."
"Forged VIF, VIP and ES frames, and the 8 forgeries above sent through sigreturn, each end with SIGSEGV."

"enter_handler shall enter a 32-bit handler with EAX the signal, EDX and ECX the siginfo and ucontext for SA_SIGINFO and zero otherwise; sigcontext_of shall record a fault's trap number and error code."
"A handler reads these registers, and a fault's trap number, and exits with a status saying each matched."
"compat::restore shall restore the mask an i386 frame saved, and for rt_sigreturn its alternate-stack record."
"After each return, rt_sigprocmask reports the mask from before the signal, and sigaltstack the frame's record."

children.name: SystemCallEntry
children.doc: src/kernel/src/arch/x86_64/syscall.rs: SYSCALL's entry, the registers a call reads and a fork child resumes from, and entering a program.

children.value: "syscall::init shall enable SYSCALL and point IA32_LSTAR at the stub, so that a 64-bit program's SYSCALL enters at the stub's first instruction, is dispatched, and returns through its sysretq."

"With breakpoints on the stub's first instruction and on its sysretq, a program that writes and exits hits the first at least twice and the second at least once, and exits 42 (the first `debug` line)."
"syscall::init shall park zero in IA32_KERNEL_GS_BASE, and the GS base saved and restored for a program shall be the program's, so that no program runs with a per-processor record as its GS base."
"After a program has run on a processor, the program's GS base names no processor's per-processor record."

"syscall::init shall point IA32_CSTAR at a stub answering -ENOSYS and leave IA32_SYSENTER_CS zero, so that SYSCALL from compatibility mode answers -ENOSYS, or is #UD on Intel, and SYSENTER ends the program."

"A 64-bit program that far-returns to 0x23 and makes SYSCALL there exits 0, with -ENOSYS, or is ended by SIGILL; one that makes SYSENTER there is ended by SIGSEGV or SIGILL and never reaches its exit (the first `i386` line)."
"ferrix_syscall_entry shall dispatch a SYSCALL with its number from RAX and its first four arguments from RDI, RSI, RDX and R10, and return the result in RAX."
"The 64-bit signal program's rt_sigaction and rt_sigprocmask, whose set size 8 is in R10 and is refused EINVAL otherwise, each answer 0, and the program exits 77, not 99."
"ferrix_syscall_entry shall pass R8 and R9 as a SYSCALL's fifth and sixth arguments."
"A program maps a memfd with its descriptor in R8 and a non-zero page offset in R9 and reads that page's marker."
"syscall::init shall set IA32_FMASK so that SYSCALL clears TF, IF, DF, NT, RF and AC on entry."
"A program calling exit_group with TF set exits with its status; one with DF and AC set makes a call that copies user memory and gets the right answer."
"syscall::init shall program STAR so that SYSRET leaves SS the user data selector at RPL 3."
"A program reads SS after a system call and finds user data at RPL 3."

"set_entry_stack and restore_user_state shall point both ways in from ring 3 -- the SYSCALL entry stack and the TSS's RSP0, which set_privilege_stack finds through STR and SGDT -- at the incoming task's kernel stack, so that two programs taking turns on one processor keep their own registers."
"Two spinning programs pinned to one processor, each preempted in user mode at least twice, exit 41 and 43 with their stack pointers unchanged (the `procs` line)."
"arch_prctl shall refuse ARCH_SET_FS with an address outside the user half with EPERM, and any other request with EINVAL."
"A program's ARCH_SET_FS with 0xffff800000000000 answers -1 and its ARCH_GET_FS -22, and it exits 0 (the `prctl` line)."

"arch_prctl(ARCH_SET_FS) with a user address shall set this processor's FS base, and save_user_state and restore_user_state shall save and restore each task's FS base and its program GS base where its selector is null."
"Two 64-bit programs pinned to one processor each set a distinct FS base and GS base and read their own words through %fs and %gs N times across sched_yield: 0 foreign reads."
"UserRegs::for_child shall copy a SYSCALL frame with every register the parent's but RAX, which is zero, and UserRegs::stack_pointer shall answer its user RSP."
"A frame of 16 distinct values copied for a child prints all 16 by name, RAX 0 and the other 15 unchanged, and its stack pointer is the parent's (the `regs` line)."
"resume_user shall resume a 64-bit fork child from its copied SYSCALL frame through SYSRET, after the call, with the call answering zero."
"The 64-bit fork program's child sees fork answer 0 and exits 23; the parent's wait4 reaps it and the parent exits 24 (the `fork` line)."

"system_call shall hand the dispatcher the trap frame as the caller's registers, and resume_user shall resume the child of a fork made through int $0x80 from it through an IRETQ, after the call, with EAX zero."
"The i386 signal program's fork child exits 23 and wait4 answers its pid with status 23, and the program exits 42."
"UserRegs::set_stack shall start a clone child, from a SYSCALL or an int $0x80 frame, on the stack clone names."
"A thread made with a stack argument reads its stack pointer on entry and finds it at that stack's top, for each ABI."
"rewind_syscall shall, for a SYSCALL restarting without a restart block, point RIP back at the syscall instruction and put the call's number back in RAX, so that the call is made again."
"A FUTEX_WAIT with no timeout, stopped by SIGSTOP and continued by SIGCONT, never records a return and is back on its word (the `threads` stop line)."
"rewind_syscall shall restart a call with a restart block as restart_syscall, x86-64's number through SYSCALL and i386's through int $0x80, and rewind an int $0x80 call by two bytes."
"A clock_nanosleep interrupted by a stop resumes as restart_syscall and sleeps only the rest, for each entry; an i386 futex wait stopped and continued restarts."
"enter_user shall, for a native program, enter ring 3 at its entry point on the stack given, with the start argument in RDI."
"A program started with argument 57 exits 57 (the `argument` line)."
"ferrix_syscall_entry shall, when a SYSCALL's outcome is to enter a new native image, leave through SYSRET at its entry point on its stack."
"A program's execve of the user test program ends with that program's status, 42 (the `execve` line)."
"A program entered fresh, by enter_user or by an execve through SYSCALL, shall find every general register zero but its start argument and stack pointer, with RFLAGS 0x202."
"A program that ORs its registers on entry exits 0, on first start and after execve, for each ABI."
"enter_compat_after_execve shall start an i386 image that a 64-bit program execve'd through SYSCALL, in compatibility mode."
"A 64-bit program execve's the i386 hello program, which exits 42."

"ferrix_syscall_entry and system_call shall ask the registered filter about a call before arch_prctl, sigreturn and rt_sigreturn are answered and before the dispatcher is, with the number's low 32 bits, the instruction after the call, and the token of the entry: x86-64's for SYSCALL and i386's for int $0x80, whatever the image; and shall apply the filter's errno as the dispatcher's answer."

"A test-only filter is shown arch_prctl and rt_sigreturn through SYSCALL and sigreturn and rt_sigreturn through int $0x80 once each, before their answers, and its value comes back; a filter about x86-64 alone does not judge an int $0x80 call."
"syscall_rollback_value shall give the value for RAX that makes the frame of a call that did not run read as it did at the call: the number."
"The value for number 0x2222 is 0x2222 (the `seccomp` line's rollback check); the handler of a trapped call reads it from a real frame in a later landing."

"ferrix_syscall_entry shall test a number against the native range before any Linux table, pass a native number on to the dispatcher without decoding it against x86-64's table, and answer arch_prctl and rt_sigreturn from one decode of a Linux number behind its clamp."

"Every number of the native range, 0x1000 + 158 (arch_prctl's low bits) among them, sorts as native, the numbers either side as Linux numbers the table does not hold, and 158 and 15 as arch_prctl and rt_sigreturn (the `decode` line); with the native test removed the line fails."

children.name: CompatEntry
children.doc: src/kernel/src/arch/x86_64/mod.rs and trap.rs: int $0x80, and which mode an image runs in.

children.value: "An int $0x80 from ring 3 shall be answered as an i386 system call: through a gate ring 3 may use, classified as a system call, its number from EAX and arguments from EBX, ECX and EDX as their low 32 bits, decoded through the i386 table, its result in EAX."

"An ELF32 i386 program's write(1, msg, 16) answers 16, write(-1) answers -9 in EAX, number 90 answers -38, and it exits 42; a 64-bit program's int $0x80 getpid equals its SYSCALL getpid in all of RAX, and dup(0x1_0000_0001) duplicates descriptor 1 (the first `i386` line)."
"system_call shall answer sigreturn and rt_sigreturn by restoring the frame the handler left rather than dispatching them, and dispatch shall deliver a pending signal on the way back to user mode."
"The i386 signal program's two handlers are entered and their kills answer the EAX each wrote into its frame, and the program exits 42 (the signal `i386` line)."
"image_abi shall answer no ABI for an image of another machine, so that the loader refuses it."
"An ELF64 image built for another machine is refused by the loader."
"system_call shall start the image an i386 program execve's through int $0x80 in its mode."
"An i386 program execve's an i386 image through int $0x80, which runs and exits with its status."
"user_platform shall name the program's platform as Linux does: x86_64 for a 64-bit program and i686 for an i386 one."
"AT_PLATFORM reads x86_64 for a 64-bit program and i686 for an i386 one."

children.name: Exceptions
children.doc: src/kernel/src/arch/x86_64/trap.rs and src/kernel/src/trap.rs: the gates, and what a fault becomes.

children.value: "init_traps and trap::init shall install and load a gate for every exception vector, and classify and fault_signal shall name for an exception a user-mode instruction took the signal Linux sends: #DE SIGFPE, #UD SIGILL, #PF on an unmapped address SIGSEGV, #GP SIGSEGV, #MF SIGFPE."

"Programs that divide by zero, run ud2, read an unmapped address, run hlt in ring 3 and take an unmasked x87 zero-divide end with SIGFPE, SIGILL, SIGSEGV, SIGSEGV and SIGFPE, 5 of 5, and the boot goes on (the `fault` line)."

"dispatch shall answer a breakpoint, illegal instruction or other fault taken from user mode by forcing the architecture's signal on the program through the registered return path, and shall not stop the kernel."
"The faulting programs of the `fault` line are ended by their signals and the check returns to the boot."
"handle_page_fault shall answer with SIGBUS a user fault the address space reports as past the end of a mapped file."
"A program that reads the second page of a two-page shared mapping of a one-page memfd ends with SIGBUS (the `fault` line)."
"handle_page_fault shall resolve a user-mode fault in a region the running program's space maps by making the mapping true, so that the instruction is retried."
"The user test program runs with at least 1 page fault resolved and exits 42."
"dispatch shall count an interrupt taken from user mode, have the architecture service it and signal its end, and then preempt the program."
"Two spinning programs pinned to one processor are each preempted at least twice and switched to at least twice, and the count of interrupts taken in user mode rises while they run."
"trap::init shall route the debug exception and the NMI to the paranoid entry."

"An NMI sent to this processor with interrupts masked is taken at least once with a GS naming a processor's record, and hardware breakpoints on the SYSCALL entry and return fire with the kernel's GS while the program exits 42 (the `nmi` and `debug` lines)."
"trap::init shall let ring 3 raise no vector but int $0x80 and the breakpoint."
"A program running int $0x81 and int $14 is ended with SIGSEGV, 2 of 2."
"fault_signal and ferrix_trap_entry shall end a program's int3 and a trap-flag single step with SIGTRAP, clearing DR6, and an alignment check with SIGBUS."
"A program's int3 and its single step each end it with SIGTRAP, and an #AC with SIGBUS."
"trap::init shall give the double fault and the machine check their own interrupt stacks, so that a kernel stack overflow is taken as a double fault on its own stack."
"A deliberate kernel stack overflow ends in the FX-9004 report."
"dispatch shall step a kernel breakpoint's saved instruction pointer past it, count it, and return."
"Two kernel int3s each return, the count rises by 2, and a register the handler must preserve comes back intact."
"report, fatal, report_trap and vector_name shall print a trap the kernel cannot continue past -- its headline, vector, faulting address and saved registers -- with its catalogue entry, and stop."
"A boot that faults in the kernel on purpose ends with `FERRIX-PANIC page fault at` its address, the vector, CR2 and register lines, and the catalogue entry."
"handle_page_fault shall resolve a kernel fault inside the on-demand window by mapping a zeroed page and retrying."
"Three touches of the demand window are resolved, each page read back zero, within the window's frames."

children.name: Processor
children.doc: src/kernel/src/arch/x86_64/mod.rs and cpu.rs: per-processor state, the user root, interrupts, and how a run ends.

children.value: "set_cpu_local shall install the processor's own per-processor record as its GS base, and cpu_local and cpu_local_register shall read that address back."
"Over 100 rounds on every online processor, the record reached through the register names the processor's own APIC ID: 0 misplaced (the `smp` line)."
"set_cpu_local shall arm SYSCALL on the processor it runs on."
"A program pinned to the checking processor makes write and exit_group by SYSCALL and exits 42."
"prepare_user_root shall make a new root share the kernel's upper half, and install_user_root shall make this processor translate its user half through that root."

"Installed twice across an uninstall, a space's 2 faulted pages each read back what the processor wrote through the user address, and the write is found through the direct map at the frame the walk names."
"uninstall_user_root shall return this processor to the kernel's own root."
"After uninstall, CR3 is the kernel's root and the user address no longer translates."
"init_traps shall set SMEP, SMAP and UMIP in CR4 where the processor offers them."
"CR4 reads back SMEP, SMAP and UMIP set on each online processor that offers them."
"init_interrupts shall bring up the counter and the local APIC timer so that a timed sleep is woken."
"A 20 ms sleep returns after at least 20 ms and at most 400 ms."
"Irq::disable shall mask interrupts and answer whether they were open, and Irq::restore shall open them only when that answer says they were."
"With interrupts open, disable answers open, a nested disable answers closed, the inner restore leaves them closed and the outer one opens them."
"send_ipi_to shall interrupt the processor with the APIC ID it names, and refuse an ID above 255."
"For each online secondary, send_ipi_to its ID raises its IPI count and no other's, and ID 256 is refused."
"mask_interrupt and unmask_interrupt shall refuse every line on x86-64, whose devices mask their own MSI-X entries."
"Both answer an error for any line number."
"service_interrupts shall signal no end of interrupt for the spurious vector."
"A spurious interrupt provoked on purpose is answered without an EOI, and the next real interrupt is delivered."
"console_receive_irq and enable_console_receive shall route the serial port's receive interrupt, so that a byte typed arrives through the ring by interrupt."
"On q35 the receive interrupt is installed, and a byte typed on the serial port arrives by interrupt, not by polling."
"init_console shall bring up the 16550 so that the kernel's lines reach the serial port."
"cargo xtask test-boot reads FERRIX-BOOT-OK from the x86-64 guest's serial output."
"shutdown shall drain the console and power the machine off."
"After init exits, QEMU exits by itself within the grace, with status 0 or 33, and init's exit line is in the log."
"reset shall restart the machine from firmware after the console has drained."
"Under ferrix.onexit=reset the kernel says it is resetting and the loader's banner is printed again after it."
"halt shall stop the processor for good."
"After the FX-1501 panic nothing more is printed and QEMU does not exit by itself."
"vdso_spec shall describe the vDSO's code with __vdso_clock_gettime, __vdso_gettimeofday and __vdso_time and their aliases at the offsets the code puts them."
"The image exports each function and alias where its code is, and a program calling each answers between two system calls: exit 120."
"A secondary that masks interrupts, finds no work and waits with enable_interrupts_and_halt shall be woken by an interrupt sent to it."
"Every online processor runs the work handed out once in each of 100 rounds, and every secondary takes at least 1 inter-processor interrupt (the `smp` line)."
"load_gdt, reload_segments, load_tss and load_idt shall install the kernel's descriptor tables, segments and task state, so that an exception from ring 3 enters the kernel's handler for its vector."
"The six faulting programs of the `fault` line end with SIGFPE, SIGILL, SIGSEGV, SIGSEGV, SIGFPE and SIGBUS, 6 of 6, and the boot goes on."
"gdt's load shall give RSP0 the current stack pointer, rounded down to 16 bytes, before any task replaces it."
"Right after gdt::init, the TSS's RSP0 equals the stack pointer at that point rounded down to 16."
"frame_pointer shall answer the calling function's frame record, from which a failure report's backtrace walks."
"The ferrix.onexit=panic report carries at least 1 `trace #0` line that xtask's symbolizer resolves to a kernel function."
"triple_fault shall reset the processor by loading an empty IDT and raising a breakpoint."
"A --reset boot with no FADT reset register and no keyboard controller starts the loader again."
"hardware_random shall answer a word from RDSEED, or from RDRAND without RDSEED, retrying up to 10 times while the carry is clear, and nothing on a processor with neither."
"With RDRAND and RDSEED offered the `random` line counts at least 1 word from the processor; with neither, 0."

children.name: Memory
children.doc: src/kernel/src/arch/x86_64/cpu.rs: the control-register and TLB operations the memory code relies on.

children.value: "flush_tlb_including_global shall drop every cached translation on its processor, global ones included, by toggling CR4.PGE and reloading CR3."

"20 remaps of a global kernel page to a new frame are each seen by every online processor: 0 stale reads (the `tlb` line). Under TCG a plain CR3 reload would pass as well; the KVM boot row is the one that tells them apart."
"invalidate_page shall drop this processor's translation of the page holding an address, global or not."
"A global kernel page read, remapped to another frame and invalidated by invalidate_page alone reads the new frame's value: 0 stale reads."
"write_cr3 shall make the processor translate user addresses through the tables at the root it is given."
"Two tasks pinned to one processor, each in its own address space, read one user address 64 times each across yields: 128 reads see their own space's value, 0 the other's (the `spaces` line)."
"kernel_write_protected shall report CR0.WP, so that the boot stops when the kernel could write through a read-only mapping."
"Stage 1 reads CR0.WP set, and a kernel write through a read-only mapping faults."
"enable_umip shall set CR4.UMIP where the processor offers it, so that ring 3 cannot read the descriptor tables' addresses."
"A program executing SIDT and one executing SGDT each end with SIGSEGV, 2 of 2."

children.name: Interrupts
children.doc: src/kernel/src/arch/x86_64/msi.rs: message-signalled interrupts.

children.value: "msi_allocate shall answer a message address and data that, written by a device, raise the vector it allocated on the calling processor's local APIC and reach the handler registered for it."
"On x86-64 the `pci` line reports at least 1 entropy request completed by MSI-X."
"allocate_vector shall hand out each of vectors 0x40 to 0x7F at most once and answer nothing once all 64 are taken, and msi_allocate shall refuse then, and refuse a local APIC ID above 255."
"64 allocations answer 64 distinct vectors in 0x40..0x80; the 65th answers nothing and msi_allocate its error."

children.name: Console
children.doc: src/kernel/src/arch/x86_64/console.rs: the serial port.

children.value: "read_byte shall answer each byte received at the serial port once, in the order received, and nothing when none waits."
"cargo xtask test-jobs on x86-64 types 18 steps at the serial port, and each step's answer appears after its keystrokes."
"transmit_interrupt shall enable the serial port's transmit-empty interrupt while bytes are queued, so that a task's queued write goes out by the interrupt."
"A task's write longer than a 64-byte burst leaves at most 64 bytes to the writer, and the rest is sent by the transmit interrupt within 2 s."
"console::init shall record whether the port's FIFOs came on, transmit_room shall offer 16 bytes with them and 1 without, and transmit_buffer shall name which."
"On QEMU's 16550A, transmit_buffer names a 16550's FIFO and transmit_room answers 0 or 16, never 1."
"write_byte shall wait at most 100000 polls for the holding register, and drain shall return once the transmitter is idle or after 10000000 polls."
"Against a port that never reports ready, write_byte and drain each return; after drain returns on a live port, the transmitter reads idle."

children.name: Dispatch
children.doc: src/kernel/src/syscall/mod.rs's dispatcher and src/kernel/src/trap.rs's registration: which calls reach which answer.

children.value: "system_call shall pass a call to the entry set_syscall_entry registered, and dispatch_with shall answer a native-entry number that no table carries with -ENOSYS, not a handler or a fault."
"0xDEAD, usize::MAX and usize::MAX - 1, each dispatched as a native call through the registered entry, are answered -38, 3 of 3."
"decode_syscall shall decode a number through x86-64's own table."
"Of getpid's numbers in the three tables, exactly x86-64's decodes to getpid, and dispatching it answers a pid above zero."
"mmio's read8 to write32 shall each make one volatile access of its width at the address given, never elided, merged or reordered with another volatile access."
"Every device the boot drives answers through them, so each architecture's boot test runs them; no check tells a merged access from two."

"enable_extended_state shall, only when CPUID reports XSAVE and leaf 0xD supports x87 and SSE, set CR4.OSXSAVE and load XCR0 with x87 and SSE, and AVX where CPUID reports it and the standard-form area for them is 832 bytes with AVX at 576; load_extended_state_on_this_cpu shall load the same XCR0 on each secondary, whose CR4 is the boot processor's."

"The boot says 'program register state: x87, SSE and AVX, saved with XSAVE' on a model with AVX and XSAVEOPT, and 'saved with FXSAVE; no XSAVE, so no AVX' on qemu64; Claude Code's AVX2-only runtime completes test-claude-code's turn on four processors, and on qemu64 does not."

"Where AVX is enabled, setup_signal_frame shall carry the interrupted state as Linux's XSAVE area -- FP_XSTATE_MAGIC1, the sizes and components in the software-reserved bytes, XSTATE_BV, the YMM upper halves, FP_XSTATE_MAGIC2 -- with UC_FP_XSTATE in uc_flags; restore_signal_frame shall take AVX back only from a whole area and reset it otherwise, take nothing of the header but XSTATE_BV, and XSTATE_BV shall name only AVX, x87 and SSE, and only XCR0's components, before XRSTOR64 sees it."

"A handler that sets every bit of its frame's XSTATE_BV, XCOMP_BV and reserved header bytes, keeping the magic words and sizes, returns through rt_sigreturn and its program runs on to exit 79 (the `xstate` line); with restore_fpu's and set_xstate_bv's masks both taken out, the boot stops on a #GP in ring 0, under TCG and under KVM."

"With the speculation switch on, vector_leak shall, on a Zen 2 processor (family 0x17, Linux's amd_zenbleed models), set DE_CFG[9] on every processor unless the microcode is at the fixed revision, and withhold AVX from XCR0 in a guest; and on an Intel model Linux lists for Gather Data Sampling without GDS_NO, keep AVX only where GDS_CTRL's microcode mitigation is on or can be turned back on, which it does on every processor; the boot line shall say which."

"decide_vector_leak gives each of twelve processors -- Zen 2 bare metal with old, fixed and unlisted microcode, a Zen 2 guest, one without AVX, a Zen 5, Kaby Lake without and with GDS_NO, with GDS_CTRL on, off and unlocked, off and locked, an Alder Lake -- its verdict, and family_and_model reads a Matisse and a Kaby Lake right; with the guest rule taken out, the check fails. The writes, DE_CFG[9] and clearing GDS_MITG_DIS, are not exercised on the gate's machines, which are not affected parts; in a guest the verdict rests on the model the hypervisor presents (SPECULATION.md section 9, AoU-11)."
"dispatch_with shall send a native-entry number in the native range to native_call, which answers it for the calling task's own process."
"Two programs whose every native call is made by SYSCALL -- vmo_create, channel_write with a handle, object_wait_one, channel_read, vmo_read -- each exit 0."
"dispatch_with shall answer an int $0x80 number in the native range with -ENOSYS, never as a native call."
"An int $0x80 with a number in 0x1000..0x1FFF answers -38."
"unanswered shall print a call answered ENOSYS by name while report_unanswered's bound lasts, and nothing once it is spent."
"After report_unanswered(1), two unanswered calls print exactly one `syscall ... answered ENOSYS` line."

"The personality, an interface the item states: its Process::end, the one path exit_group, a kill, a job's kill, an OOM kill and a last thread's exit take, shall record the end through the core's end_record; and a task it launches after its process began to end, or while another thread replaces the program, shall be posted END through notify once it is listed, unless has_end says it holds it."

"The personality, an interface the item states: execve's end_other_threads shall post END through post_to_tasks to every task of the process but the caller's after it records the replacing thread, waking each and interrupting its processor."

"In a program of three threads, two counting in user mode and one waiting, the first thread's replacement of the program sees the other two leave within a second (stage 7's replacement check); with the post removed the counting one outlives it and the check fails by name."

"The personality, an interface the item states: enter_stop shall post STOP to every task of the process after it stores the stop: the caller's own through post_own when it is one of the process's threads, and every other's through post_to_tasks, woken and interrupted."
"The stop check's second stop, made with no signal, parks both counting threads; with the post to the other tasks removed it fails by name, and with the look of L.sched.33 on it stops with FX-0520."

"The personality, an interface the item states: SIGNAL shall be posted wherever needs_attention can turn true for a thread's signals: by Process::post with every signal it records, to the thread it was sent to or to every thread that does not block it; by change_blocked when a change unblocks a signal or saves a mask, to that thread; by force and by a marked restart, to the running task; to the thread a signal is handed on to; to a task launched with a signal it can take already pending; and by return_to_user to its own task when a pass ends on its delivery cap of 65, so the masked look goes round again for the rest."

"A signal sent to a process whose first thread blocks it is taken by its second, which spins alone on its processor (stage 7's hand-off check); with Process::post's and the wake's SIGNAL removed it never is, and the check fails by name. 35 ignored signals pending for a check's process and for its thread, 70 deliveries, are all taken before the way back returns (the `capped` line); with the capped pass's post removed the boot stops on FX-0520."
"system_call shall answer ENOSYS with no entry registered, and the first registration shall stand."
"With no entry registered, system_call answers -38; a second set_syscall_entry leaves the first in place."
"system_call and dispatch shall regroup the running task after a call or a trap from user mode, so that a process moved to another job runs in it from then on."
"After a program writes its pid to another cgroup's cgroup.procs, its next charges land in that job."

"filter_system_call shall answer nothing with no filter registered and ask the registered filter otherwise, the first registration shall stand, and an errno the filter answers shall be cut to 4095 before it is written as the call's result."

"Every entry of the running architecture, driven with frames of the check's own, asks the registered filter exactly once per call, and the errnos 0, 13, 512, 4095, 4096, 5000 and 4294967295 come back as 0, -13, -512, -4095, -4095, -4095 and -4095; a slot with nothing registered answers nothing, and one registered twice asks the first (the `seccomp` line)."

children.name: InterruptRemapping
children.doc: NVIDIA's N0g on x86-64 (docs/NVIDIA.md section 12.3): remapped messages, the console's I/O APIC line converted at bring-up, and x2APIC handled on every processor.

children.value: "Where a unit remaps, msi_allocate shall write the vector's interrupt remapping entry, indexed by the vector's slot among the sixty-four, for the function's requester ID and the asking processor, and answer a remappable-format message naming it with data 0; where no unit remaps, a compatibility-format message as before. The check vector 0xFC shall be outside the sixty-four, only counted and acknowledged, and counted stray outside checks R1 and R2."

"On x86-64 under KVM and TCG edu's remapped MSI is delivered unmasked and not masked (R4) and virtio-rng's MSI-X completes; edu's MSI capability programmed in compatibility format to 0xFC (R1), and as an NMI (R2), faults 0x25 and arrives nowhere, and programmed with another function's entry (R3) faults 0x26 and arrives nowhere within the unit's patience; with remapping left off the forged 0xFC arrives and R1 fails. Host test: a remappable message names its handle by bits 19:5 and 2, format bit 4."

"At a unit's interrupt remapping bring-up, the console's I/O APIC line, live in compatibility format since stage 3, shall be converted when that unit's DMAR scope names its I/O APIC by its MADT identifier: masked under its lock; a fresh vector V1 taken and its entry written, with the line's destination, trigger and the I/O APIC's source ID, outside the lock; V0 kept taken for good; and its handler moved to V1 through the generic interrupt layer, still masked, leaving V0 a handler that counts. No vector shall have been handed out by then but the line's, or the boot stops by name. After IRE, its entry shall be rewritten in remappable format with V1 as its vector, unmasked, and the port serviced once. With no scope naming its I/O APIC, no unit shall remap. A delivery on V0 afterwards shall be counted and fail the boot."

"On x86-64 under KVM (split irqchip) and TCG the bring-up line says the console's line is converted, V0 retired; check R9's line says every vector handed out is the console's; a byte looped back while the line is masked is read by the service once, by reading the port; check R5 sees a looped-back byte arrive through V1 and none on V0, and on a UART that raises no interrupt in loopback says it is not observable and fails only on a delivery to V0 (test-boot requires the positive line on the reference machine); the end-of-boot line counts 0 on V0. Controls: the line left unmasked through the conversion lets KVM's old compatibility route deliver on V0 after IRE, which is counted, and the boot fails; the entry left not present, the byte never arrives; the service dropped, the masked byte is not read; edu minted before bring-up, the boot stops on R9. Host tests: the remappable entry's handle and vector, and the I/O APIC's source ID matched by its identifier."

"Every processor, the boot processor in apic::init and each application processor first in secondary_start, shall read its own IA32_APIC_BASE before it uses the local APIC's MMIO window, and one in x2APIC mode shall be taken to disabled and then to xAPIC; where the platform locks legacy xAPIC (IA32_XAPIC_DISABLE_STATUS), the boot shall stop naming the processor."

"On x86-64 under KVM and TCG the check puts the first application processor in x2APIC mode before its own look; every processor looks, that one is switched to xAPIC and comes up, and stage 4's apic line counts them; with secondary_start's look removed that processor never comes up and stage 4 fails."

"An interrupt remapping entry's destination shall be built only by ferrix_paging::vtd::remap::destination, in xAPIC format (the APIC ID in bits 15:8), and an APIC ID above 255 shall be refused rather than truncated; the x2APIC work must set EIME and widen it."
"Host tests: IDs 0 and 255 encode in bits 15:8, 256 and above are refused, and an entry carries the encoded destination in DST."

children.name: Traps
children.doc: src/kernel/src/arch/aarch64/trap.rs: the vector table, the save and restore sequences, and the decoding of a syndrome into the architecture-neutral trap the generic dispatcher acts on.

children.value: "classify shall turn a trap frame into the trap its vector entry and exception class name: a breakpoint, a system call, an undefined instruction, a data or instruction abort as a page fault with its address, access and origin, an IRQ entry as an interrupt, and any other class, allocated or not, as a named fault; and came_from_user shall answer from the vector entry."

"The machine check's 14 frames, one per class a boot or a program raises and one the architecture has not allocated, are each classified as the trap listed for them, and a frame from EL0 and one from EL1 are told apart."

"fault_signal shall give a program's unresolved trap the signal, si_code and address Linux's arch/arm64 gives it: SIGTRAP for a breakpoint, SIGILL for an undefined or unallocated instruction class, SIGSEGV with MAPERR or ACCERR for an abort, SIGBUS with ADRALN for a misaligned program counter or stack pointer, SIGFPE for a trapped floating-point exception."
"Each of the machine check's 12 faulting frames is given the signal, si_code and address listed for it."

"A program whose own instruction takes a misaligned program counter, an undefined instruction, a breakpoint or a read past the end of a file it mapped shall be ended by SIGBUS, SIGILL, SIGTRAP and SIGBUS respectively, the kernel going on: the vector table's entry from EL0 saves the frame, hands it to ferrix_trap_entry and returns through resume_user."
"Four programs, each one of those instructions and then exit_group(97), are run from the trap check, and each ends with the status 128 plus its signal."

"system_call shall refuse an svc taken from EL1, answer rt_sigreturn itself by replacing the whole frame, and otherwise pass x8 and x0 to x5 to the dispatcher and write its result into x0, or begin the program an execve or clone child enters at its entry and stack."
"Every program the boot runs makes its calls through this path; a check that an svc from EL1 is refused and that a call's six arguments and its number reach the dispatcher unchanged is not written."

"report_trap shall print the interrupted state -- the exception class by name, the syndrome, the fault address and the registers -- without taking the console's log, for a trap that stops the kernel."
"A kernel trap's failure report carries the class name, esr, far and the 31 registers; no boot check provokes one, and a deliberate crash is the failure path's evidence."
"A breakpoint the kernel raised itself shall be stepped over and returned from: advance_past_breakpoint moves the return address past the brk, which AArch64 leaves pointing at it."
"Stage 3's check raises two breakpoints; both reach the handler and return to the instruction after them, a register kept across them unchanged."

"set_cpu_local shall point TPIDR_EL1 at this processor's own per-CPU record, and cpu_local and cpu_local_register shall read it back, so that the trap path finds this processor's state whatever a program left in its registers."
"Each processor's per-CPU record is its own: a check that every online processor reads back the record it installed is not written."

children.name: Signals
children.doc: src/kernel/src/arch/aarch64/signal.rs: the rt_sigframe Linux builds on AArch64 and the restore that reads it back, and the rewind of a system call a signal interrupted.

children.value: "rewind_syscall shall make an interrupted svc run again when the program resumes: x0 gets its first argument back, the return address steps back over the svc, and x8 keeps the program's number, or becomes restart_syscall's when the call's restart is restart_syscall's."
"A clock_nanosleep frame rewound both ways has x0 its argument, the return address four bytes back, and x8 clock_nanosleep's number and restart_syscall's respectively."

"setup_signal_frame shall write an rt_sigframe as arch/arm64 lays it out -- siginfo, ucontext with the registers and one fpsimd_context, a frame record -- 16-byte aligned below the stack pointer, and enter the handler with x0 the signal, x1 the siginfo, x2 the ucontext and x30 the restorer."

"A handler entered from a frame this writes reads its signal, its siginfo and its interrupted registers where musl reads them; the generic signal checks run handlers but assert the generic layer's behaviour, and a check of the frame's layout on this architecture is not written."

"restore_signal_frame shall refuse a frame whose stack pointer is not 16-byte aligned or whose records hold no single fpsimd_context, and shall load the registers from it with PSTATE's mode, interrupt masks and execution state forced to EL0's."

"A frame forged with EL1 in PSTATE and masked interrupts returns to EL0 with them clear, and a misaligned or fpsimd-less frame is refused; not written as a check here (the x86-64 part of H.TRAP.5 has its forged frames)."

children.name: Context
children.doc: src/kernel/src/arch/aarch64/switch.rs: moving between kernel stacks, and a user task's floating-point, SIMD and thread-pointer state across the switch, a fork and an execve.

children.value: "switch_to shall save the callee-saved registers and the stack pointer of the running context and resume the one saved at next, and prepare_stack shall lay out a new stack so that the first switch to it calls entry with argument."

"Every task the scheduler starts runs its entry and every switch returns to the task switched from; the scheduler's checks assert the generic layer's fairness and wakes, and a check that a switch preserves x19 to x30 is not written."

"save_user_state and restore_user_state shall carry a user task's q0 to q31, FPCR, FPSR and TPIDR_EL0 across a switch, capture shall copy them for a fork child, and reset_user_state and new shall give an execve the starting state: every register zero, round to nearest, no exception trapped, no thread pointer."
"Two tasks whose SIMD registers hold different values each read back their own after switches; a check of it is not written, though every musl program's memcpy would corrupt without it."

children.name: Interrupts
children.doc: src/kernel/src/arch/aarch64/gic.rs, gic/gicv3.rs, gic/gicv3_its.rs and the interrupt half of mod.rs: which controller the machine has, a GICv3 and its ITS brought up, lines masked and let through, and interrupts claimed, dispatched and retired.

children.value: "described_version shall give a GIC the driver of the version firmware states, and for version 0 the one its register blocks imply -- a CPU interface GICv2's, a redistributor region GICv3's -- and none to a description with neither."
"Each of the machine check's 6 descriptions, versions 0, 2, 3 and 4 with and without each block, is given the driver listed for it."

"init and init_from_tree shall find the interrupt controller in the MADT or the device tree and bring up the driver described_version chose, with its GICv2m frame or its ITS where the description has one, before any line is enabled."

"Every aarch64 boot the suite runs reports the controller it described, GICv2 by default and GICv3 with an ITS under boot-gicv3, and takes interrupts; the report is judged by test-boot's stage lines rather than by a check that asserts the version."

"gicv3::init shall map the distributor and the redistributor region, put every shared line off in group 1 at the default priority with affinity routing on, and init_this_cpu shall wake this core's redistributor, found by its affinity, and enable its CPU interface's system registers."
"The boot-gicv3 boot takes its timer and device interrupts on every core; a check that a shared line is off after bring-up and that each core found its own redistributor is not written."

"mask_interrupt and unmask_interrupt shall stop and let through a line at the controller, in the distributor for a shared line and this core's redistributor for a private one, so that the register reads back what was asked."
"An idle private line and an idle shared line, unmasked and masked again, each read back enabled and then disabled at the controller, on the GICv2 boot and the GICv3 one."
"mask_interrupt and unmask_interrupt shall refuse the identifiers 1020 to 1023, which are the controller's answers and not lines."
"service_interrupts shall claim every pending interrupt, dispatch it and retire it with exactly the value its claim returned, until the controller answers spurious."

"Every boot's timer ticks and device interrupts arrive; the generic interrupt checks assert delivery to the holder (H.IRQ.1), not the claim and retire order, and a check of that order is not written."

"send_ipi_to_others and send_ipi_to shall interrupt the other processors on the IPI line after ordering the sender's stores before the interrupt, by the distributor on a GICv2 and ICC_SGI1R_EL1 on a GICv3."
"The shootdown check's flushes reach every processor (H.MEM.7, smp/check.rs); a check that an IPI arrives on each other core and on none twice is not written."

"The ITS driver shall quiesce an ITS firmware left on, give it zeroed device and collection tables, a command queue and each core's LPI property and pending tables, and map a device's next event to a free LPI collected on the boot core, waiting for each command to be consumed."
"Under boot-gicv3 the virtio devices' message interrupts arrive through the ITS; a check that a mapped event raises its LPI and only it is not written."
"gicv3_its::allocate shall refuse a device ID past the device table the ITS was given, rather than map it."
"On the GICv3 boot with an ITS, asking for a vector for device ID u32::MAX is refused."
"msi_doorbell shall name the page a device's message writes land in -- the ITS's translater or the GICv2m frame -- so that an IOMMU domain maps it, and none on a machine with neither."
"The iommu domain check's device writes its message through its domain (L.iommu); a check that the page named is the one the controller decodes is not written."

"disable_interrupts shall mask debug, SError, IRQ and FIQ, enable_interrupts shall unmask IRQ alone, a saved DAIF shall be put back exactly by Irq::restore, and wait_for_work shall wait with IRQ masked and then unmask it, so that an interrupt pending before the wait ends it."
"Every lock that masks interrupts restores the state it found; a check that a nested save and restore leaves DAIF as it was is not written."

children.name: Timer
children.doc: src/kernel/src/arch/aarch64/timer.rs and its wrappers in mod.rs: the generic timer's virtual counter and comparator.

children.value: "timer::arm shall make the virtual timer fire once, nanos from now, by setting its comparator to the counter plus nanos in counter ticks and enabling it, and disarm shall mask it."

"Stage 3's timer check: a one-shot armed for a millisecond fires, and has not fired again ten intervals later; then 250 ticks at a requested 1,000 Hz take a time the counter measures as within 25 per cent of that rate, every tick an interrupt a handler took."

"timer::init and init_from_tree shall take the timer's interrupt as firmware describes it, a private one, and shall refuse a counter whose CNTFRQ_EL0 reads zero or that does not advance; counter_now shall read the counter after an isb."
"Every boot reports the counter's frequency and ticks; a check that a zero frequency is refused is not written."
"allow_user_counter shall let EL0 read the virtual counter and CNTFRQ_EL0, as Linux does, and nothing else of the timer."
"A program's clock_gettime through musl reads the counter; a check that EL0 can read CNTVCT_EL0 and cannot write the comparator is not written."

children.name: Console
children.doc: src/kernel/src/arch/aarch64/console.rs and its wrappers in mod.rs: which console the command line names -- the PL011 (arch/arm_common), a 16550 at an MMIO address, or a ramoops record -- and bytes to and from it.

children.value: "ns16550_port shall read `uart8250,mmio,<address>` as a 16550 at that address only when the address is hexadecimal with a 0x prefix, and shall refuse a port in I/O space and any other console's value. The ramoops zone's value is console's (L.console.40)."
"`uart8250,mmio,0x3f8` is read as the port at 0x3f8; `uart8250,mmio,3f8`, `uart8250,mmio,0x`, `uart8250,io,0x3f8` and a ramoops value are each refused."

"console::init shall map the console the command line names as device memory before the first byte: a 16550's page at its address, a ramoops zone whole, continuing the loader's record where its signature is, or else the PL011."

"QEMU's boots print through the PL011; the crosvm guest's log (~/.local/share/ferrix/pixel7/vm-20260926-140648) through its 16550; the Pixel 7's boot log through its ramoops zone after the watchdog reset. None of the three is a check."

"write_byte and put shall hand a byte to the console the command line named -- the PL011, the 16550 once its holding register has room within a bounded wait, or the ramoops record, dropping it once the zone is full -- and drain shall wait, bounded, until the port has sent everything."
"Every gate reads the boot's log from the serial port, FERRIX-BOOT-OK among it; the 16550 and ramoops arms run only on the crosvm guest and the Pixel 7."

"read_byte shall give a byte the port received, none from a ramoops record, and the receive interrupt shall be enabled at the controller and in the port only for the PL011, whose bytes read_console_byte then takes from the receive ring."
"The console input check runs the ring (console/input.rs); a check that a byte the host sends reaches a reader on this architecture is test-shell's typing, not a check."

children.name: Translation
children.doc: The translation half of mod.rs and cpu.rs: the loader's identity map dropped, a program's tables installed in TTBR0_EL1 beside the kernel's in TTBR1_EL1, the TLB invalidated, and the cache maintenance code and shared memory need.

children.value: "install_user_root shall translate the lower half through a program's root in TTBR0_EL1 and drop this processor's cached user translations, and uninstall_user_root shall stop translating the lower half, so that a kernel thread reaches no program's memory."
"Two programs mapping one address reach their own frames (H.MEM.1, checked generically); a check that a kernel thread's lower-half access faults is not written."
"drop_identity_map shall stop the lower half translating through the loader's identity map, and identity_map_live shall read from TCR_EL1 and TTBR0_EL1 whether it still does."
"Stage 1 requires identity_map_live false after the drop; it is in main.rs, product code."

"flush_tlb and flush_tlb_page shall make every table write before them visible to the walker (dsb ishst) and then invalidate the whole TLB, or the page's entries for every ASID, inner-shareable, so that every core drops them."

"The shootdown checks (smp/check.rs) assert that a table waits for its shootdown and that a flushed translation is gone on every processor, across architectures; this architecture's instructions are not asserted apart."

"clean_to_poc and clean_invalidate_to_poc shall write back, and drop, every data cache line covering a range by the smallest line CTR_EL0 gives, and sync_instructions shall make instructions written through the data side the ones every core fetches."

"A secondary that starts with its caches off reads the start block the boot core wrote, and a program's page of code runs as written; on QEMU, which models no caches, neither can fail, and a real core's evidence is the board's boot."
"enable_user_access_protection shall turn on PAN where the core implements it, and permit_user_access and forbid_user_access shall clear and set PSTATE.PAN around a user copy alone."
"The boot line says PAN on under QEMU's max CPU; a check that a kernel read of a user page outside a copy faults is not written."

"dma_barrier shall order every memory access before it against every one after it as a DMA master observes them, both ways -- dmb osh, the outer-shareable domain a device sits in -- so that the item's virtqueue publishes a descriptor before the index that counts it, reads a used entry only after the index that counts it, and rings the doorbell only after the index is published."

"No check can fail without it on the machines the suite boots: QEMU's TCG makes a core's accesses in program order. The instruction is argued (F-44). A real core's evidence is the Pixel 7's crosvm guest running stage 10's virtio check, when the hardware may be used (F-44's BACKLOG row): the DK1 has no PCI and no virtio. H.DMA.2 is its parent because the item's virtqueue exists only to drive that requirement's out-of-domain probe."

children.name: Processors
children.doc: src/kernel/src/arch/aarch64/smp.rs and the processor half of cpu.rs: which processors firmware says can be started, starting them through PSCI, and what each core says it has.
