children.value: "describe_cpus shall name every processor the MADT's enabled GIC CPU interfaces, or the device tree's /cpus with PSCI as its enable method, describe, by affinity, with this one as the boot processor, and the boot processor alone under nosmp."
"The boot line counts the cores QEMU was given (4, and 1 under boot-nosmp); it is judged by test-boot's lines, not a check."

"CpuStarter shall start a processor through PSCI CPU_ON on its own stack with an identity map and a start block whose registers are the boot core's, secondary_start shall bring it into the kernel, and finish shall take the identity map down only after every started core has reported in."
"Every core described reports in; the count is judged by stage 4's line in main.rs, product code."
"user_hwcaps shall give a program the AT_HWCAP and AT_HWCAP2 bits arch/arm64 gives for what ID_AA64PFR0_EL1, ID_AA64ISAR0_EL1 and ID_AA64ISAR1_EL1 say the core has, and user_platform none."
"The mapping is ferrix-linux-abi's hwcap, host-tested against Linux's bits; that the registers read here reach it is not checked on the machine."

children.name: Speculation
children.doc: src/kernel/src/arch/aarch64/speculation.rs: what each core needs against Spectre v2, Spectre-BHB, Meltdown and speculative store bypass, from its own identification registers and Arm's lists, what firmware is asked, what is applied and read back, and the index clamp at the system call boundary.

children.value: "A core shall be given the Spectre-BHB loop count, the Spectre v2 safe listing, the Meltdown safe listing and the in-order classification Linux's proton-pack.c and cpufeature.c give its part, none of Arm's listings to a core another company designed, and no loop to a core whose branch history is not shared."
"Each of the check's 12 cores -- ten of Arm's parts, one with ECBHB, one of Qualcomm's -- is given the figures listed for it, and the ECBHB core is reported unaffected by Spectre-BHB."
"An SMCCC_ARCH_FEATURES status shall be read as ARM DEN 0028D defines it -- 0 required, 1 not required, -2 always on, anything else not supported -- and shall survive the record it is packed into."
"Each of the five statuses the check tries is read as listed and comes back from its bits unchanged."

"Each processor shall decide its defences from its core and firmware's answers, apply them, record what it saw and applied, and the vector entry's branch history loop shall run exactly when some processor recorded that it needs it."
"After every processor has started, the loop's count is non-zero exactly when a processor's record holds the loop."

"apply shall clear SCTLR_EL1.DSSBS and PSTATE.SSBS on a core that needs the store bypass defence and has them, read back what can be read, and say what took; firmware's workaround 1 shall be asked on each switch only by a core whose plan holds it."
"The speculation report names each kind of core and what was applied; QEMU's max CPU needs none of them, and a check that a cleared DSSBS reads back cleared on a core that has it is not written."

"switch_barrier_in_domain shall issue nothing: this architecture's switch barrier is ARCH_WORKAROUND_1, the predictor invalidation a speculation domain leaves out, and the Spectre-BHB loop on entry from EL0 is not on the switch path."
"Switches between two members of one marked job decide no barrier and switches out of the domain decide one each way (the `domain` line on an AArch64 boot)."
"clamp_index and clamp_below shall answer an index below its bound unchanged and any other as zero, with a csel and a csdb so that no later instruction uses a predicted result."
"The generic speculation check requires the clamp on every architecture (arch/speculation_check.rs), whose criterion is the clamp's result, not this instruction sequence."

children.name: Firmware
children.doc: What firmware is asked for: power off and reset through PSCI, the Pixel 7's watchdogs fed, and entropy from its TRNG through SMCCC (trng.rs) or the core's RNDR.

children.value: "fill_from shall fill its buffer from TRNG_RND64 192 bits at a time, each call's x3 then x2 then x1 as little-endian bytes, asking again at most ATTEMPTS times while firmware reports none ready, and shall stop at the bytes already taken when a call fails."

"Against scripted firmware: 40 bytes are taken over three calls, the first finding nothing ready, in that order; a failure on the second call leaves 24 bytes taken and the rest untouched; a firmware never ready is asked 8 times and gives 0 bytes."

"offers_rnd64 shall ask TRNG_RND64 only of firmware that reports PSCI 1.0 or later, answers SMCCC_VERSION through PSCI_FEATURES, reports SMCCC 1.1 or later and TRNG 1.0 or later, and offers TRNG_RND64 through TRNG_FEATURES."
"Five scripted firmwares -- PSCI 0.2, no SMCCC, SMCCC 1.0, no TRNG, no TRNG_RND64 -- each give 0 bytes and are asked no TRNG_RND64."

"firmware_entropy shall ask the TRNG through the conduit the machine describes PSCI on, and give 0 bytes where it describes none; hardware_random shall give a word only from a core ID_AA64ISAR0_EL1 says has RNDR, and only one RNDR reports valid within ten tries."
"The crosvm guest's boot seeds 48 bytes from its TRNG (~/.local/share/ferrix/pixel7/vm-20260926-140648) and QEMU's 0; neither is a check, and RNDR is not asserted."
"shutdown and reset shall drain the console and then ask PSCI for SYSTEM_OFF or SYSTEM_RESET, powering off where reset returns and halting where power-off returns."
"Every gate's QEMU exits when the boot powers off, and boot-reset's ferrix.onexit=reset is x86-64's; a reset on this architecture is not asserted."

"init_watchdogs shall feed once every watchdog the device tree lists that firmware left running, and start_watchdogs shall start the task that keeps feeding them, and nothing where the tree lists none."
"The Pixel 7 runs past its watchdogs' timeout; QEMU's tree lists none. Not a check."

"mmio's read8, read16 and read32 shall each be one ldrb, ldrh or ldr, and write8, write16 and write32 one strb, strh or str, with a bare base register and no writeback, so that a hypervisor can emulate the access from its fault's syndrome."

"No check can fail without it on the machines the suite boots: QEMU's TCG emulates any load or store. The Pixel 7's crosvm guest is the evidence: with read_volatile, LLVM made stage 10's DMA switch check a pre-indexed ldrh, KVM_RUN failed with ENOSYS and the guest stopped with neither boot marker; with these, it boots to init."

"system_call shall ask the registered filter about a call before rt_sigreturn is answered and before the dispatcher is, with x8's low 32 bits, ELR as the instruction after the svc and AArch64's token, apply the filter's errno as the dispatcher's answer, and syscall_rollback_value shall give x0 the call's first argument so that a call that did not run reads as it did at the call."
"A test-only filter is shown rt_sigreturn once, before its answer, and its value comes back in x0 (the `seccomp` line)."

children.name: Claims
children.doc: src/kernel/src/claim.rs: a device claimed through a core's control channel, which a quiesce waits out, and the numbers the cores' nodes are published under.

children.value: "Claims::claim shall record a claim of a node nobody holds, and refuse a second claim of it while the first stands."
"A published node nobody holds is claimed, and a second claim of it is refused."
"Claims::claim_up_to shall record up to its limit of claims of one node, each through its own channel, and refuse one more."
"At a limit of 2, two claims of one node through two channels are recorded and a third is refused."
"Claims::wait_until_released shall answer ByADriver, at once, while any driver end a node is claimed through is still open."
"With a node claimed through two channels, one driver end closed and the other open, the wait answers ByADriver."
"A wait for a node whose drivers have gone shall answer Ok once no claim of it stands, whether its release came before the wait began or while the wait was parked."
"A wait begun after the node's release ends Ok at once, and a wait parked on a node released by another task once the wait is blocked ends Ok."
"A wait for a node still claimed shall answer Waiting when its caller is cancelled."
"A wait on a node whose driver end has closed and whose claim stands, cancelled, answers Waiting; after the release, the same wait answers Ok."
"A wait for a node still claimed shall answer Waiting when its patience runs out."
"A wait of 10 ms on a node whose driver end has closed and whose claim stands answers Waiting."
"Claims::release_one shall let go only the claim made through its channel, leaving the node's others standing."
"Of a node's two claims, one let go leaves the node waited for under the other's driver; the other let go frees it."
"A claim, or a node's number, with no memory to record it shall be refused and record nothing."
"With the one allocation of a claim refused, the claim is refused and the next, with memory, is recorded; with the one allocation of a number refused, none is taken and the next is the first."
"Numbers::take shall give the lowest number from the first nothing holds, and a number given back shall be the next taken."
"From 7, two numbers taken are 7 and 8; 7 given back is the next taken."

children.name: Nodes
children.doc: src/kernel/src/device.rs: the apertures and vectors a node hands out, the nodes published, and the bus mastering a node's DMA is switched with.

children.value: "DeviceNode::mint shall withhold, and count, an aperture that overlaps memory the kernel uses, so that no published aperture does."
"Every aperture of every published node is clear of every reserved range."
"DeviceNode::aperture shall grant a range only when it lies inside one of the node's apertures, and none of length 0 or past the address space's end."

"For every published aperture: the whole is granted, and its last byte; a range one byte past its end, one ending before its start by a byte, one of length 0 and one wrapping the address space are refused."
"DeviceNode::pci shall keep a function's MSI-X table and pending-bit pages out of every aperture it grants."
"For every published PCI function, the whole of each MSI-X table or pending-bit range, its first byte and its last byte are refused."
"DeviceNode::vector shall hand out a node's recorded vectors as recorded, and none past its count."
"For every published node without MSI-X, each index below the count answers its recorded vector and the count itself answers none."

"publish shall take from a later node an aperture an earlier one holds, so that no two published nodes' apertures overlap, and publish no device tree vector that is not a shared peripheral interrupt or that two nodes hold."
"Sorted by start, no two published apertures overlap; every device tree vector is 32 or above and held by one node."
"MsixTable::mint shall mint an entry once and answer the same vector when asked again, never on a number that has a handler, and none past the table."
"On the first published MSI-X table, entry 0 minted twice is one vector, its number has no handler, and the entry at the table's size is refused."
"A minted MSI-X entry shall be masked until unmasked, and shall read back masked or unmasked as it was last told."
"The first published MSI-X table's minted entry 0 reads masked; unmasked it reads unmasked, masked again it reads masked."
"DeviceNode::domain shall make a node's domain once and answer that one domain afterwards."
"Every published node asked for its domain twice answers one domain."
"enable_dma shall set a PCI function's bus mastering and memory decoding, and disable_dma shall clear its bus mastering and keep its memory decoding."
"On the first published function with a configuration space, its command register reads bus mastering and decoding on after enable_dma, and bus mastering off with decoding on after disable_dma."
"DeviceNode::describe shall report a PCI function's location, identity, aperture and vector counts and virtio placement as the node holds them."
"For the first published PCI function, device_info's location, vendor and device, counts and virtio blocks agree with the node and with enumeration."
"A node's failure shall read as its location -- a PCI function's address, a device tree node's registers -- and what it did."
"A failure of a PCI function, a virtio,mmio node and a device tree node reads as the address or registers and the sentence."
"DeviceNode::reads_log shall allow the kernel log to no node but a GS201's DWC3."
"A published node of another binding asking for the kernel log is refused."
"board_clock shall answer no clock for a node whose board keeps none for it."
"A clock asked of a published node whose board keeps none is refused."
"Reserved::of shall reserve the framebuffer, every memory-map region but MMIO, the ECAM windows, the kernel's device windows, every IOMMU unit's registers and, without ACPI, the device tree console."
"Each of those ranges on the booted machine is covered by the reserved set."
"A function's host-visible window shall be taken only from an assigned memory BAR it fits, in whole pages, clear of reserved memory."
"A window from a BAR that is not assigned, does not fit, is not whole pages or overlaps reserved memory is refused, and one that is all four is taken."
"MsixTable::of shall find a function's MSI-X table only inside an assigned memory BAR, clear of reserved memory."
"A table in an unassigned BAR, past its BAR or overlapping reserved memory is not found."
"A PCI function's legacy interrupt shall be one controller vector with its firmware trigger, on a line of 32 or above that no kernel handler holds and no other function took."
"Two functions offered one line give it to the first; a line below 32 or with a handler is given to neither."

"The device tree's and the boards' finders shall publish a device tree node only with registers clear of reserved memory and an interrupt no other node or handler holds, and leave it alone, saying why, otherwise."
"A board node whose registers overlap reserved memory, or whose interrupt is taken, is left alone and named on the console; one clear of both is published."
"DeviceNode::describe shall report a device tree node as not PCI, with its binding and its first two apertures."
"A published virtio,mmio or board node's device_info names no PCI location, its binding, and its apertures 0 and 1."
"An MSI-X vector shall be minted, masked or unmasked only for a published node."
"A node not in the published list asked for an MSI-X vector answers none, and a vector naming one refuses to mask."
"DeviceNode::input_functions shall allow eight input claims of an STM32 USB host's node, and one of every other."
"An STM32 USB host's node answers 8 and a PCI function answers 1."

"A PCI function with an MSI capability and no MSI-X table shall be offered one vector, minted once with INTx off -- written under the node's command-register lock, which bus mastering's writes take too (L.object.117) -- and the message masked, none past the one message, and no vector allocated for a 32-bit capability the architecture's message address is above."

"On x86-64 test-boot requires the devices line's 1 vectors minted and 2 deliveries: QEMU's edu device's vector 0 minted twice is one vector with no handler on its number, vector 1 is refused, it reads masked as minted and as told, the command register reads INTx off, and edu's raised interrupt arrives twice unmasked and not while masked. Without edu on the machine, or with the INTx write skipped, the boot fails."

"An MSI message shall be programmed with MSI off while its registers are written, at the offsets its capability's address width puts them, and left masked: by its mask bit, with MSI on, where the function can mask its vector, and by MSI Enable otherwise; masking, unmasking and reading back use the same bit."

"Host tests: a maskable 32-bit capability is programmed with its data at +8, its mask bit set and MSI on, and is masked and unmasked by the mask bit with Enable untouched; a non-maskable 64-bit one gets both address halves, its data at +0xC and MSI off, and is masked and unmasked by Enable; one message is enabled whatever the function could use. With the two paths swapped the tests fail."

"device_aperture shall report each of a device's apertures with the address, length, BAR, offset in that BAR and flags it was minted with, whole however far past 4 GiB, and refuse an index past them with INVALID_ARGS; DeviceInfo shall keep its 96 bytes."

"Every aperture of every published node is answered as minted, the index past the last INVALID_ARGS, and on x86-64 pci-testdev's 8 GiB 64-bit BAR above 4 GiB is answered whole (the first config line's 1 above 4 GiB, which xtask requires). With the length cut to 32 bits the boot fails."

"A driver's configuration write touching any byte outside its function's writable ranges shall be refused whole with ACCESS_DENIED and change nothing, and a malformed access shall be INVALID_ARGS; reads of the function's configuration space shall be answered; and a node whose kernel-owned registers read back other than the kernel made them, at an accepted HELLO or a quiesce, shall have its bus mastering turned off and be refused in one hold of its configuration lock, every call needing MANAGE on it answering BAD_STATE, and its bus mastering never turned on again."

"Header reads answer what enumeration read, and the MSI, MSI-X and extended reads are answered; writes to the command register, a BAR, the MSI and MSI-X capabilities, Device Control, an uncovered byte and ATS where present are refused and read back unchanged; a write spanning a kernel-owned and a writable byte is refused; malformed accesses are INVALID_ARGS; a command register rewritten behind the kernel is found, bus mastering reads off, the node answers BAD_STATE, the line names COMMAND, and an enable_dma after it is refused with bus mastering still off (the config lines). With the allowlist widened, the whole-range test reduced to one byte, verify_config not comparing, or the refused node's enable_dma let through, the boot fails."

"A function's driver-writable configuration bytes shall be the bodies of its vendor-specific capabilities, a standard one past its three-byte header and a VSEC past its eight, cut at the end of their space, less virtio's pci_cfg_data, computed at stage 10 from both capability lists; a list that loops, holds a capability starting inside a vendor body, or holds more capabilities or vendor bodies than the walk records, shall leave the function nothing writable."

"ferrix_pci::window's host tests: the header, MSI, power management, PCI Express, MSI-X, ATS, AER and uncovered bytes are refused and vendor bodies writable; pci_cfg_data is refused and virtio's bar, offset and length writable; a body past its space is cut; overlapping and looping lists, 65 VSECs and an extended list past 304 capabilities leave nothing writable. With the extended list skipped the VSEC test fails. At boot virtio-rng's offset field is written and read back and its pci_cfg_data refused (the second config line)."

"description::of shall read a machine by its ACPI tables when they open, whether or not a device tree came too, by its device tree when the tables do not open and the tree parses, and by neither otherwise; and shall not parse the tree when the tables open."
"For ACPI only, both, tables that fail to open beside a tree, a tree only, and neither, the description is ACPI, ACPI with the tree unopened, the tree, the tree and neither."

children.name: Quiesce
children.doc: The quiesce in src/kernel/src/syscall/native.rs: every core that serves a device waited out, its DMA turned off, and the claims a core keeps past its driver let go, before the next driver is given it.

children.value: "device_quiesce shall be refused with ACCESS_DENIED through a device handle without MANAGE."
"A quiesce through a handle to the device without MANAGE answers ACCESS_DENIED."
"A quiesce shall answer BAD_STATE, changing nothing, while a driver serves the device."
"A quiesce of the device a running driver serves answers BAD_STATE, and the driver goes on serving it."
"A quiesce made as a driver dies shall wait for every core serving the device to let go, turn the device's DMA off, let go the claims a core keeps past its driver, and answer success."
"A quiesce the instant a block driver's handles close answers success, and the next driver is given a ring on the device."
"The kernel shall quiesce every device a dead devmgr's drivers served before a devmgr started again is handed them."
"Restarting devmgr.service starts a second devmgr, which is given the devices and starts their drivers."
"A quiesce whose device a core has not let go within its patience shall answer TIMED_OUT, and one whose DMA cannot be turned off BAD_STATE."
"A quiesce with a core that never lets go answers TIMED_OUT; one on a function whose configuration space cannot be mapped answers BAD_STATE."

children.name: IsolatedInterrupts
children.doc: NVIDIA's N0g (docs/NVIDIA.md section 12.3, condition G5): the isolated-interrupts mark, device_isolation, and no vector for a function whose messages arrive under another's source ID.

children.value: "device_set_limit's DEVICE_LIMIT_ISOLATED_INTERRUPTS shall set a node's isolated-interrupts mark through a handle with SET_LIMIT, and a value that would clear a set mark shall be refused ACCESS_DENIED; nothing else shall clear it. While a node's mark is set and its interrupts are not isolated, interrupt_create and vmo_pin shall be refused ACCESS_DENIED. device_isolation shall answer bit 0 for a translated domain and bit 1 for isolated interrupts. devmgr shall start no driver of a device that runs firmware of its own whose mark the kernel refused."

"On x86-64 check R10 sets edu's mark, reads device_isolation 0x3, is given a vector, is refused one ACCESS_DENIED while the machine's interrupts are forced not isolated, and is refused clearing the mark; with the refusal skipped R10 panics. devmgr-proto's host tests: a firmware device starts only once marked, with its line when refused; with the refusal ignored they fail."

"While a unit remaps, a function the remapping units do not place as its own requester -- behind no unit, or under a bridge's alias -- shall be given no message route, and so no vector, and the boot shall name each such function."
"On x86-64 a requester no unit places is refused a route (the remap line); with the refusal turned into a compatibility route the boot panics."

"system_call shall ask the registered filter about a call before set_tls, sigreturn and rt_sigreturn are answered and before the dispatcher is, with r7 as the number, the saved pc as the instruction after the svc, ARM or Thumb, and ARMv7-A's token, and shall apply the filter's answer as the dispatcher's; with nothing registered, set_tls and the signal returns shall be answered as they were before the filter existed."

"A test-only filter is shown set_tls, sigreturn and rt_sigreturn once each, before their answers, with the number, the instruction pointer and the first argument the frame held, and its errno comes back in r0 (the `seccomp` line)."

"audit_arch shall give the token of the entry a call was made through, AUDIT_ARCH_ARM for the svc, and syscall_rollback_value shall give r0 the call's first argument so that a call that did not run reads as it did at the call, r7 still holding the number."
"The value for first argument 0x1111 is 0x1111 and the token read back from a driven svc is ARMv7-A's, 0x40000028 (the `seccomp` line)."

"switch_barrier_in_domain shall issue nothing: this architecture's switch barrier is BPIALL, or ICIALLU with ACTLR.IBE, the predictor invalidation a speculation domain leaves out, and no defence of the kernel is on the switch path."
"Switches between two members of one marked job decide no barrier and switches out of the domain decide one each way (the `domain` line on an ARMv7-A boot)."

children.name: Processors
children.doc: The processors firmware describes, the record each is given, and how code finds the record of the processor it runs on.

children.value: "Topology::from_described shall refuse a processor list that is empty, that names one hardware identifier twice, or that does not name the processor running it."

"Described lists that are empty, that hold one identifier twice and that omit the boot processor's identifier are each refused with its own error, 0 accepted; a list of 4 distinct identifiers including the boot one is accepted."

"Topology::from_described shall give the boot processor logical number 0 and the others 1 to N-1 in table order, one record each that holds its own address, with only the boot processor's record online."

"A described list of 4 identifiers whose boot identifier is third yields 4 records, the boot identifier's at index 0 and the other three at 1 to 3 in table order, each record's own address in its first word, and 1 online."
"On every processor that has installed its record, this_cpu shall return the record that names that processor's hardware identifier."

"In 100 rounds of work run on every online processor at once, each processor runs each round once and the record this_cpu gives it names its own hardware identifier every time: 0 misplaced runs (the `smp` line)."
"this_cpu shall return nothing until the boot processor has installed its record, and shall not read the per-processor register before then."
"Called before discover, this_cpu returns None with the register holding a value that is no record's address; after discover it returns the boot processor's record."

"discover and secondary_main shall halt a processor whose register does not lead to its own record, whose record does not hold its own address or lead back to itself by its logical number, or names another processor's hardware identifier; and a secondary that arrives with an address that is no processor's record shall halt."

"A secondary started with another processor's record address, and one started with an address that is no record's, each end the boot in their catalogued panic (FX-0405, FX-0404); a boot processor record made to name another hardware identifier ends the boot in FX-0401."

"this_cpu_for_report shall name the processor whose record's address the register holds, and otherwise say that the processor has not installed a record or that no other processor was started, without following the register."

"With the register holding a processor's record address the report names that processor; holding any other value, it answers with the no-record sentence; before discover, with the boot-processor sentence; 0 reads through the register's value."

children.name: BringUp
children.doc: Starting the secondaries, and what each does as it arrives: the handshakes that let a shootdown or a grace period racing its arrival cover it, and the wait for work until the scheduler takes the processor over.

children.value: "start_secondaries shall start every processor the topology lists but the boot one, one at a time, each on a kernel stack of its own, and shall return only once each has reported itself online."
"On each configuration `cargo xtask test-boot` boots, the `cpus` line counts as many processors online as firmware described (4 of 4 on x86-64 and AArch64, 2 of 2 on ARMv7-A at `--smp 2`)."
"start_secondaries shall fail, and leave the architecture's start block in place, when a processor it started has not reported itself online within one second."
"A secondary made never to set its online flag ends the boot in FX-0402 with the never-reported-in sentence 1 s or more after it was started, and the start block is not freed."
"start_secondaries shall apply the side-channel defences on the boot processor before it starts any other processor, on a machine with one processor as well."
"The boot processor's speculation controls read back as decided before the first secondary's start is requested, on each architecture, and with `--smp 1`."
"start_secondaries shall register the inter-processor interrupt's handler before any secondary starts, and shall fail if another handler holds its line."
"0 inter-processor interrupts are counted unclaimed across a boot; with the line registered beforehand, start_secondaries fails with the line-taken sentence and starts no processor."
"A secondary waiting in secondary_main shall take an inter-processor interrupt sent to it, count it, and look for work when it returns."
"In 100 rounds of work handed to every online processor, each processor runs each round once and every secondary takes 1 or more inter-processor interrupts (the `smp` line)."

"secondary_main shall mark its processor online before it reads the shootdown generation, and flush its TLB after, so that a shootdown racing its arrival either waits for it or is covered by that flush; and shall answer every grace period requested before it came online."

"A secondary held between reading the generation and flushing while a shootdown is taken reads, once let go, the translation the shootdown changed; a grace period requested before it came online completes without its interrupt."
"Once the scheduler has started, secondary_main shall hand its processor to the scheduler's idle loop and not return to waiting for work."
"After sched::init, tasks pinned one to each online processor all run, each on its own processor: N of N."

children.name: Shootdown
children.doc: Dropping stale translations from every processor's TLB: the whole-TLB shootdown, the turn that keeps shootdowns one at a time, the wait for every processor's answer and its bound. The Arm pair invalidates by broadcast in hardware, so the waits here are x86-64's.

children.value: "When flush_tlb_everywhere returns, no online processor shall still translate through an entry it held before it was called."

"Over 20 rounds in which every online processor reads a kernel page and the page is then moved to another frame, every processor reads the page's new value each round: 0 stale reads (the `tlb` line), on each architecture."
"take_turn shall let one shootdown hold the turn at a time, and a processor waiting for it shall answer the shootdowns of others while it waits."

"Two processors each requesting a shootdown while a third holds the turn both complete once it is let go, one after the other: 0 generations taken by two holders at once, and 0 waits for the turn ending in FX-0001."
"Where invalidation is not broadcast, a task waiting for the shootdown turn shall answer shootdowns for the processor it is running on at each moment, never for one it has left."

"On x86-64 with 3 or more processors online, a task waiting for the turn that moves to another processor answers a generation requested with no interrupt on the processor it moved to, and the processor it left is not recorded as answering (the `migrate` line)."
"wait_for shall stop the kernel in the safe state, naming the processor, once its wall-clock bound has passed and it has asked patience's count of polls, and not before both."
"A processor made to stop answering its interrupt ends the boot in FX-0001 naming it, after 1 s or more and 16,777,216 polls or more, under tcg and under KVM."

"take_turn shall stop the kernel in the safe state when the shootdown generation has stood still for 4 s and patience's count of polls while it waits for the turn, and shall start its count again whenever the generation moves."
"A holder made to stop with the turn in hand ends the boot in FX-0003 after 4 s or more; a holder that keeps taking generations for longer than that is waited for."
"wait_for shall send its interrupt again every 10 ms while a processor it waits for has not answered."
"With a processor's first interrupt dropped, the shootdown still completes, the processor answering the second."
"A shootdown shall be refused with a diagnostic when it is requested holding a lock that disables preemption, or, once tasks run, when it would wait for another processor with interrupts masked."

"A shootdown requested holding a SpinLock, and one that would wait for another processor with interrupts masked, each stop the kernel with the assertion naming the rule, in a build with debug assertions."

"service_tlb shall flush the whole TLB of a processor more than one generation behind, or whose generation's request is not a scoped one or was rewritten while it was read, and shall record the latest generation answered without taking back a later one."

"A processor two generations behind, one a generation behind a whole-TLB request, and one reading a scoped request whose generation changes under the read each flush the whole TLB; tlb_seen after each is the latest generation, never less than a value recorded meanwhile."

children.name: ScopedShootdown
children.doc: The shootdown for a change to one address space: the pages that changed, on the processors that may hold that space's translations, and the page tables it gives back afterwards (finding F-36). The mask an address space keeps of those processors is here too.

children.value: "scoped_request shall give a processor in a scoped request's set that request's pages, or the whole TLB where it asks for more than the ceiling, and a processor outside the set nothing to invalidate."
"For a request of 3 pages to processors 1 and 3, processor 1 is given the 3 pages and processor 2 none; for a request of the whole TLB, a member is given everything."
"flush_tlb_pages shall invalidate the pages it names on the online processors in its set other than the one it runs on before it returns."

"On a machine with two processors or more, a child that wrote a shared page and holds still on its processor has the page protected read-only from this one, whose scoped shootdown names the child's processor: the child's next write ends it with SIGSEGV, 11, instead of answering (the `rmap` line), on each architecture."
"flush_tlb_pages shall give back every page table its pages hold once its invalidation has returned, and none before it is called."
"Of the tables an unmap_in emptied, 0 are given back before flush_tlb_pages is called and every one is given back by it, its list left empty, with an empty set of processors."

"invalidate_pages shall interrupt no processor when there is nothing to invalidate, when its set is empty, before the processors are discovered, when this processor is the only one online or where invalidation is broadcast, and shall invalidate the pages on this processor itself in the last three."

"Each of those five calls raises the unsent count by 1 or leaves it (nothing to invalidate) and sends 0 interrupts; after the last three a translation of the named page cached before is gone on this processor."

"A TlbPages shall list each page asked for once, up to 33 pages, ask for the whole TLB past that, and when merged with another shall list both sets' pages once each and ask for the whole TLB if either did."

"33 pages added by range and one again by an address inside it list 33 pages; 34 by range ask for everything; two sets of 1 and 2 pages sharing one merge to 2 pages in order; a merge with a set asking for everything asks for everything."
"A CpuMask's snapshot shall hold every processor that joined it and has not left since."
"A mask joined by processors 0 and 3 and left by 0 snapshots as 3 alone."
"add_cpus shall add every processor of one set to another and remove none."
"{0, 2} added to {1, 2} gives {0, 1, 2}; the empty set added changes nothing."

children.name: GracePeriods
children.doc: Read-side sections and the wait for every one of them to end: what lets a writer free an object it has unpublished. Nothing in the product calls synchronize yet (src/kernel/src/irq.rs names the handler unregistration it is for); stage 4's grace check does.

children.value: "synchronize shall return only once every online processor has been outside a read-side section since it was called."

"A writer that replaces an object every other online processor is reading in read_section, synchronizes and poisons the replaced one, 100 times over, leaves 0 reads of a poisoned object among more than 0 reads (the `grace` line)."

children.name: Stopping
children.doc: What a panic asks of the other processors, and where they look.

children.value: "stop_others shall set the stop request and interrupt every other online processor, and return how many it asked: none before the processors are discovered."
"A panic on one of N online processors reports N-1 asked (the `stopped` line), and 0 before discovery."

"Once a panic has asked every processor to stop, a processor shall halt on its next inter-processor interrupt, and on its next poll while it waits for the shootdown turn or for other processors' answers."

"With a panic on one processor while the others are idle, waiting for the turn and waiting for answers, each other processor halts: 0 lines printed and 0 shootdowns completed by them after the report begins."

children.name: Kick
children.doc: The interrupt the scheduler sends a processor it has given work.

children.value: "interrupt_one shall interrupt the online processor it names, and every other processor where the architecture cannot address it alone, where that processor is not online, or before the processors are known."
"On x86-64 a kick to processor 2 raises its inter-processor interrupt count by 1 and the others' by 0; a kick to a processor that is not online raises every other online processor's."

children.name: Lines
children.doc: The kernel's own lines, from println! to the port.

children.value: "write_as, emit and drain shall send nothing to the port, and record nothing in the kernel log, the recent-output ring or the screen, until mark_ready has said the port is configured."
"A line and a program's write made before mark_ready leave the port untouched and the kernel log's and the recent-output ring's counts where they were; the same made after it raise both."
"write_as shall put a formatted line into the transmit ring or the port under one hold of the port's lock, each bare newline as CRLF, so that no other writer's bytes fall inside it."
"1,000 lines of 200 bytes printed from every processor at once reach the port each whole and ending in CRLF: 0 lines with another writer's bytes inside."

"A writer that may not queue -- the port's interrupt not installed, its processor's interrupts masked, or a failure report begun -- shall first poll out everything the transmit ring holds, then write its own bytes straight to the port."
"With bytes queued in the transmit ring, a line printed with interrupts masked reaches the port after every one of them, and the ring is empty when the print returns."

children.name: ProgramOutput
children.doc: A program's bytes, through write_bytes and write_raw, and the transmit ring a writer queues them into.

children.value: "emit shall send a program's bytes to the port in the order given, each bare newline as CRLF for write_bytes and every byte as it is for write_raw."
"A write_bytes of text holding bare newlines, and a write_raw of the same, reach the port with CRLF for each newline in the first and LF alone in the second, every other byte the same and in order."

"emit shall send a program's bytes through write_waiting only from a task that may sleep, and otherwise queue them without waiting, Transmit::queue polling the oldest queued byte out to the port to make room when the ring is full."
"A program's write made with a spin lock held returns without sleeping and its line reaches the port; with the ring full, each byte it queues sends one queued byte first and counts it as polled."

"write_waiting shall queue a task's write only when the ring has room for the whole of the next chunk, and otherwise sleep until the ring drains to half or a tenth of a second passes, never polling out bytes other writers queued."

"A task writing 16 KiB to a port that sends slower than it writes sleeps at least once, the ring never holds more than 4,096 bytes, 0 bytes are polled out by it, and every byte reaches the port in order."

"next_chunk shall take the whole of what is left when it costs at most 2,048 bytes on the wire, a newline sent as CRLF costing two; otherwise the longest part within that cost that ends in a newline, or failing one the longest part within it."

"What is left of 100 bytes is taken whole; of 3,000 bytes with newlines at the 1,000th and 2,500th, the first 1,000; of 3,000 bytes with none, 2,048; with CRLF asked for, each newline counted as 2 in the cost."
"try_queue shall record a chunk in the kernel log once, when it is queued, and never for a try that found no room."
"A task's write that finds the ring without room twice before it is queued appears in the kernel log exactly once."
"Transmit::pump shall give the port no more than it reports room for and no more than 64 bytes, never waiting for room, and charge them to the count of whoever pumped."
"A task's line of 172 bytes on the wire, written on a port with an interrupt, has all but at most 64 of them sent by the transmit interrupt (the `output` line)."

"The port's interrupt shall give the port what it has room for of the transmit ring, and settle shall keep the port's transmit interrupt enabled exactly while the ring holds bytes, so that what a writer left is sent with no further write."
"A task's write left in the ring is sent within 2 seconds with no further write and 0 stalls polled out (the `output` line)."
"settle shall ask for waiting writers to be woken when the ring drains from above half its length to half or less, and a writer shall wake them only after it has dropped the port's lock."
"A task waiting for room in a full ring is woken once the ring holds 2,048 bytes or fewer, and not while it holds more."
"unstall shall poll the transmit ring out to the port, and count a stall, when the port has taken none of its bytes for a tenth of a second."
"With the port's transmit interrupt suppressed, a line queued reaches the port at the first write made after 100 ms, and the stall count rises by 1."
"drain shall poll out everything the transmit ring holds and then wait for the port to have sent it before it returns."
"A line printed just before drain and a power off reaches the port whole, on each architecture, 3 of 3."

children.name: FailureReports
children.doc: Writing once begin_panic has been called, and the recent-output ring a panic screen and the screen console draw.

children.value: "Once begin_panic has been called, write_as shall write through write_panicking, which, when it gets the port's lock, sends the line straight to the port."
"A boot told to panic at its end (`ferrix.onexit=panic`) shows the FX-1501 line on the port after init's exit (`cargo xtask test-init-file`)."
"write_panicking shall try the port's lock at most 10,000,000 times and then send the line straight to the port without it, recorded in the kernel log if asked, leaving what was queued in the ring."
"A report written while another context holds the port's lock for good reaches the port whole after at most 10,000,000 attempts, and is in the kernel log."
"During a failure report, drain shall try the port's lock at most 10,000,000 times, leave the ring as it is if it never gets it, and wait for the port either way."
"drain called during a report while another context holds the port's lock for good returns after at most 10,000,000 attempts, having waited for the port to empty."
"recent shall give back, oldest byte first, the most recent bytes of the kernel's own lines as they were printed."
"A line printed is found as printed, its newline without the CR, in the last 1,024 bytes recent copies out."
"Writer::bytes shall keep a kernel line, logged or not, in the recent-output ring and on the screen console, and a program's output in neither."
"After a program's write of a marker line and a kernel line, the last 4,096 bytes recent gives hold the kernel line and not the marker."
"recent shall copy at most its buffer's length and at most the 4,096 bytes the ring keeps, and a writer racing it shall leave a byte stale at worst."

"recent into a 16-byte buffer copies 16 bytes; into an 8,192-byte buffer after 10,000 bytes printed, 4,096, the last printed; with another processor printing throughout, every copy stays within those bounds."

children.name: Input
children.doc: What the port receives, between its interrupt and the reader.

children.value: "receive shall move what the port gives into the receive ring in order, dropping and counting every byte that finds it full, and pop and has_input shall give the reader those bytes in order and say without a lock whether any are held."

"4,099 bytes offered to the empty ring come back as the first 4,096 in order, a 4,097th pop finds nothing, has_input says so before and after, and the overrun count rises by exactly 3 (the `input` line)."
"receive shall wake the input's waiters, after it has dropped the ring's lock, whenever it added a byte."
"A task waiting for input with the ring empty is woken by the first byte the port receives, within the interrupt that took it."

"receive shall take at most 8,192 bytes from the port per call, and on_interrupt shall make at most 68 passes of receiving and transmitting, stopping at the first the port says nothing is pending after."
"A port that never reports itself empty lets the handler return after 68 passes of at most 8,192 received bytes each; a port with nothing pending after the first pass, after 1."

"init shall register the port's receive interrupt and mark input and output interrupt-driven before it enables the line; answer None, installing nothing, when the machine gives the port no interrupt this kernel can take; and refuse when the interrupt is already held."

"On QEMU's x86-64, AArch64 and ARMv7-A machines the `input` line says the port receives by an interrupt; a second init of the same number is refused with nothing changed; a machine whose port has no interrupt leaves input polled."
"read_byte shall take from the receive ring once the receive interrupt is installed, and poll the port only until then."
"Before init a byte comes through the poll; after it, a byte received by interrupt comes through the ring and the poll is called 0 times."

children.name: Log
children.doc: The kernel log: what it records, what it promises a reader, and what it keeps out.

children.value: "Ring::record shall claim exactly one place per byte, so that the ring's count of bytes recorded is exact however many writers race."
"Two writers recording 20,000 bytes each at once, on two processors where there are two, leave the ring's count at exactly 40,000."
"A ring of N bytes written past its length shall keep its last N - 1 bytes in order, and unread shall count exactly those for a reader at its start."
"A 64-byte ring given 100 bytes answers unread 63 for a cursor at 0, and its reads from there give the last 63 bytes in order."
"read shall move a cursor behind the oldest byte kept up to it and report exactly the bytes it skipped as lost."
"A reader at 0 of a 64-byte ring given 100 bytes is told 37 lost; caught up and then 200 bytes behind, it is told 137 lost and given the 63 kept."
"read shall copy no more than the reader's buffer holds and move the cursor past exactly what it copied, so that the next read goes on from there."
"A 10-byte read with 63 unread leaves 53 unread, and the next read gives those 53 in order with 0 lost and 0 left unread."
"read shall hand a reader only bytes writers recorded, dropping and counting as lost any a writer replaced while they were being copied, so that every byte recorded is either read or counted lost."
"While two writers record 20,000 bytes each into a 256-byte ring, a reader reading 97 bytes at a time reads only bytes they wrote, and the bytes it read and was told it lost come to exactly 40,000."
"read shall bring a cursor ahead of the newest byte back to it, copying nothing and reporting nothing lost."
"A read at a cursor 1,000 past the ring's count copies 0 bytes, reports 0 lost and leaves the cursor at the count."
"A task's write to the console shall be recorded in the kernel log as the task wrote it, without the CR the port is sent."
"A task's write of a line is found, byte for byte and with no CR, in the last 4,096 bytes of the kernel log."
"write_panicking, asked to log, shall record the line in the kernel log when it writes it under the port's lock."
"A line written through write_panicking with logging asked for, the panicking flag not set, is found in the last 4,096 bytes of the kernel log."
"write shall record a kernel line in the kernel log as printed, before its newline becomes CRLF."
"A line printed with println! is found, without a CR, in the last 4,096 bytes of the kernel log."
"write_unlogged shall keep its line out of the kernel log."
"A line sent with println_unlogged! is not in the last 4,096 bytes of the kernel log, read after it was sent."
"record shall take no lock, allocate nothing and wake no reader, so that a writer recording in any context, a panic's included, is never held up by the log."

"A byte recorded from an interrupt handler, from the idle task and from a failure report written while another processor holds every lock the kernel has is recorded, with 0 heap allocations and 0 wakes."

children.name: Screen
children.doc: The boot console drawn on the framebuffer firmware left, which a machine whose port is out of reach -- the Pixel 7 -- shows until a panic draws its own screen over it.

children.value: "screen::start shall draw the console only when the command line holds ferrix.fbcon and there is a framebuffer: clear it, and draw what recent keeps of the lines printed before, from the first whole one."
"A boot without ferrix.fbcon leaves the framebuffer as firmware left it; one with it shows the boot's earlier lines from a line's start, and every later kernel line."
"Board::new shall pick the largest glyph scale up to 4 that leaves at least 60 columns, inside the margins and the top inset, and refuse a surface with room for no column or fewer than 2 rows."
"A 1080-pixel-wide surface gets scale 2 and 65 columns; a 640-pixel one, scale 1; a surface 20 pixels high is refused."

"Board::put shall ignore a CR, start a new row at a newline, advance a tab to the next stop of eight, draw a printable byte and draw anything else as the replacement character, wrapping at the last column and from the bottom row to the top, and keep the row after the newest line blank."

"Drawn on a board of 3 rows, a line with a tab, a CR and a byte 0x01 puts its glyphs at the columns the rule gives, the replacement glyph for 0x01, and after a fourth newline the text is on row 1 with row 2 blank."
"screen::stop shall stop the screen console for good and wait a bounded time for a draw in flight to finish, and a byte that finds the board taken shall not be drawn."
"After stop, 0 bytes are drawn; stop called by a processor part way through a draw returns after at most 1,000,000 attempts at the board."

children.name: Ports
children.doc: Which console the kernel writes to, where firmware or the loader says. The ports' drivers are the arch slices'.

children.value: "ramoops_zone shall read the loader's `console=ramoops,<base>,<size>` as a zone only when both numbers are hexadecimal with a 0x prefix, no third field follows, the base is a page's and the size is more than the record's 12-byte header."

"`ramoops,0x9ff00000,0x40000` is read as the zone at 0x9ff00000 of 0x40000 bytes; a base not a page's, a 12-byte zone, a missing size, a third field, a number without 0x and `ttyAMA0` are each refused: 0 of 6 taken (the AArch64 `machine` line)."

"chosen shall take the port a `console=` in the device tree's bootargs names, where the tree has that port with registers; else the port stdout-path names; else the first port the kernel drives that the tree has not turned off."

"Of 4 trees built for the check, `console=pl011` against a stdout-path naming the USART gives the PL011; a `console=ttyS0` falls through to stdout-path's PL011; no stdout-path gives the first port not disabled; a lone STM32 USART gives it: 4 of 4 (the ARMv7-A `machine` line)."

children.name: Superblocks
children.doc: The superblock: the one structure read before anything is known about the volume.

children.value: "Superblock::parse shall answer any bytes with a superblock or an error, and every accessor of a superblock it returns shall answer without a panic."
"Each of 4,096 single-byte patches of a well-formed superblock (the first 1,024 bytes, each set to 0x00, 0x01, 0x7F and 0xFF) parses or is refused, and every accessor of each that parses answers."
"Superblock::parse shall refuse a superblock whose CRC-32C does not match its bytes, with BadChecksum."
"A superblock with one checksummed byte changed is refused with BadChecksum."
"Superblock::parse shall refuse bytes without the btrfs magic, with BadMagic."
"A superblock with its magic changed is refused with BadMagic."
"Superblock::parse shall refuse a buffer shorter than a superblock, with Truncated."
"A superblock cut short is refused with Truncated naming the bytes needed and found."
"Superblock::parse shall refuse a sector, node or leaf size btrfs would not write, with BadSectorSize or BadNodeSize naming it."
"Each combination of sector, node and leaf size the test lists -- nodes smaller than a sector among them -- is refused with the error naming the size."
"Superblock::parse shall refuse a superblock naming a root, a chunk root or a log root no tree can have."
"A root and a chunk root of level 8, a log root of level 255 and each other root the test lists are refused."
"Superblock::parse shall refuse a superblock whose checksum type is not CRC-32C, with UnsupportedChecksum carrying the type."
"A superblock of checksum type 2 is refused with UnsupportedChecksum(2)."
"crc32c shall compute the CRC-32C (Castagnoli) of its input."
"crc32c of each published test vector equals its published value."
"Volume::open shall refuse a volume setting an incompatible feature bit the reader does not know, one spanning more than one device, and one naming a log tree not yet replayed."
"Volume::open of an image with an unknown incompatible bit answers UnsupportedFeature, of one with two devices MultipleDevices, and of one with a log root UnreplayedLog."

"No addition, subtraction, multiplication or shift in ferrix-btrfs or ferrix-btrfs-write shall be able to overflow: each shall be checked, saturating or wrapping by intent, so that a value read from a volume can neither wrap silently in the release kernel, which has no overflow checks, nor panic one built with them."
"clippy's arithmetic_side_effects lint, denied for both crates' product code, reports no site. Not yet enforced: on 2026-10-02 it reports 112, 56 in each crate."

children.name: Nodes
children.doc: Tree nodes, parsed before any field of them is used.

children.value: "Node::parse shall answer any bytes with a node or an error, and every accessor of a node it returns shall answer without a panic."
"Each of 4,096 single-byte patches of a well-formed leaf parses or is refused, and every accessor of each that parses answers."
"Node::parse shall refuse a node that records another address than the one it was read from, with WrongAddress."
"A node parsed at another address than its own is refused with WrongAddress naming both."
"Node::parse shall refuse a node whose CRC-32C does not match its bytes, with BadChecksum."
"A node with one checksummed byte changed is refused with BadChecksum."
"Node::parse shall refuse a node claiming more items than a node of its size holds, with TooManyItems."
"A node whose item count exceeds its capacity is refused with TooManyItems."
"Node::parse shall refuse a leaf with an item whose data lies outside the node or over the item array, with ItemOutOfBounds."
"A leaf with an item running past the node is refused with ItemOutOfBounds naming its slot."
"Node::parse shall refuse a node whose keys are not strictly ascending, with ItemsOutOfOrder."
"A node with two keys out of order is refused with ItemsOutOfOrder naming the slot."
"Node::parse shall refuse a leaf whose item payloads are not packed back to back from the node's end."
"A leaf with a gap or an overlap between payloads is refused."
"Node::parse shall refuse a node whose level exceeds MAX_LEVEL."
"Node::parse shall refuse a buffer shorter than the node it describes, with Truncated."
"A node cut short is refused with Truncated."
"Node::search shall return a present key's slot, and for an absent key the slot it would be inserted at."
"Present keys are found at their slots and absent ones answer the slot they would go in, as the test lists."

children.name: Chunks
children.doc: Chunk items and the logical-to-physical map built from them.

children.value: "ChunkMap::insert shall answer ChunkMapFull, not write past its storage, when the map is full."
"A map one entry short of the chunks inserted answers ChunkMapFull for the last and keeps the others."
"ChunkMap::insert shall refuse a chunk whose range overlaps a different chunk already mapped, with BadChunk."
"A chunk overlapping one already mapped is refused with BadChunk."
"ChunkMap::map shall answer UnsupportedProfile for an address in a chunk of a striped or parity profile, never a guessed physical address."
"An address in a RAID0, RAID10, RAID5 or RAID6 chunk is refused with UnsupportedProfile carrying its type bits."
"ChunkMap::map shall map an address in a SINGLE chunk to its stripe's offset plus the address's offset into the chunk."
"Addresses in a SINGLE chunk map to the physical addresses the test computes."
"ChunkMap::map shall map an address in a DUP or RAID1 chunk to the first stripe, and refuse one in a RAID0 chunk."
"A DUP and a RAID1 chunk map to their first stripe; a RAID0 chunk is refused."
"ChunkItem::parse shall refuse a chunk item of a stripe length, length, type or stripe count btrfs would not write, with BadChunk."
"Each malformed chunk item the test lists is refused with BadChunk."
"ChunkItem::parse shall refuse a chunk item with no stripes."
"A chunk item with num_stripes zero is refused."
"ChunkItem::parse shall refuse a chunk item shorter than its stripe records."
"A chunk item cut inside its stripe records is refused."
"A chunk shall be refused when its sector size differs from the volume's or its start is off the sector grid."
"A chunk of another sector size, and one starting off the grid, are refused."
"The system chunk array shall be refused when it holds a chunk that is not a system chunk."
"A system chunk array holding a data chunk is refused."
"ChunkMap::load_sys_chunk_array shall map every chunk the superblock's system chunk array holds."
"Every chunk of the system chunk array the test builds is mapped after the load."

children.name: Items
children.doc: Item payloads, parsed for their key type.

children.value: "Iterating a directory item shall stop, not read past the item, at an entry whose name runs past the item's end."
"A directory item whose last name runs past its end yields the entries before it and then stops."
"InodeItem::parse shall refuse a payload shorter than an inode item."
"An inode item cut short is refused."
"Iterating a directory item shall refuse an entry btrfs would not write: an empty or over-long name, an unknown type, or data where none belongs."
"Each malformed entry the test lists is refused."
"Iterating an inode reference shall accept names of 1 to 255 bytes and refuse others."
"Names of 1 and 255 bytes are read, and names outside that length are refused."
"ExtentData::parse shall refuse a payload shorter than its form of extent item."
"The truncated extent items the test lists are refused."
"ExtentData::parse_item shall refuse an extent item btrfs would not write: an unknown type, a range outside its extent, or a misaligned offset."
"Each malformed extent the test lists is refused with BadItem."
"Iterating an inode extended reference shall refuse the records Linux refuses."
"Well-formed extended references parse, and each the test lists that Linux refuses is refused."

children.name: Compression
children.doc: The three decoders of compressed extents.

children.value: "zlib::decompress shall answer every stream with an error or the bytes it encodes, within its output buffer."
"Every single-bit flip of real zlib extents decodes to what miniz_oxide decodes or is an error; 0 panics."
"zlib::decompress shall refuse a stream cut before its end."
"Every truncation of a real extent before its trailer is an error."
"zlib::decompress shall refuse a stream that decodes to more than its output buffer holds."
"A stream decoding past a smaller output buffer is an error, and nothing is written past the buffer."
"zlib::decompress shall refuse a back-reference before the start of its output."
"A stream whose first match reaches before the output's start is an error."
"lzo::decompress shall answer every stream with an error or decoded bytes, within its output buffer."
"Every single-bit flip of real LZO extents answers; 0 panics."
"lzo::decompress shall answer every truncated stream without a panic."
"Every truncation of a real LZO extent answers."
"lzo::decompress shall decode no more than its output buffer holds."
"A stream decoded into a smaller output buffer stops at the buffer and writes nothing past it."
"zstd::decompress shall answer every stream with an error or decoded bytes, within its output buffer."
"Every single-bit flip of real zstd frames answers; 0 panics."
"zstd::decompress shall refuse a frame cut short as corrupt."
"Every truncation of a real zstd frame is BadCompressedData."
"zstd::decompress shall refuse a frame whose content is larger than its output buffer."
"A frame decoded into a buffer smaller than its content is BadCompressedData."
"zstd::decompress shall refuse a match before the start of its output."
"A frame whose first match reaches before the output's start is BadCompressedData."

children.name: Walks
children.doc: Searching and walking a tree.

children.value: "Volume::walk shall visit every key of a tree once, in strictly ascending order."
"A walk of each of the four images' fs trees visits every key once, each greater than the one before."
"Volume::walk shall stop at the key its visitor breaks on."
"A walk whose visitor breaks stops at that key."
"Volume::last_at_or_before shall return the last key at or before the one asked, across leaf boundaries."
"For every pair of neighbouring keys of the four images, the later finds itself and a key in the gap finds the earlier."
"predecessor shall return the greatest key below its argument, through every field."
"predecessor steps back through each field of a key as the test lists."

children.name: NodeReads
children.doc: Reading a node from the copy that passes its checks.

children.value: "Volume::read_node shall try each copy of a node in turn and return the first that passes its checks."
"With the first copy of a DUP node damaged, the read returns the node from the second."
"Volume::read_node shall refuse a node none of whose copies passes its checks, with the first copy's error."
"A tree node with a damaged byte, in a SINGLE chunk, is refused and not read as a node."
"Volume::read_node shall refuse a node whose generation differs from what its parent named, with BadTree."
"A root pointer with its generation raised by one is refused with BadTree."
"A failed device read shall be answered as DeviceRead at its physical address, not as damage."
"A device failing the root's read answers DeviceRead at that address."
"A tree whose root names a level above MAX_LEVEL shall be refused with BadTree before anything is read."
"A root of level 8 is refused with BadTree."

children.name: Files
children.doc: Names and file contents, read through a subvolume.

children.value: "Subvolume::lookup shall refuse an entry filed under another name's hash."
"A lookup reaching an entry whose name hashes to another key is refused."
"Subvolume::lookup shall refuse a name that no longer matches its hash."
"A lookup of a name changed on the disk after it was filed is refused."
"check_name shall refuse an empty name, `.`, `..` and a name holding `/` or NUL, and accept other names of up to 255 bytes; a lookup shall refuse the same names."
"Six names -- empty, `.`, `..`, `/`, `a/b` and one with a NUL -- are refused by check_name and by a lookup, and six others, `...` and one of 255 bytes among them, are accepted."
"Subvolume::read_dir shall refuse a listing that holds a name with a slash."
"A listing whose entry's name holds a slash is refused."
"Subvolume::lookup shall answer a name the directory does not hold as a miss, not an error."
"A lookup of an absent name answers None."
"Subvolume::read shall return an uncompressed file's bytes as they were written."
"Every file of the uncompressed image reads back byte for byte."
"Subvolume::read shall return a zlib-compressed file's bytes as they were written."
"Every file of the zlib image reads back byte for byte."
"Subvolume::read shall return an LZO-compressed file's bytes as they were written."
"Every file of the LZO image reads back byte for byte."
"Subvolume::read shall return a zstd-compressed file's bytes as they were written."
"Every file of the zstd image reads back byte for byte."
"Subvolume::read past a file's end shall return nothing, and Subvolume::read_dir shall resume a listing from the cursor it returned."
"A read past the end returns nothing, and a listing resumed from its cursor yields the rest."
"Subvolume::read shall return zeroes for a hole."
"Subvolume::read shall refuse an extent that starts inside the one before it."
"An extent starting inside the one before it is refused."
"ReadBuffers::new shall refuse buffers smaller than the largest extent they must hold."
"Buffers smaller than an extent are refused."

children.name: DataSectors
children.doc: The reader's checksums of file data.

children.value: "A file read shall answer DataChecksum, and no bytes, for a data sector whose CRC-32C differs from the checksum tree's."
"A read of a file with one damaged data sector, in a SINGLE chunk, answers DataChecksum."
"A file read shall read a DUP data sector that fails its checksum from its other copy, and answer an error when both fail."
"With the first copy of a DUP sector damaged the read returns the file's bytes; with both damaged it answers DataChecksum."
"A compressed extent shall be checked against its checksums before it is expanded."
"Damage inside a compressed extent is DataChecksum, not BadCompressedData."
"A file marked nodatasum shall be read without checksums, as Linux reads it."
"A nodatasum file reads back byte for byte."

children.name: Commit
children.doc: The write path's crash safety: copy-on-write and the order of a commit's writes.

children.value: "WriteVolume::commit shall flush directly before writing the primary superblock, make the primary durable before any mirror, and write no node after it."
"In the device's record of a commit a flush directly precedes and directly follows the primary superblock, and no node write comes after it."
"No write a transaction makes before its superblock shall land on a block the last commit's trees reach."
"500 inserts committed, their writes replayed without the superblocks onto the volume as it was, leave a volume that checks clean and holds exactly the last commit's items."

"WriteVolume::open shall refuse with Unsupported a volume of more than one device, of a profile other than SINGLE or DUP, without a valid free-space tree, with non-skinny metadata, without NO_HOLES, with mixed groups, an unknown read-only-compatible feature, a subvolume, quotas or a shared tree block."
"WriteVolume::open of an image with each of these answers Unsupported naming it, and the device has no write."

children.name: Log
children.doc: The log a fsync commits, and its replay at open.

children.value: "An inode's data logged with log_inode and commit_log shall be read back after a crash, the log replayed when the volume opens."
"A file rewritten, logged and never committed, then opened from the crashed device, holds the rewrite."
"A commit shall carry what a log held into the trees and leave the superblock naming no log."
"After a log commit and then a commit, the superblock names no log and the file holds the logged data."
"commit_log shall flush directly before writing the superblock that names the log."
"In the device's record of a log commit a flush directly precedes the superblock."
"A log commit's writes without its superblock shall leave the volume at its last commit."
"The log commit's writes replayed without its superblock leave the file as last committed."
"Replaying a log of an inode logged twice shall leave the later of the two."
"An inode logged with one content and again with another opens holding the second."
"Replaying a logged extent cut in two shall make one extent referred to twice, not two."
"A file whose extent an overwrite cut in two replays with one extent and two references to it, and checks clean."

children.name: Space
children.doc: The write path's allocator and the bookkeeping trees that record what it handed out.

children.value: "A metadata block group whose chunk covers a superblock mirror shall allocate no tree block in the mirror's stripe, and its free-space tree shall still list the stripe free."

"On the blank fixture, whose DUP metadata chunk covers the 64 MiB mirror, edits until past the mirror leave no tree block in its stripe, the volume checks clean, and the free-space tree lists the stripe free."
"A data chunk made over a superblock mirror shall keep the mirror's stripe out of data allocation."
"On a volume grown until a data chunk covers the 64 MiB mirror, every data extent then allocated lies outside the stripe."
"Each commit shall leave every tree block's and data extent's references, each block group's usage and free space, and the superblock's total consistent with the trees."
"After 3,000 random edits with commits between them, the writer's checker finds every count consistent and the reader reads back every item the model holds."
"Deleting every item added to a tree shall shrink it back to a leaf holding what it held before."
"2,000 items inserted, making a tree of three levels, then deleted, leave a tree of level 0 with the items it had, checking clean."
"ExtentRecord::apply shall refuse a reference count taken below zero, or above one for a tree block's single owner."
"Removing a reference never added, and adding one owner twice, are refused."
"RangeSet::insert shall merge a run with the runs it touches."
"Runs inserted touching on either side become one run."
"RangeSet::remove shall split the run a removal falls inside."
"A range removed from inside a run leaves the two runs around it."
"RangeSet::first_fit shall return the first start that is aligned, holds the length and does not cross the boundary."
"Each fit the test lists is aligned and does not cross the boundary."
"RangeSet::first_prefix shall return the longest aligned prefix of at most the length wanted and at least the minimum."
"Each request the test lists takes the prefix the run has."
"RangeSet::add shall union overlapping and touching runs."
"Overlapping and touching runs added become their union."
"RangeSet::extract shall take exactly the bytes two sets share."
"Extracting one set from another takes exactly their intersection and leaves the rest."
"place_stripes shall place every copy of a new chunk in the device's holes, or answer None."
"In one 8 MiB hole two copies of 8 MiB are refused and two of 4 MiB are placed side by side."
"WriteVolume::alloc_data shall answer NoSpace, aborting nothing, when neither a block group nor the device has room for a data extent."
"Data extents taken until the device has no room end in NoSpace with the transaction not aborted."

children.name: Full
children.doc: A volume that runs out, and a transaction that fails.

children.value: "A file write larger than the data room shall be refused with NoSpace before it changes anything, aborting nothing."
"A write one sector past data_room is NoSpace, the transaction is not aborted, and its commit leaves a volume that checks clean."
"A file write of exactly the data room shall succeed and leave no data room."
"A write of exactly data_room succeeds, data_room is then 0, and the commit checks clean."

"An operation the metadata room cannot hold, with the commit's reserve and the global reserve, shall be refused with NoSpace before its first edit, and an operation that frees space may still use the global reserve."
"Creates until the trees are full end in NoSpace with the transaction not aborted, the commit succeeds, 64 unlinks succeed, and a create after their commit succeeds."
"A data write on full trees shall be refused with NoSpace, aborting nothing."
"After the trees are filled, 64 KiB writes end in NoSpace with the transaction not aborted, and the commit checks clean."
"A data write that needs a new metadata chunk shall succeed or be refused with NoSpace, aborting nothing."
"With metadata used until the next edit must make a chunk, a write of the data room succeeds or is NoSpace, the transaction is not aborted, and the commit checks clean."
"Through a mount, a write to a full volume shall be refused with ENOSPC at exactly the room statfs offered, keeping what was written."
"Through ferrix-btrfs-vfs, writes stop with ENOSPC at the byte statfs offered, the file holds every byte written, and after an unlink a 1 MiB file is written and read back after remounting."
"Through a mount, creates on full trees shall be refused with ENOSPC, and the mount shall stay writable."
"Through ferrix-btrfs-vfs, creates end in ENOSPC, another create is ENOSPC too, the sync succeeds and 64 unlinks succeed."

"A failure after an edit changed something shall mark the transaction aborted, and reload_read_only shall replace it with the last commit read from the device and answer ReadOnly to every edit after it."

"Through a mount, a commit whose device write fails answers EIO; the mount then reads the last commit, has no trace of the aborted transaction, answers EROFS to a write, a truncation and a create, and the disk holds the last commit."
"reload_read_only shall leave the volume aborted, and every read answering an error, when the last commit cannot be read."
"Through a mount, with writes and reads failing, the sync answers EIO and every later lookup answers EIO."
"Every heap allocation of the btrfs crates' product code shall be made through a helper that reports a refused allocation as an error, never through one that stops the element."
"tools/common/check/check-fallible-alloc.py finds 0 unmarked allocating calls in ferrix-btrfs and in ferrix-btrfs-write."
"An operation of the write path whose allocation is refused shall answer OutOfMemory, and either leave the transaction as it was or abort it, so that the volume reopens at its last commit."

"With each allocation of a script of eleven file operations and a commit on a populated volume failed once in turn, every failing operation answers OutOfMemory; where the transaction was not aborted, the script resumed from that operation ends with the fs tree an undisturbed run makes; where it was, the volume reopens at the commit before the script with its fs tree; every volume checks clean."
"WriteVolume::open shall answer OutOfMemory when an allocation is refused, having written nothing to the device."

"With each allocation of opening the blank and the populated volume failed in turn, once and from then on, each open succeeds or answers OutOfMemory, and the device then opens at the same generation with the same fs tree and checks clean."
"The reader shall answer a device read that ran out of memory with OutOfMemory, reading no other copy and reporting no damage."
"With each device read of an open, a lookup and a whole-file read failed in turn with OutOfMemory, on a plain, a zstd and a DUP image, the answer is OutOfMemory and no read follows the failed one."
"WriteVolume::read_node shall answer a device read that ran out of memory with OutOfMemory, reading no other copy."
"With the first copy of a DUP fs tree root failing with OutOfMemory, a lookup answers OutOfMemory after that one read, aborts nothing, and succeeds once the device reads again."

"A RangeSet insert, removal or union that has to make a run of its own shall, when that allocation is refused, answer OutOfMemory with the set unchanged; one that edits a run in place shall allocate nothing."
"Six edits that make a run, each with its first allocation failed, answer OutOfMemory and leave the set equal to what it was; three in-place edits under the same failure succeed."
"A commit shall make everything it needs after writing the primary superblock before writing it, so that running out of memory is never reported for a commit that is on the device."

"With each allocation of a script of file operations and a commit on the blank volume failed from then on, in turn, no run whose failure was reported finds the script's commit on the device when the volume is reopened."
"An open whose log replay is refused an allocation shall leave the device so that a later open replays the log."

"With each allocation of opening a volume that holds a committed log failed in turn, the open answers OutOfMemory or succeeds, and the next open of the same device holds the logged file's bytes, commits and checks clean."
"A read of the write path whose allocation is refused shall answer OutOfMemory and abort nothing."
"With each allocation of reading a populated volume's whole fs tree from cold failed in turn, the read answers OutOfMemory, the transaction is not aborted, and the tree then reads whole."
"Every ordered map the write path keeps shall have nodes no larger than the kernel heap's largest size class, so that the kernel's reserve can serve its inserts."
"The node bound of each of the ten map and set types the write path keeps is at most ferrix_heap::LARGEST_CLASS."
